Remove unsupported withdrawal tonnage and arrest detail; the supported shorter description does not cure the unresolved date.

sources.name: WHO authors in Environmental Health Perspectives: The Melamine Incident
Food Policy: China's milk scandal and its institutional roots

original.title: Islamabad Marriott Hotel bombing
original.description: A dump truck carrying about 1,000 kg of explosives detonated at the security gate of the Marriott Hotel in Islamabad on the evening of 20 September 2008, gutting the building and killing 54 people, including the Czech ambassador to Pakistan, three US citizens, and a Danish intelligence agent, while wounding at least 266. The attack, hours after President Asif Ali Zardari's first address to parliament, was one of the worst terrorist attacks in Pakistan's history; no group claimed responsibility.

retained.title: Islamabad Marriott Hotel bombing
retained.description: A suicide truck bombing struck the Marriott Hotel in Islamabad on the evening of September 20, 2008, causing a major fire and killing dozens. A group calling itself Fedayeen Islam later claimed responsibility, but that claim was not authenticated in the contemporaneous Reuters report.

review.note: September 20 evening is established, but the exact victim total is not: the US State Department's annual report says 53, the original says 54, and a 2012 US court opinion cites 56 from BBC reporting. These are not demonstrated to be solely attacker-inclusion differences. The statement that no group claimed responsibility is false: Reuters reported a Fedayeen Islam claim on September 22 while explicitly saying it was unauthenticated. Remove the unsupported explosive weight, nationality breakdown and ranking; preserve the unverified nature of that claim. Toll remains a publication blocker.

sources.name: US State Department: Pakistan human rights report 2008
Reuters via RFE/RL: unauthenticated responsibility claim
US District Court: DiFederico v Marriott memorandum opinion

original.title: Balochistan earthquake
original.description: A magnitude 6.4 earthquake struck the remote Ziarat and Pishin districts of Balochistan Province in southwestern Pakistan on 29 October 2008, flattening mud-brick villages and triggering landslides. The government's final toll was 215 confirmed dead with several hundred injured (official counts rose from 115 to 236 as reports came in), and about 120,000 people were left homeless in freezing mountain conditions. The UN appealed for emergency shelter after an initial government appeal failed to secure funds.

retained.title: Balochistan earthquake
retained.description: A magnitude-6.4 earthquake struck Balochistan on October 28, 2008 UTC, in the early morning of October 29 locally, severely damaging villages in the Ziarat area. IFRC reporting recorded 166 deaths and hundreds of injuries; other published death totals differ.

review.note: The first destructive magnitude-6.4 shock was October 28 at 23:09 UTC, October 29 locally; another large shock occurred October 29 UTC. Propose October 28 for the first shock. IFRC's initial appeal update and later Pakistan plan report 166 deaths, whereas the original calls 215 final and inconsistently says official reports had reached 236. Those alternative totals are not reconciled. IFRC's roughly 122,000 refers to people affected, not all homeless. Remove that conflation and the unsupported failed-appeal story. The ASC event page was indexed but could not be opened; the exact UTC time is also given in the secondary earthquake record.

sources.name: IFRC: Pakistan earthquake appeal update MDRPK00201
Amateur Seismic Centre: October 28, 2008 Balochistan earthquake
Wikipedia: 2008 Ziarat earthquakes, UTC event times

original.title: Gaza War (Operation Cast Lead) begins
original.description: Israel launched Operation Cast Lead on 27 December 2008 with air strikes on Hamas targets in the Gaza Strip, including a missile attack on the Gaza City police headquarters that alone killed about 40 people, followed by a ground invasion on 3 January 2009. Over the 22-day offensive, at least 1,387 Palestinians were killed, including roughly 773 civilians and 320 children, with over 5,000 wounded, according to Palestinian and human-rights organizations; 13 Israelis were also killed. A UN investigation found the offensive used disproportionate force and caused widespread destruction of homes, schools, and hospitals.

retained.title: Gaza War (Operation Cast Lead) begins
retained.description: Israel began Operation Cast Lead with airstrikes in Gaza on December 27, 2008 and launched a ground invasion on January 3, 2009. The offensive continued until January 18. B'Tselem's later accounting recorded 1,391 Palestinian deaths and 13 Israeli deaths across the conflict; official Israeli and earlier published Palestinian totals differed.

review.note: The December 27 start and January 3 ground invasion are supported by the IDF chronology; the toll covers the whole offensive through January 18, not only the opening day. The original 1,400 numerically combines an older B'Tselem count of 1,387 Palestinians with 13 Israelis. B'Tselem subsequently revised its Palestinian count to 1,391 (1,404 combined), while other B'Tselem pages contain older 1,385/1,390 figures; Israel's official total of 1,166 Palestinians also differs in inclusion and classification. Preserve those contradictions: this batch does not certify one exact total or reconcile civilian/child definitions. Remove outdated subtotals, the unverified 40-at-headquarters detail and the compressed UN legal conclusion. Toll and geographic scope remain unresolved for integration.

sources.name: B'Tselem: September 2009 casualty release, with update notice
B'Tselem: Gaza Strip background and updated conflict totals
Israel Defense Forces: Operation Cast Lead chronology

original.title: Gaza War (Operation Cast Lead)
original.description: Israel's military offensive against Hamas in the Gaza Strip ran from December 27, 2008, to a ceasefire on January 18, 2009. Human rights organizations and UN agencies documented approximately 1,340-1,400 Palestinians killed, including around 750-770 civilians and more than 300 children, with over 5,000 wounded. Thirteen Israelis were killed, including 3 civilians. The offensive included heavy air strikes and ground operations and caused extensive destruction of homes, schools, and infrastructure across Gaza.
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
Al Mezan Centre for Human Rights

original.title: Sri Lankan Civil War Final Offensive
original.description: Between January and May 2009, the Sri Lankan military's final offensive against the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) trapped roughly 330,000 civilians in an ever-shrinking 'no fire zone' in the northeast. A UN Secretary-General-appointed panel of experts estimated in 2011 that as many as 40,000 civilians were killed, most by government shelling, with the LTTE also accused of using civilians as human shields. The government's own figures put the toll at about 7,000-9,000. The war ended on May 18, 2009, with the military declaring victory.

retained.title: Sri Lankan Civil War Final Offensive
retained.description: Between January and May 2009, the Sri Lankan military's final offensive against the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) trapped roughly 330,000 civilians in an ever-shrinking 'no fire zone' in the northeast. A UN Secretary-General-appointed panel of experts estimated in 2011 that as many as 40,000 civilians were killed, most by government shelling, with the LTTE also accused of using civilians as human shields. The government's own figures put the toll at about 7,000-9,000. The war ended on May 18, 2009, with the military declaring victory.

review.note: 40,000 is an upper estimate cited by the UN panel, not a confirmed count. AP corroborates tens of thousands and abuses by both sides. Government 7,000-9,000 attribution and the precise 330,000 trapped figure remain unestablished. The military defeat on May 18 and presidential victory declaration on May 19 must not be conflated.

original.title: Cyclone Aila
original.description: Cyclone Aila, a severe cyclonic storm in the Bay of Bengal, made landfall on May 25, 2009, near the Bangladesh-India border, bringing storm surges of up to 6 meters. Final official tallies recorded about 339 deaths across the region, including roughly 190 in Bangladesh and 140 in eastern India's West Bengal state, with hundreds of thousands left homeless and millions affected by flooding and breached embankments.
sources: University of Colorado Natural Hazards Center

retained.title: Cyclone Aila

Final official tallies recorded about 339 deaths across the region, including roughly 190 in Bangladesh and 140 in eastern India's West Bengal state, with hundreds of thousands left homeless and millions affected by flooding and breached embankments.
sources: University of Colorado Natural Hazards Center

review.note: Aila and May 25 landfall corroborated, but 339 as a final official regional count and the 190/140 split were not established. IMD-hosted assessment describes a 3 m surge in western Bangladesh; the claimed 6 m maximum needs a location-specific source. Satkhira is narrower than the regional toll.

original.title: Typhoon Morakot
original.description: Typhoon Morakot, the deadliest typhoon to hit Taiwan in about 50 years, made landfall on August 7-8, 2009, dumping record rainfall of up to 3 meters in the southern mountains. A massive mudslide buried the village of Xiaolin in Kaohsiung County, killing an estimated 400-500 residents. More than 670 people were confirmed dead in Taiwan, with additional deaths in China and the northern Philippines, for a regional total of roughly 700-800 lives lost.
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs

retained.title: Typhoon Morakot

More than 670 people were confirmed dead in Taiwan, with additional deaths in China and the northern Philippines, for a regional total of roughly 700-800 lives lost.

review.note: Taiwan reconstruction record lists 681 dead and 18 missing separately; paper dates the typhoon strike to August 7. Existing 700 is an untraceable rounded regional total. Need landfall time/UTC, final cross-country sum and Xiaolin toll before replacing date or numeric field.

original.title: Baghdad Ministry Bombings
original.description: On August 19, 2009, coordinated truck bombings hit the Iraqi Foreign Ministry and Finance Ministry in Baghdad, along with other explosions, killing at least 95 people and wounding about 563 according to Iraqi Interior Ministry officials. The attacks, blamed on al-Qaeda-linked militants and Baathist elements, were the bloodiest day in Baghdad since February 2008 and the worst since US troops withdrew from Iraqi cities at the end of June 2009.

retained.title: Baghdad Ministry Bombings
retained.description: On August 19, 2009, coordinated truck bombings hit the Iraqi Foreign Ministry and Finance Ministry in Baghdad, along with other explosions, killing at least 95 people and wounding about 563 according to Iraqi Interior Ministry officials. The attacks, blamed on al-Qaeda-linked militants and Baathist elements, were the bloodiest day in Baghdad since February 2008 and the worst since US troops withdrew from Iraqi cities at the end of June 2009.

review.note: Reuters photograph corroborates ministry attack and August 19 date. The searches did not independently establish 95/563, the comparative superlatives or final perpetrator attribution; BBC access was blocked. Keep unverified until a casualty report is checked. Only one checked source is recorded; the two-source publication minimum is not met.

original.title: Kunduz Fuel Tanker Airstrike
original.description: On September 4, 2009, NATO aircraft, at the request of German forces, bombed two fuel tankers hijacked by Taliban insurgents near Kunduz City. Villagers had gathered around the stranded tankers to siphon fuel. Death toll estimates range from 56 to 179, with a German parliamentary investigation concluding up to 142 people died, including more than 100 civilians. The strike sparked a major political crisis in Germany and led to compensation payments to victims' families.

retained.title: Kunduz Fuel Tanker Airstrike

review.note: Bundestag says the exact number remains unknown and cites reports up to 142; it does not establish over 100 civilians as the parliamentary conclusion. Numeric 100 is unsupported precision. Also verify local overnight strike against UTC before retaining September 4. Do not replace it with a different estimate as a confirmed count.

original.title: Typhoon Ketsana (Ondoy)
original.description: Tropical storm Ketsana (Ondoy) struck the Philippines on September 26, 2009, bringing the heaviest rainfall to Metro Manila in more than four decades — about a month's rain in under 12 hours — and causing catastrophic flash flooding. The consolidated regional death toll reached roughly 900, including 671 in the Philippines, 179 in Vietnam, and dozens more in Cambodia and Laos. Hundreds of thousands were displaced across Southeast Asia.
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs

retained.title: Typhoon Ketsana (Ondoy)

The consolidated regional death toll reached roughly 900, including 671 in the Philippines, 179 in Vietnam, and dozens more in Cambodia and Laos. Hundreds of thousands were displaced across Southeast Asia.
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs

review.note: JICA cites 464 Philippine deaths; GMA's 277 is explicitly an October 1 preliminary count. Neither supports 671 Philippine deaths or the 921 regional field. Need comparable final country reports; do not add preliminary and final or Ondoy/Pepeng totals.

original.title: West Sumatra (Padang) Earthquake
original.description: A magnitude 7.6 earthquake struck off the coast of West Sumatra on September 30, 2009, about 45 km northwest of Padang. The Indonesian government confirmed 1,115 deaths, with more than 1,200 seriously injured and about 450,000 people displaced. Widespread collapse of poorly reinforced buildings in Padang and Padang Pariaman district caused most casualties. USGS called it the deadliest earthquake of 2009.

The Indonesian government confirmed 1,115 deaths, with more than 1,200 seriously injured and about 450,000 people displaced. review.note: Date, Padang/Pariaman area and magnitude corroborated by assessment material; retrieved assessment gives over 1,117, not 1,115. Exact final toll, displacement and strongest mortality ranking need reconciliation with BNPB/USGS, rather than selecting a convenient near-match.

original.title: Typhoon Parma (Pepeng)
original.description: Typhoon Parma (Pepeng) made landfall in northern Luzon on October 3, 2009, and lingered over the island for a week, making landfall three times and causing torrential rains. Massive landslides in Benguet province and the Cordillera Administrative Region killed 465 people in the Philippines, with total regional deaths near 500, including in Vietnam and China. Landslide-buried villages in La Trinidad and Baguio City accounted for the heaviest losses.
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs

Regional 500, non-Philippine deaths and the claim that landslides alone caused all 465 require corroboration. Secondary lead is not sufficient to verify this record. Only one checked source is recorded; the two-source publication minimum is not met.

original.title: Peshawar Meena Bazaar Bombing
original.description: On October 28, 2009, a car bomb exploded in the Meena Bazaar, a women's market in Peshawar, killing approximately 110-120 people — about 70 of them women and children — and injuring more than 200. The blast, among the deadliest attacks in Peshawar's history, destroyed several buildings and trapped many victims in rubble. Pakistani Taliban-linked militants were suspected. The bombing came amid a surge of militant attacks across Pakistan's northwest.

review.note: Dawn's October 30 report gives 117; later retrospective says 137. The existing 112 and demographic split require reconciliation, not certification.

original.title: Nevsky Express Bombing
original.description: On the night of November 27, 2009, a bomb equivalent to roughly 7 kg of TNT derailed the Nevsky Express train traveling from Moscow to St. Petersburg near Bologoye, killing 28 people and injuring about 90. Russian authorities declared the derailment a terrorist attack, blaming militants from the North Caucasus. It was the second bombing on the line, following an explosion in August 2007 that injured dozens.

original.title: Chile earthquake and tsunami
original.description: A magnitude 8.8 earthquake, one of the strongest ever recorded, struck off the coast of central Chile on February 27, 2010, generating a tsunami with waves up to 24 meters that destroyed coastal towns such as Dichato and Constitución. Authorities confirmed 525 deaths and 25 missing, about 800,000 people displaced, and roughly 370,000 homes damaged. The quake triggered over 1,000 landslides and a nationwide blackout affecting 93 percent of the population; the death toll was comparatively low due to Chile's stringent building codes adopted after the 1960 Valdivia earthquake.

Existing 525/25 may be a different official snapshot; needs dated Chilean authority reconciliation. 24 m waves, landslide count, displacement and building-code causal comparison were not all established.

original.title: Lahore Ahmadiyya mosque attacks
original.description: Gunmen from the Punjabi Taliban wing of Tehrik-e-Taliban Pakistan attacked two Ahmadiyya mosques in Lahore during Friday prayers on May 28, 2010, using automatic weapons, grenades, and suicide vests, and holding worshippers hostage for several hours. Human Rights Watch documented 94 people killed, 27 at the Baitul Nur mosque in Model Town and 67 at the Darul Zikr mosque in Garhi Shahu, with more than 100 wounded. The attacks were the deadliest assault on the Ahmadiyya religious minority in Pakistan's history.

The community's June 12 primary clarification explicitly revised its own earlier 94 to 86, with some injured still hospitalized; the tertiary overview now gives 87. These competing and evolving totals are not reconciled as a final victim count. The original 94 cannot be certified merely by citing the earlier HRW report. Hostage duration and historical ranking also remain unsupported; the archived clarification opened successfully, while its original URL returned 404.

original.title: Osh ethnic violence in southern Kyrgyzstan
original.description: Four days of inter-ethnic violence between Kyrgyz and Uzbek communities erupted in Osh on June 10, 2010 and spread to Jalal-Abad, following the ouster of President Kurmanbek Bakiyev in April and a period of political instability. The Kyrgyz health ministry reported an official toll of about 312 dead and over 2,300 injured, while the International Crisis Group estimated up to 470 killed; interim leader Roza Otunbayeva said the true figure was likely around 2,000 because many victims were buried quickly per local tradition. Hundreds of thousands of ethnic Uzbeks fled across the border into Uzbekistan, and the U.N. reported whole districts of Osh burned to the ground.

Exact source for 312/2,000 and cross-border versus total displacement needed; do not call these interchangeable final counts.

original.title: Russian heatwave and wildfires
original.description: A record-breaking heatwave in July and August 2010, the hottest in eastern Europe in 500 years, combined with massive wildfires and dense smog across western Russia, causing an estimated 55,000 excess deaths nationwide, according to the Center for Research on the Epidemiology of Disasters and peer-reviewed studies. In Moscow alone, an estimated 10,900 to 11,300 excess deaths occurred during the 44-day heat wave and accompanying smog episode, largely from cardiovascular and respiratory failure. The fires destroyed about one-third of Russia's grain harvest and caused roughly $15 billion in economic losses.
sources: Center for Research on the Epidemiology of Disasters (CRED)

original.title: Kampala World Cup bombings
original.description: Three suicide bombs exploded in Kampala on July 11, 2010, while crowds watched the FIFA World Cup final, killing 74 people and injuring over 70. Two devices were detonated at the Kyadondo Rugby Club and one at the Ethiopian Village restaurant. The Somali militant group Al-Shabaab claimed responsibility, stating the attacks were retaliation for Uganda's participation in the African Union peacekeeping mission in Somalia (AMISOM), marking the first major Al-Shabaab attack outside Somalia.

retained.title: Kampala World Cup bombings
retained.description: Three suicide bombs exploded in Kampala on July 11, 2010, while crowds watched the FIFA World Cup final, killing 74 people and injuring over 70. Two devices were detonated at the Kyadondo Rugby Club and one at the Ethiopian Village restaurant. The Somali militant group Al-Shabaab claimed responsibility, stating the attacks were retaliation for Uganda's participation in the African Union peacekeeping mission in Somalia (AMISOM), marking the first major Al-Shabaab attack outside Somalia.

review.note: July 11 Kampala venues corroborated. Reports use both 74 and 76 and differ in preliminary reporting; final victim/attacker scope not resolved. Three devices must not automatically be described as three suicide bombers.

original.title: Pakistan floods
original.description: Unprecedented monsoon rains in late July and August 2010 caused the Indus River and its tributaries to burst their banks, flooding nearly one-fifth of Pakistan's land area across 78 of its 121 districts. Official figures recorded 1,985 deaths and 2,946 injuries, while more than 20 million people were affected, making it one of the largest humanitarian disasters in modern history. The floods destroyed roughly 1.7 million homes, submerged vast agricultural areas, and forced the U.N. to launch a $2 billion relief appeal for what it called the worst flood disaster in Pakistan's history.

original.title: Zhouqu mudslide
original.description: A massive debris flow triggered by heavy rain swept through the mountain county town of Zhouqu in Gansu Province, China, on the night of August 7, 2010, burying about 2.4 square kilometers of the town under mud and rock and damming the Bailong River. Final official loss statistics recorded 1,557 confirmed dead and 284 missing, a combined toll of 1,765, with more than 2,300 injured or sick. It was described by Chinese authorities as the most severe debris-flow disaster since the founding of the People's Republic, with surges reported up to five storeys high.

retained.title: Zhouqu mudslide
retained.description: Heavy rain triggered devastating debris flows in Zhouqu, Gansu, around midnight on August 7-8, 2010 local time (August 7 UTC). Mud and rock swept through the town and blocked the Bailong River. NASA's retrospective, citing landslide research, reports a toll of 1,765; this is not a separately reconciled count of confirmed dead and missing.

review.note: 1,557 + 284 equals 1,841, not 1,765. NASA and research report 1,765; do not retain the inconsistent confirmed/missing breakdown. Around midnight August 7-8 China time is August 7 UTC. The proposed 1,765 remains unreconciled with the competing confirmed-dead/missing breakdown; shortening the prose does not resolve that numeric field. Withhold pending a consistent casualty definition.

original.title: San Fernando migrant massacre
original.description: Mexican marines discovered the bodies of 72 Central and South American migrants, 58 men and 14 women, bound, blindfolded, and shot dead inside a grain barn on a ranch near San Fernando, Tamaulipas, on August 24, 2010. The sole survivor, an Ecuadorean who escaped by feigning death, told investigators that members of the Los Zetas drug cartel killed the migrants after they refused to be forcibly recruited to work for the gang. The massacre was the largest single mass killing of the Mexican drug war at the time and drew international condemnation, with U.N. human rights chief Navi Pillay demanding an end to impunity.

original.title: Mentawai Islands earthquake and tsunami
original.description: A magnitude 7.7-7.8 earthquake struck beneath the Indian Ocean off the Mentawai Islands, west of Sumatra, Indonesia, on October 25, 2010, generating tsunami waves up to 3 meters that devastated low-lying coastal villages. The Indonesian disaster management agency and IFRC recorded 452 people dead and 76 missing, with nearly 15,000 displaced. The disaster struck the same week as the Mount Merapi eruption, and both events combined killed over 700 people, with many of the tsunami victims never recovered from the sea.

original.title: Mount Merapi eruption
original.description: Mount Merapi in central Java began a series of violent eruptions on October 26, 2010, with major eruptions continuing through November 5, including a powerful blast that killed its spiritual guardian Mbah Maridjan and overwhelmed emergency shelters. The final toll recorded 273 deaths, 176 from pyroclastic flows on the spot and 97 from related causes after hospitalization, with 577 people injured and up to 300,000 displaced across Central Java and Yogyakarta. It was the volcano's most powerful eruption in over a century, its eruptive activity peaking in early November.

original.title: Our Lady of Salvation church siege
original.description: Gunmen from the Islamic State of Iraq stormed Our Lady of Salvation, a Syriac Catholic church in Baghdad, during Sunday Mass on October 31, 2010, taking more than 100 worshippers hostage before Iraqi security forces stormed the building. The siege killed 58 people, including 44 worshippers, two priests, seven security personnel, and five attackers, and wounded more than 70. It was the deadliest attack on Iraq's Christian community since the 2003 invasion and prompted an exodus of Iraqi Christians, with many families fleeing the country.

original.title: Libyan civil war and NATO intervention
original.description: Anti-government protests erupted in Benghazi on February 15, 2011, and escalated into a nationwide armed rebellion against the rule of Muammar Gaddafi. A UN-mandated NATO bombing campaign began in March, and fighting continued until the fall of Tripoli in August and Gaddafi's capture and killing on October 20, 2011. Estimates of the conflict's death toll range from about 20,000 to 30,000; a 2013 statistical study published by The New York Times estimated approximately 25,000 killed during the eight-month conflict, including thousands of civilians.

original.title: Tohoku earthquake, tsunami and Fukushima disaster
original.description: A magnitude 9.0 earthquake struck off the Pacific coast of Japan on March 11, 2011, generating a massive tsunami that inundated the northeastern coastline. Waves up to 40 metres high destroyed entire towns in Iwate, Miyagi and Fukushima prefectures, and the tsunami caused a nuclear meltdown at the Fukushima Daiichi power plant. Japan's National Police Agency final figures record 19,759 deaths and 2,553 missing, with most victims drowned by the tsunami; the majority of the deceased were over 60 years old.

original.title: Syrian uprising and government crackdown
original.description: Pro-democracy protests inspired by the Arab Spring began in the city of Daraa in mid-March 2011 and spread across Syria, where they were met with a violent government crackdown involving live fire, tanks, mass arrests and torture. The unrest progressively militarized into an armed insurgency as army defectors formed the Free Syrian Army in July. By December 13, 2011, UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Navi Pillay reported that more than 5,000 people, including over 300 children, had been killed in the uprising.

review.note: UN figures are a dated cumulative estimate, not March 15 deaths. Pillay briefing was Monday December 12, rather than the December 13 publication date. Exact onset in Daraa and July FSA chronology need primary corroboration.

original.title: 2011 Super Outbreak tornadoes
original.description: Between April 25 and 28, 2011, a record outbreak of 360 tornadoes struck 21 US states from Texas to New York, with 216 tornadoes touching down on April 27 alone. The outbreak killed 324 people across six states, including 238 in Alabama, and injured more than 3,100; four tornadoes were rated EF5. The deadliest tornado, the Hackleburg-Phil Campbell EF5 in Alabama and Tennessee, killed 72 people. It was the deadliest US tornado outbreak since 1936, with damages exceeding US$10 billion.

Only one checked source is recorded; the two-source publication minimum is not met.

original.title: Mumbai triple bombings
original.description: On July 13, 2011, three improvised explosive devices hidden on a parked motorcycle, in a tiffin box and on an electric pole exploded within 11 minutes at crowded commercial locations in Mumbai: Zaveri Bazaar, Opera House and Dadar. The blasts killed 26 people and injured more than 130 during evening rush hour. No group claimed responsibility initially; investigations linked the attack to the Indian Mujahideen network, and authorities later named co-founder Yasin Bhatkal as the alleged mastermind.

original.title: 2011 Thailand floods
original.description: Torrential monsoon rains from late July 2011 triggered the worst flooding in Thailand in more than half a century, affecting 65 of the country's 77 provinces and about 13.6 million people over more than five months. Official figures recorded 815 deaths and three missing. Floodwaters inundated Bangkok's outskirts and submerged large parts of the central plains, destroying millions of acres of crops and crippling the country's industrial estates, including hard-disk drive and automobile factories, with total economic damages estimated at around US$45 billion.
sources: Thai Department of Disaster Prevention and Mitigation

original.title: 2011 Pakistan monsoon floods
original.description: Heavy monsoon rains from mid-August to mid-September 2011 caused severe flooding across southern Pakistan, with the province of Sindh the hardest hit, followed by Balochistan. The official damage assessment recorded 520 deaths (497 in Sindh and 23 in Balochistan), about 9.6 million people affected, and more than 1.5 million homes damaged. The floods destroyed over a million acres of crops and livestock, compounding the effects of the record 2010 floods, and forced roughly 744,000 people to be displaced.

original.title: Sikkim earthquake
original.description: A magnitude 6.9 earthquake struck on September 18, 2011 near the Nepal-Sikkim border in northeastern India, with the epicentre in the Kanchenjunga Conservation Area. At least 111 people were killed, including 97 in India (mostly in Sikkim), 7 in China's Tibet region, 6 in Nepal and 1 in Bhutan, and hundreds were injured. The quake, felt across northern India, Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh and Tibet, triggered landslides and rockfalls that cut off remote areas and damaged roughly 43,000 houses in Sikkim.

original.title: Van earthquake
original.description: A magnitude 7.1 earthquake struck eastern Turkey near the city of Van on October 23, 2011, collapsing poorly constructed masonry and adobe buildings, particularly in the town of Ercis. It killed 604 people, injured about 4,152, and left roughly 60,000 people homeless, with 11,232 buildings damaged. A magnitude 5.7 aftershock on November 9 killed about 40 additional people, bringing the earthquake sequence's combined toll to approximately 644.
sources: AFAD (Disaster and Emergency Management Presidency of Turkey)

original.title: Typhoon Washi (Sendong) flash floods
original.location: Cagayan de Oro and Iligan, Philippines
original.description: Tropical Storm Washi (locally named Sendong) made landfall on Mindanao on the night of December 16-17, 2011, dumping up to 20 cm of rain in 24 hours and triggering flash floods that swept away thousands of sleeping residents in the riverside cities of Cagayan de Oro and Iligan. The Philippines' NDRRMC final count recorded 1,268 fatalities, 181 missing and 6,071 injured, with nearly 700,000 people affected and more than 11,000 homes destroyed. It was the deadliest tropical cyclone to hit Mindanao in recorded history.

original.title: Afghanistan conflict — 2012
original.description: UNAMA documented 2,769 civilian deaths and 4,821 injuries in Afghanistan during 2012, making it the first year of decline since UN casualty tracking began, though the toll remained among the highest of the war; several thousand Afghan security forces, international troops (about 400 coalition deaths) and insurgents were also killed. 2012 saw a record spike in insider 'green-on-blue' attacks on coalition personnel.

original.title: Iraq insurgency attacks — 2012

retained.title: Iraq civilian deaths in 2012 (annual total)

Retain the original identity in quarantine and withhold from the dated public event dataset pending an appropriate period representation. The supported title/toll/prose corrections do not solve the date blocker.

original.title: Somalia famine — 2011-2012 crisis

original.title: Syrian civil war — 2012 escalation
original.description: The Syrian civil war escalated dramatically in 2012, from protests to full-scale urban warfare including the Battle of Aleppo from July.
