retained.description: From July to October 2012, the worst flooding in Nigeria in four decades submerged large areas of the country, peaking in October. The National Emergency Management Agency reported 363 deaths and over 2.1 million people displaced, with 30 of Nigeria's 36 states affected; Kogi and Benue were the hardest hit, and more than 150,000 hectares of farmland were destroyed.

review.note: 363 and more than 2.1 million displaced supported for July-October; October 1 is not a established unique event date. State count, hardest-hit ranking and 150,000 hectares require assessment-level corroboration. Record overlaps a multi-month season.

original.title: Typhoon Bopha (Pablo)
original.description: Typhoon Bopha, the strongest storm ever recorded to strike the Philippines at that time of year, made landfall on Mindanao late on 3 December / early 4 December 2012 as a Category 5-equivalent super typhoon. The NDRRMC's final toll was 1,901 dead, with widespread flash floods and landslides in Davao Oriental and Compostela Valley, where mudslides buried villages, including in New Bataan.

retained.title: Typhoon Bopha (Pablo)
retained.description: Typhoon Bopha, the strongest storm ever recorded to strike the Philippines at that time of year, made landfall on Mindanao late on 3 December / early 4 December 2012 as a Category 5-equivalent super typhoon. The NDRRMC's final toll was 1,901 dead, with widespread flash floods and landslides in Davao Oriental and Compostela Valley, where mudslides buried villages, including in New Bataan.

review.note: NASA gives 04:45 December 4 local, i.e. December 3 UTC, and strongest recorded in Mindanao, not strongest nationwide for the season. 1,901 combines commonly reported 1,067 dead and 834 missing rather than 1,901 confirmed dead. ADRC full-page open failed (502); obtain final NDRRMC table before replacing toll.

original.title: Kiss nightclub fire
original.description: On January 27, 2013, pyrotechnics set off by the performing band ignited flammable acoustic foam on the ceiling of the Kiss nightclub in Santa Maria, Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil. The resulting fire, dense smoke, and stampede killed 242 people, mostly university students, and injured at least 630 others; the venue's single functioning exit and the absence of adequate fire safety systems contributed to the deaths, making it the second-deadliest fire in Brazilian history.

retained.title: Kiss nightclub fire
retained.description: A fire at the Kiss nightclub in Santa Maria, Brazil, began early on January 27, 2013, after a band's pyrotechnics ignited ceiling foam. It killed 242 people and injured at least 636; toxic smoke and evacuation failures contributed to the disaster.

review.note: The commission records 242 deaths and at least 636 injured, with a 02:30 local start on January 27 (same UTC date). Replace unsupported stampede causation and historical ranking with documented facts. Only one checked source is recorded; the two-source publication minimum is not met.

original.title: Quetta Hazara market bombing
original.description: On February 16, 2013, a suicide bomber detonated an explosives-laden vehicle at a vegetable market in Hazara Town, Quetta, Pakistan, in an attack targeting the Shia Hazara community. At least 84 people were killed and more than 170 were wounded; the Sunni militant group Lashkar-e-Jhangvi claimed responsibility, and the bombing was the latest in a series of attacks that year against Hazaras in Balochistan.

retained.title: Quetta Hazara market bombing
retained.description: A remote-controlled bomb struck a market in Hazara Town, Quetta, in February 2013, targeting the Shia Hazara community. Lashkar-e-Jhangvi claimed responsibility. Reports placed the death toll at at least 84, with later and contemporary accounts differing on the total.

review.note: Remote detonation contradicts the suicide-bomber claim. Contemporary reporting dates the attack February 16; HRW's retrospective says February 17 and at least 84 deaths, while SRW reports 89. Final toll needs reconciliation; do not silently replace it with an unattributed exact number.

sources.name: Human Rights Watch, Hazara killings report

original.title: Uttarakhand floods and landslides
original.description: In mid-June 2013, exceptionally heavy monsoon rains caused flash floods, cloudbursts, and landslides across the Himalayan state of Uttarakhand, India, with the worst devastation around Kedarnath on June 16-17. More than 5,700 people were presumed dead in the state (over 6,000 including surrounding regions), and tens of thousands of pilgrims and tourists were stranded in the Kedarnath valley before rescue operations ended.

retained.title: Uttarakhand floods and landslides
retained.description: Heavy rain, flooding and landslides devastated Uttarakhand on June 16-17, 2013, particularly around Kedarnath. Thousands died or were reported missing and presumed dead, and large-scale rescue operations evacuated stranded residents and visitors. Official reports differ on the death and missing totals.

review.note: Government sources conflict materially: year-end MHA reports 580 dead plus over 5,526 missing, while NIDM lists 169 dead plus 4,021 presumed dead. Neither establishes 5,700 as an exact final fatality count or the surrounding-region 6,000 claim. June 16 is a period anchor, not a verified instantaneous UTC onset.

sources.name: India Ministry of Home Affairs, 2013 review

original.title: Lac-Mégantic rail disaster
original.description: On July 6, 2013, an unattended 73-car freight train carrying crude oil rolled down a slope and derailed in downtown Lac-Mégantic, Quebec, Canada, exploding into fires that destroyed much of the town center and killed 47 people. Investigators found the train had been left with insufficiently secured brakes; the disaster became the deadliest rail accident in Canadian history.

retained.title: Lac-Mégantic rail disaster
retained.description: An unattended freight train carrying crude oil rolled downhill and derailed in Lac-Megantic, Quebec, at about 05:15 UTC on July 6, 2013. Spilled oil ignited, killing 47 people and destroying much of the town centre. Investigators found that the train had not been adequately secured.

review.note: Investigation gives July 6 about 01:15 EDT (05:15 UTC), 47 deaths, 72 loaded tank cars plus other rolling stock. Remove misleading 73-car shorthand and unsupported all-time Canadian ranking. Only one checked source is recorded; the two-source publication minimum is not met.

sources.name: Transportation Safety Board of Canada, investigation

original.title: Rabaa massacre
original.description: On August 14, 2013, Egyptian security forces violently dispersed sit-in camps of supporters of deposed President Mohamed Morsi at Rabaa al-Adawiya and al-Nahda squares in Cairo. At least 817 people and more than 1,000 by some counts were killed (Human Rights Watch documented 904-1,000+, while the government reported 638), including four journalists; HRW called it one of the largest single-day killings of demonstrators in recent history.

retained.title: Rabaa massacre
retained.description: Egyptian security forces dispersed the Rabaa al-Adawiya sit-in in Cairo on August 14, 2013. Human Rights Watch documented at least 817 people killed there and judged the actual toll likely above 1,000. These figures concern Rabaa, not the separate al-Nahda dispersal or all deaths across Egypt that day.

review.note: 817 is HRW's documented Rabaa minimum; more than 1,000 is its likely total, not an exact count. Original mixes Rabaa, Nahda and broader official figures. Proposed text separates scope, but the schema's exact lives_lost=1000 remains an estimate needing an explicit editorial counting policy. Only one checked source is recorded; the two-source publication minimum is not met.

original.title: Ghouta chemical weapons attack
original.description: On August 21, 2013, rockets carrying the nerve agent sarin struck opposition-held suburbs of Damascus in the Ghouta region of Syria, killing an estimated 1,400 people (estimates range from 281 to 1,729, with the U.S. government assessing about 1,429). United Nations investigators confirmed the use of sarin, and the attack, attributed to Syrian government forces, was the deadliest chemical weapons use since the Iran-Iraq War and led to an international disarmament agreement.

retained.title: Ghouta chemical weapons attack
retained.description: Sarin attacks struck opposition-held areas of Ghouta near Damascus in the early hours of August 21, 2013, local time. UN investigators confirmed chemical-weapons use. Human Rights Watch's analysis attributed the attacks to Syrian government forces. Death estimates vary and should not be presented as a confirmed count.

review.note: UN confirmed chemical-weapons use but was not mandated to assign responsibility. HRW attributes the attacks to government forces. Reported early-morning local attacks may begin August 20 UTC; exact onset must be extracted before changing the date. Fatality estimates vary substantially, so 1,400 is not a confirmed exact toll.

original.title: Zamboanga City siege
original.description: From September 9 to 28, 2013, members of a faction of the Moro National Liberation Front (MNLF) seized coastal districts of Zamboanga City in the Philippines, holding dozens of residents hostage in a three-week standoff that ended in military operations. More than 200 people were killed, mostly MNLF fighters along with 20 soldiers, 5 policemen, and 13 civilians, and over 119,000 residents were displaced.

retained.title: Zamboanga City siege
retained.description: Fighting between government forces and an MNLF faction began in Zamboanga City early on September 9, 2013, local time, or September 8 UTC. The city government's commemoration records 38 civilian and security-force deaths, excluding rebel fatalities, during the siege.

review.note: 04:30 September 9 local is September 8 UTC. City government confirms 38 non-rebel deaths (20 soldiers, five police, 13 civilians), not the overall 200 figure. Rebel toll, total displacement and endpoint differ across accounts; these remain unverified.

original.title: Benisheik massacre
original.description: On September 18, 2013, Boko Haram militants attacked Benisheik in Borno State, northeastern Nigeria, shooting and setting fire to vehicles along the highway and raiding the town, killing about 161 people, including travelers, police officers, and soldiers (some reports cited at least 143). It was among the deadliest single attacks by the insurgency in 2013, and the group claimed responsibility.

retained.title: Benisheik massacre
retained.description: Suspected Boko Haram militants attacked Benisheik and nearby travellers in Borno State on Tuesday night, September 17, 2013. UPI's September 20 report, citing Nigerian officials and Daily Trust, put the reported death toll at at least 161 after additional bodies were found.

review.note: Contemporaneous UPI and the Eagle Online place the attack on Tuesday September 17; the latter specifies 6-7 p.m., the same UTC date. The tertiary overview instead dates it September 18 and gives 159, while UPI's later body-recovery report estimates at least 161. The date correction is supported, but final victim total and scope are not reconciled. Withhold the partially corrected record.

original.title: Peshawar church bombing
original.description: On September 22, 2013, two suicide bombers attacked All Saints Church in Peshawar, Pakistan, during Sunday services, killing at least 85 people and injuring more than 200 in the deadliest attack on Christians in Pakistan's history. A Taliban-linked group claimed responsibility; the official toll was later revised upward to as many as 127 in some tallies.

retained.title: Peshawar church bombing
retained.description: Two suicide bombers attacked worshippers at All Saints Church in Peshawar on September 22, 2013. Reported death totals differed: the bishop of Peshawar reported 127 by September 30, above figures circulating in official and international reporting. A reconciled final count is not established by these sources.

review.note: Bishop's September 30 account gives 127 dead and 170 injured; Dawn reports competing 83/123 totals. These are competing sources, not a demonstrated official upward revision. Exact final toll remains unresolved.

sources.name: Titus Presler, account from bishop of Peshawar
Dawn, competing official and community tolls

original.title: Balochistan earthquake
original.description: On September 24, 2013, a magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck Awaran District in Balochistan, Pakistan, killing at least 825 people (some tallies cite 840) and injuring about 600, with thousands of mud-brick homes destroyed in the remote region. The quake also thrust up a new island off the coast near Gwadar and was the deadliest earthquake in Pakistan since 2005.

retained.title: Balochistan earthquake
retained.description: A magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck Balochistan, Pakistan, at 11:29 UTC on September 24, 2013, causing extensive destruction around Awaran. Published fatality figures differ, and totals must distinguish the mainshock, subsequent earthquakes and geographic scope.

review.note: USGS confirms magnitude 7.7 and September 24 at 11:29 UTC. The 825/840 total has not been reconciled with lower official district counts or the September 28 aftershock. NDMA PDF opened, but casualty search failed; do not certify its unread table.

original.title: Outbreak of the South Sudanese Civil War
original.description: On December 15, 2013, fighting broke out in Juba, South Sudan, between forces loyal to President Salva Kiir and supporters of former Vice President Riek Machar following an alleged coup attempt, igniting a civil war. At least 1,000 people were killed in the initial outbreak by late December 2013, including civilians massacred along ethnic lines, and tens of thousands were displaced; the conflict subsequently spread nationwide.

retained.title: Outbreak of the South Sudanese Civil War
retained.description: Fighting began between military factions in Juba on December 15, 2013, and spread into South Sudan's civil war. By December 26, UNMISS estimated about 1,000 deaths in Juba, a preliminary count rather than the eventual nationwide war toll.

review.note: December 15 onset is established. 1,000 was a preliminary estimate, with Amnesty specifying UNMISS's Juba estimate by December 26. Original wording risks treating this as exact national deaths or onset-day deaths. Precise onset UTC time not established.

original.title: Kunming Railway Station Attack
original.description: On 1 March 2014, eight knife-wielding attackers stormed the Kunming Railway Station in Yunnan province, China, stabbing passengers in a coordinated assault. Thirty-one people were killed and more than 140 injured before police shot four of the attackers dead. Chinese authorities attributed the attack to Uyghur separatists from Xinjiang.

retained.title: Kunming Railway Station Attack
retained.description: Five knife-wielding attackers assaulted passengers at Kunming Railway Station on March 1, 2014, killing 31 people and injuring 141, according to the court account. Four attackers were killed by police. Three other members of the group had been arrested before the assault.

review.note: Court account distinguishes eight members of the group from five people who actually attacked the station; three had been arrested earlier. 21:12 local March 1 is 13:12 UTC. Keep 31 victim deaths excluding four attackers. Only one checked source is recorded; the two-source publication minimum is not met.

original.title: Nyanya Bus Station Bombing
original.description: On 14 April 2014, a bomb exploded at the Nyanya bus station on the outskirts of Abuja, Nigeria, during the morning rush hour. Around 75 people were killed and more than 100 injured. Boko Haram claimed responsibility for the attack, which occurred on the same day the group abducted more than 270 schoolgirls in Chibok.

retained.title: Nyanya Bus Station Bombing
retained.description: A bomb exploded at Nyanya bus station outside Abuja during the morning rush on April 14, 2014. Later reporting put the toll at at least 75 dead and 141 injured. Boko Haram claimed responsibility.

review.note: Initial official 71 became at least 75 in later reporting; neither should be called an exact final tally. Morning Nigerian event retains April 14 UTC. Concise replacement removes unrelated kidnapping detail. The later reported minimum does not settle the final tally; the correction is partial and not publication-ready.

original.title: Balkan Floods
original.description: Record rainfall in mid-May 2014 triggered the worst floods in the Balkans in more than a century, inundating Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and parts of Croatia. At least 80 people died, hundreds of thousands were displaced, and landslides in Bosnia uncovered mass graves from the 1990s war. The floods caused billions of euros in damage across the region.

retained.title: Balkan Floods
retained.location: Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and Croatia
retained.description: Exceptional rainfall in mid-May 2014 caused devastating floods across the Sava River basin, including Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and Croatia. ICPDR reported at least 80 deaths after a week of flooding, with extensive damage to homes and infrastructure.

review.note: May 14 is a defensible period anchor for record rainfall, not an instantaneous UTC incident. ICPDR gives at least 80 regional deaths; do not attribute them only to two countries. Mass-grave and displacement details not fully established here are removed. A period anchor must not be treated as a verified UTC incident date; this date blocker remains after the description correction.

sources.name: ICPDR and ISRBC, final flood report

original.title: Camp Speicher Massacre
original.description: On 12 June 2014, days after capturing the city of Tikrit, fighters of the Islamic State group captured and systematically executed hundreds of unarmed Iraqi Air Force cadets from Camp Speicher military base. Iraqi authorities put the death toll at about 1,700, while human rights investigators documented at least several hundred victims in mass graves. The United Nations described the massacre as a war crime and possible crime against humanity.

retained.title: Camp Speicher Massacre
retained.description: From June 12 to at least June 14, 2014, Islamic State fighters killed about 1,700 soldiers, cadets and volunteers who had fled Tikrit Air Academy, known as Camp Speicher. UNITAD documented the mass killings in and around Tikrit's presidential palace complex.

review.note: Updated primary evidence gives about 1,700 soldiers, cadets and volunteers killed June 12 through at least June 14 near presidential palaces, not all at the base or all on June 12. Retain June 12 as start and 1,700 as approximation. Only one checked source is recorded; the two-source publication minimum is not met.

original.title: Gaza War (Operation Protective Edge)
original.description: Israel and Hamas fought a 50-day conflict in the Gaza Strip from 8 July to 26 August 2014. United Nations figures recorded 2,251 Palestinian deaths, including 1,462 civilians and 540 children, alongside 66 Israeli soldiers, six Israeli civilians and one foreign national. More than 11,000 people were injured and hundreds of thousands displaced by airstrikes, rocket fire and ground operations.
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs

retained.title: Gaza War (Operation Protective Edge)
retained.description: The Gaza conflict lasted from July 8 to August 26, 2014. UNRWA records 2,251 Palestinian deaths, including 1,462 believed to be civilians, among them 551 children, and 11,231 Palestinian injuries. The numeric toll here is Palestinian-only and does not include deaths on the Israeli side.
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs

review.note: Original children count 540 should be 551 for the cited 2,251/1,462 dataset. Israeli-side counts differ between OCHA pages (67 soldiers plus six civilians versus 66 plus five Israeli civilians); do not silently merge them. 2,251 is Palestinian-only across July 8-August 26, not all conflict deaths. Exact UTC onset unestablished.

original.title: Typhoon Rammasun
original.description: Typhoon Rammasun, the strongest typhoon to hit the Philippines in decades, made landfall on Luzon in mid-July 2014 before crossing southern China and northern Vietnam. Around 190 people were killed across the three countries, more than a hundred of them in the Philippines, and hundreds of thousands of homes were damaged or destroyed. It was among the deadliest typhoons of the year.

retained.title: Typhoon Rammasun
retained.description: Typhoon Rammasun crossed the Philippines in mid-July 2014, then intensified over the South China Sea before striking southern China and affecting Vietnam. It caused widespread deaths and damage; country totals changed as assessments continued.

review.note: HKO's early figures are at least 98 Philippine deaths and 18 in China; secondary later totals are higher. A consistent final three-country 190 toll is not established. Strongest Philippine typhoon in decades is false after Haiyan in 2013. July 15 is landfall anchor, but precise UTC onset not checked.

original.title: Air Algérie Flight 5017 Crash
original.description: Air Algérie Flight 5017, an MD-83 flying from Ouagadougou to Algiers, crashed in the Gossi region of Mali on 24 July 2014 about an hour after takeoff. All 110 passengers and six crew members were killed, making it the deadliest accident in the airline's history. French investigators attributed the crash to ice accretion that triggered an aerodynamic stall.

retained.title: Air Algérie Flight 5017 Crash
retained.description: Air Algerie Flight 5017, operated by Swiftair with an MD-83, crashed near Gossi, Mali, at about 01:47 UTC on July 24, 2014, roughly half an hour after leaving Ouagadougou. All 110 passengers and six crew died. Investigators linked loss of speed and an unrecovered stall to probable ice obstruction of engine pressure sensors and the crew's response.

review.note: Final report supersedes inconsistent BEA landing-page metadata: 110 passengers plus six crew, July 24 at 01:47, takeoff about 01:15. Thus about half an hour, not about an hour. Ice likely obstructed engine pressure sensors, not simply airframe icing. Remove unsupported airline ranking. Only one checked source is recorded; the two-source publication minimum is not met.

sources.name: Mali investigation commission, final report hosted by BEA

original.title: Ludian Earthquake
original.description: A magnitude 6.1 earthquake struck Ludian County in Yunnan province, southwestern China, on 3 August 2014. The shallow quake triggered landslides that buried villages and destroyed tens of thousands of homes; 617 people were killed, more than 100 went missing and over 3,100 were injured. It was China's deadliest earthquake in several years.

retained.title: Ludian Earthquake
retained.description: An earthquake struck Ludian County, Yunnan, on August 3, 2014. China's earthquake authority's August 8 assessment recorded 617 deaths, 112 missing people and 3,143 injuries. The quake destroyed homes and caused landslides.

review.note: 617, 112 missing and 3,143 injured are the August 8 assessment, not an unexplained final count. Replacement keeps those categories distinct and omits unsupported relative ranking; afternoon China event remains August 3 UTC. The August 8 snapshot does not establish the eventual final toll, particularly with 112 then missing; withhold pending final casualty reconciliation.

sources.name: People's Daily/China News Service, official August 8 tally

original.title: ISIS Genocide of Yazidis in Sinjar
original.description: On 3 August 2014, fighters of the Islamic State group overran the Yazidi heartland of Sinjar in northern Iraq, forcing tens of thousands of people onto Mount Sinjar, where hundreds died of thirst and heat. Men and boys were executed, while women and girls were taken as sex slaves; the United Nations later estimated that about 5,000 Yazidis were killed in the 2014-2017 campaign. The UN formally declared the attacks on the Yazidis an act of genocide.

retained.title: ISIS Genocide of Yazidis in Sinjar
retained.description: Islamic State fighters attacked the Yazidi community around Sinjar on August 3, 2014, committing mass killings, abductions and sexual enslavement. UN investigators found genocidal acts. Published estimates describe thousands killed, but differ in time span, population and counting method.

review.note: UN accounts give estimates ranging from 2,000-5,500 killed since August 3 and as many as 5,000 men in 2016 remarks, not an exact 2014-2017 total. Genocide finding supported, but numeric scope remains unresolved. No exact UTC onset established.

sources.name: UN Special Adviser on Prevention of Genocide, 2016 remarks

original.title: Kashmir Floods
original.description: Torrential monsoon rains in the first half of September 2014 caused catastrophic flooding in Indian-administered Jammu and Kashmir and parts of Pakistan-administered Kashmir. The Jhelum River broke its banks and submerged much of Srinagar, killing around 500 people and stranding hundreds of thousands, with relief operations hampered by the scale of the flooding. It was the region's worst flooding in decades.

retained.title: Kashmir Floods
retained.description: Monsoon flooding in September 2014 devastated Jammu and Kashmir and parts of Pakistan, including Punjab. Srinagar was extensively inundated. Fatality reports covered different regions and reporting dates, so a Kashmir-only total must not be inferred from combined India-Pakistan figures.

review.note: Flood deaths predate September 7. 500 combines incompatible regional/time scopes; NDMA gives 367 in Pakistan including Punjab, not solely Kashmir. Resolve intended geographic extent and onset before replacing date/toll.

original.title: Iguala Mass Kidnapping of 43 Students
original.description: On 26 September 2014, municipal police in Iguala, Guerrero, Mexico, confronted students from the Ayotzinapa Rural Teachers' College who had commandeered buses to travel to a protest. Six people were killed and 43 students were abducted and have never been found; investigators concluded police handed them to a drug cartel, which killed them and burned most of the remains. The case triggered a national political crisis in Mexico.

retained.title: Iguala Mass Kidnapping of 43 Students
retained.description: Forty-three Ayotzinapa students disappeared after attacks in Iguala on the night of September 26-27, 2014, local time; six other people were killed. Independent investigators challenged the official claim that all 43 bodies were burned at a single rubbish dump. By March 2024, remains of three students had been identified, while the full fate of the group remained unresolved.

review.note: 43 is disappeared students, not a confirmed death count; six other people were killed during the attacks. Three students' remains had been identified by March 2024, contradicting 'never found.' Independent evidence rejects the original dump-burning reconstruction. Night September 26-27 local likely falls September 27 UTC, but precise start not confirmed.

original.title: Kano Central Mosque Attack
original.description: Suicide bombers attacked the Central Mosque of Kano in northern Nigeria on 28 November 2014 during Friday prayers. The first bomb exploded during the imam's sermon, and gunmen opened fire on worshippers fleeing the blast, killing around 120 people. The Boko Haram insurgency was widely held responsible for the attack on the mosque of the Emir of Kano.

retained.title: Kano Central Mosque Attack
retained.description: Bombers and gunmen attacked Kano's Central Mosque during Friday prayers on November 28, 2014. Contemporary emergency reports estimated about 120 deaths, although early hospital counts were lower. Boko Haram was widely suspected of responsibility.

review.note: Friday November 28 prayer-time attack supported; 120 was an emergency-source estimate while hospitals reported over 80. Attribute the approximate toll and do not assert a definitive claim of responsibility. The competing hospital and emergency-source figures are not a reconciled final toll; the approximate wording alone does not resolve the numeric field.

original.title: Army Public School Attack, Peshawar
original.description: On 16 December 2014, nine gunmen from the Pakistani Taliban (Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan) stormed the Army Public School in Peshawar, going classroom to classroom and firing on students. The siege lasted about eight hours and killed 141 people, including 132 schoolchildren, with around 150 injured. It was one of the deadliest terrorist attacks in Pakistan's history and prompted a nationwide military crackdown on militant groups.

retained.title: Army Public School Attack, Peshawar
retained.description: Pakistani Taliban gunmen attacked the Army Public School in Peshawar on December 16, 2014, killing students and staff. The initial reported toll of 141 rose in subsequent accounts; a reconciled final count and breakdown are needed before treating one figure as definitive.

review.note: 141 was initial; later reports give 148 and 150, with differing child counts. Seven attackers reported initially, not nine; other retrospective accounts give six. Exact final victim/perpetrator totals require reconciliation. Morning time is December 16 UTC.

original.title: Baga massacre by Boko Haram
original.description: Boko Haram militants seized the town of Baga in Borno State and attacked Baga and surrounding towns, setting homes and shops ablaze and killing civilians as they fled. Nigerian officials reported a toll of about 150, while Amnesty International estimated, based on witness accounts, that as many as 2,000 people were killed. Tens of thousands of residents fled across Lake Chad into Niger.

retained.title: Baga massacre by Boko Haram
retained.description: Boko Haram attacked Baga and Doron Baga in early January 2015, beginning on January 3. Satellite imagery showed widespread destruction, and witnesses described mass killings. Reported tolls ranged from an official figure around 150, including fighters, to local estimates as high as 2,000; the final number remains uncertain.

review.note: 2,000 was an upper estimate from local accounts, not a confirmed Amnesty body count; government put deaths including fighters at about 150. Satellite destruction cannot by itself resolve deaths. January 3 is campaign start, not a single-day total.

sources.name: Amnesty International, satellite and witness evidence

original.title: Nepal earthquake (Gorkha)
original.description: A magnitude 7.8 earthquake struck the Gorkha district of central Nepal, about 80 km northwest of Kathmandu, triggering avalanches on Mount Everest and landslides across the Himalayas. The Nepal government confirmed 8,857 deaths in Nepal, with at least 107 more in India, China and Bangladesh, for a combined toll of roughly 8,960; more than 21,000 people were injured and over 600,000 buildings were destroyed or damaged. It was Nepal's deadliest earthquake in over 80 years.
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)

retained.title: Nepal earthquake (Gorkha)
retained.description: A magnitude 7.8 earthquake struck central Nepal on April 25, 2015, causing catastrophic building damage, landslides and avalanches. USGS's 2015 summary attributes 8,964 deaths to the disaster, citing OCHA. The toll's treatment of later aftershocks needs reconciliation with separately listed events.
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)

review.note: USGS attributes 8,964 deaths to the April event citing OCHA, and discusses a sequence including later aftershocks. Country decomposition in original is not confirmed, and separate May 12 row risks double counting. April 25 11:56 local is 06:11 UTC.

original.title: Nepal earthquake aftershock
original.description: A magnitude 7.3 aftershock struck Nepal east of Kathmandu less than three weeks after the Gorkha earthquake, killing at least 218 people, most of them in the Sindhupalchok and Dolakha districts, and injuring more than 3,500. The quake triggered fresh avalanches and building collapses in a country where millions were still living in temporary shelter.

retained.title: Nepal earthquake aftershock
retained.description: A magnitude 7.3 earthquake struck east of Kathmandu on May 12, 2015, following the April 25 Gorkha earthquake. It caused additional deaths and destruction in Nepal and neighbouring countries. Its separate fatality count must be distinguished from cumulative totals for the earthquake sequence.

review.note: Magnitude/date supported; 218 combines 153 Nepal, 62 India, two Bangladesh and one China in secondary accounting, not 218 in Nepal. Primary country totals and exclusion from April cumulative toll are not established.

original.title: Indian heat wave
original.description: An extreme heat wave with temperatures exceeding 47 degrees Celsius swept southern and eastern India in May 2015, killing at least 2,500 people. Andhra Pradesh, with about 1,735 deaths, and Telangana, with about 585, were hardest hit. It was India's deadliest heat wave since 1979.

retained.title: Indian heat wave
retained.location: India, particularly Andhra Pradesh and Telangana
retained.description: Extreme heat affected India during May and early June 2015, with particularly severe mortality in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana. Contemporary estimates exceeded 2,000 deaths, while surveillance totals differed in coverage. A precise onset date and reconciled death toll remain unestablished.

review.note: May 26 is a reporting-period date, not established onset. NOAA says at least 2,300; NASA cites 2,500 reporting, while national surveillance records a lower figure under different reporting coverage. Resolve onset, death definition and countrywide scope; do not preserve Andhra Pradesh as entire location.

original.title: Karachi heat wave
original.description: A heat wave with temperatures reaching 44-49 degrees Celsius struck Karachi and southern Pakistan during the Muslim fasting month of Ramadan, killing at least 1,265 people in the city, most of them poor residents without electricity or water, and about 2,000 across the country. Hospitals reported a surge in heat-stroke cases and morgues were overwhelmed as power outages worsened the crisis.

retained.title: Karachi heat wave
retained.description: A severe heatwave struck Karachi and other parts of Sindh in June 2015 during Ramadan. Karachi reached 44.8 C on June 20, and hospitals faced large numbers of heat-related patients. Death estimates changed rapidly and must distinguish the city from provincial or nationwide totals.

review.note: Heatwave predates June 24; PMD identifies June 19-23 and a Karachi maximum 44.8 C June 20. 49 C should not be attributed to Karachi. Neither final city toll 1,265 nor national 2,000 is established by these sources; original poverty and utilities attribution too categorical.

original.title: Sousse beach attack
original.description: A gunman affiliated with the Islamic State opened fire on tourists at the Imperial Marhaba beach hotel in Sousse, a popular Tunisian coastal resort, killing 38 people, 30 of them British, and wounding 39. Security forces shot the attacker dead. It was Tunisia's deadliest terrorist attack.

retained.title: Sousse beach attack
retained.description: A gunman attacked holidaymakers at the Imperial Marhaba hotel and beach at Port El Kantaoui near Sousse, Tunisia, shortly before midday on June 26, 2015. Thirty-eight victims were killed, including 30 British citizens.

review.note: Police confirms June 26 shortly before midday, 38 victims including 30 British. Remove unverified exact injury count and superlative; 38 excludes attacker. Midday Tunisia date unchanged UTC. Only one checked source is recorded; the two-source publication minimum is not met.

sources.name: UK National Police Chiefs' Council, commemoration

original.title: Tianjin warehouse explosions
original.description: A series of explosions at a hazardous-chemicals warehouse in the Binhai New Area of Tianjin, involving roughly 800 tonnes of ammonium nitrate and stored nitrocellulose, destroyed nearby buildings and killed 173 people, including 104 firefighters, injuring about 800. An official investigation attributed the first blast to the overheating and auto-ignition of dry nitrocellulose and noted that the depot was sited close to residential areas.

retained.title: Tianjin warehouse explosions
retained.description: A fire and explosions at a hazardous-goods warehouse in Tianjin on August 12, 2015, killed 165 people, with eight others missing, according to the official investigation. Another 798 were hospitalized. Investigators traced the fire to nitrocellulose that had dried and self-heated.

review.note: Official investigation distinguishes 165 confirmed dead plus eight missing, including five missing port firefighters. Thus 173 and 104 firefighters include missing presumed dead. Proposed count is confirmed-only; remove unverified explosive quantities. Late night August 12 local remains August 12 UTC. Only one checked source is recorded; the two-source publication minimum is not met.

original.title: Yemen wedding party airstrike
original.description: A Saudi-led coalition airstrike hit a wedding party in a village near the Red Sea port of Mokha in Taiz governorate, Yemen, killing at least 131 people, including many women and children, and wounding hundreds. Yemeni officials and residents reported the toll, and Human Rights Watch documented the attack; the coalition later acknowledged the strike and said it had been a mistake.

retained.title: Yemen wedding party airstrike
retained.description: A wedding gathering near Mokha, Yemen, was struck on September 28, 2015. Residents attributed it to the Saudi-led coalition, which denied involvement. Contemporary reporting put deaths at 131, while a UN panel later cited at least 135. This was distinct from the October 2015 Sanaban wedding attack and the October 2016 Sanaa funeral strike.

review.note: Conflation: Mokha wedding was September 28; Sanaban wedding was October 7; acknowledged October 8 strike concerns Sanaa funeral in 2016. Mokha reports 131 versus UN panel at least135; coalition denied responsibility. Supported local calendar correction supplied, but precise UTC time and final toll unresolved.

original.title: Ankara peace rally bombing
original.description: Two suicide bombers, later linked to the Islamic State, detonated bombs among crowds gathered for a peace rally near Ankara's central train station, killing at least 102 people, the figure given by Turkish prosecutors, and injuring more than 500. Some later counts put the death toll as high as 109. It was the deadliest terrorist attack in Turkey's history, surpassing the 2013 Reyhanli bombings.

retained.title: Ankara peace rally bombing
retained.description: Two suicide bombers attacked a peace-rally gathering outside Ankara's central railway station on October 10, 2015. The toll rose to 103 in November 2015; later commemorative accounts differ on whether 103 or 104 victims are counted. Islamic State was identified as responsible.

review.note: 102 superseded by103 in November2015; 2025 accounts still differ103/104. The record's109 is not reconciled with these sources. Morning October10 date sound; final fatality definition and later deaths unresolved.

original.title: Hindu Kush earthquake
original.description: A magnitude 7.5 earthquake centered in the Hindu Kush mountains of northeastern Afghanistan shook a wide area of South Asia, killing 399 people, including at least 280 in Pakistan, 115 in Afghanistan and 4 in India, and injuring about 2,500. Hundreds of homes collapsed across northern Pakistan and Afghanistan, and shaking was felt as far away as Delhi.

retained.title: Hindu Kush earthquake
retained.description: A magnitude 7.5 earthquake struck Afghanistan's Hindu Kush on October 26, 2015. Reports recorded 280 deaths in Pakistan and 115 in Afghanistan, with widespread damage across both countries. A consistent all-country total remains to be established.

review.note: USGS confirms magnitude7.5 at09:09UTC October26; primary reports support280 Pakistan and115 Afghanistan. Four India deaths and exact399 total not independently established. Do not silently certify whole regional sum.

original.title: Chennai floods
original.description: Torrential northeast-monsoon rains, among the heaviest recorded in a century, flooded Chennai and surrounding districts of Tamil Nadu in late November and December 2015, killing more than 500 people, with at least 422 deaths officially recorded in Tamil Nadu alone. Much of the city remained submerged for weeks, and transport, power and communications were disrupted across a region home to tens of millions of people; neighboring Andhra Pradesh was also affected.

retained.title: Chennai floods
retained.description: Repeated northeast-monsoon rains flooded Chennai and other parts of Tamil Nadu in November-December 2015. Official and research accounts give differing death totals for the city, state and wider region. The final severe flooding followed early-December rain, but losses accumulated over a longer period.

review.note: 500 is broader South India estimate,422 appears in NIDM,470 is statewide monsoon count. December1 does not represent the whole November-December episode. Resolve period and geography before assigning a count/date. NGO CAG differs from Comptroller and Auditor General.

sources.name: NITI Aayog, Tamil Nadu flood review
Citizen consumer and civic Action Group, assessment

original.title: Lahore Easter park bombing
original.description: A suicide bomber detonated in the crowded Gulshan-e-Iqbal Park in Lahore on Easter Sunday, targeting Christian families gathered for the holiday. Seventy-five people were killed, including at least 29 children, and more than 300 were wounded. Jamaat-ul-Ahrar, a faction of the Pakistani Taliban, claimed responsibility for the attack.

retained.title: Lahore Easter park bombing
retained.description: A suicide bombing struck Lahore's Gulshan-e-Iqbal Park on Easter Sunday, March 27, 2016. Jamaat-ul-Ahrar claimed responsibility and said it targeted Christians. Published death totals differ, including reports of victims dying later from injuries.

review.note: Date, location and attack identity are supported. PIPS's annual report gives at least 74 deaths including 29 children and over 233 injuries. SATP's incident prose says 74, its table 75, and its April 21 entry reports a later victim raising the toll to 78. These inconsistencies do not establish a final 75 or a final child/injury breakdown. Christian targeting was the attackers' stated intent, not evidence that every victim was Christian.

original.title: Karrada shopping district bombing
original.description: A suicide truck bomb exploded shortly after midnight in Baghdad's Karrada district, an area crowded with families shopping during Ramadan, setting several buildings ablaze. At least 292 people were killed in the immediate aftermath, with the final toll later placed at more than 320 dead and hundreds wounded. Islamic State claimed responsibility for the deadliest single attack in Iraq since 2003.

retained.title: Karrada shopping district bombing
retained.description: An Islamic State-claimed suicide bombing devastated Baghdad's Karrada shopping district shortly after midnight locally on July 3, 2016. Later reports attributed differing tolls of 323 and 324 to Iraqi authorities, after much lower preliminary counts.

review.note: Rudaw attributes 324 to the health minister on July 31, while same-period AFP reporting gives 323; both exceed the early 250/292 counts. The attack occurred shortly after midnight July 3 local time, meaning July 2 UTC; exact timing currently has only a tertiary source here. Later tertiary totals and a minister's reported much higher estimate also prevent treating 324 as an uncontested final toll. Proposed UTC shift requires stronger timing corroboration before publication.

original.title: 2016 China floods (Yangtze basin)
original.description: Torrential monsoon rains produced the worst flooding in China since 1998, hitting the Yangtze and Huai river basins across 26 provinces and affecting an estimated 32 million people, with hundreds of thousands left homeless. More than 350 people died in the floods, and a June 23 EF4 tornado in Jiangsu Province that killed at least 99 people brought the combined toll to more than 440. Rivers breached their banks in multiple provinces, including Hubei and Anhui, and damage was estimated in the tens of billions of dollars.

retained.title: 2016 China floods (Yangtze basin)
retained.description: Torrential monsoon rains produced the worst flooding in China since 1998, hitting the Yangtze and Huai river basins across 26 provinces and affecting an estimated 32 million people, with hundreds of thousands left homeless. More than 350 people died in the floods, and a June 23 EF4 tornado in Jiangsu Province that killed at least 99 people brought the combined toll to more than 440. Rivers breached their banks in multiple provinces, including Hubei and Anhui, and damage was estimated in the tens of billions of dollars.

review.note: July 5 is a reporting date, not an established onset of the June-September flood season. The 449 total combines more than 350 flood deaths with 99 deaths in the separate June 23 Jiangsu tornado, inconsistent with the Yangtze flood title. TIME's July 5 report gives 186 dead and 45 missing as of the preceding Sunday, a preliminary count, not support for 449 flood deaths. Define flood period and geography before selecting date or final toll.

original.title: Attempted coup in Turkey
original.description: A faction of the Turkish armed forces attempted to overthrow the government on the night of July 15, bombing the parliament building in Ankara, seizing bridges and key infrastructure in Istanbul, and announcing military control of the country. The government, aided by large pro-democracy street protests, regained control within about 24 hours. Estimates of the dead range from 270 to 350, with roughly 300 people killed including about 180 civilians, and more than 2,100 wounded.

retained.title: Attempted coup in Turkey
retained.description: A faction of Turkey's armed forces attempted to overthrow the government on the night of July 15, 2016, with violence in Ankara and Istanbul. The attempt failed. Later official commemorations count 251 people killed opposing the coup, a narrower scope than totals including coup participants.

review.note: July 15-16 attempted coup in Ankara and Istanbul is supported. Later Turkish commemoration counts 251 people killed opposing the coup, excluding coup participants; HRW reported at least 241 citizens/security personnel earlier. Neither establishes a consistently scoped combined toll of 300 or the claimed 180 civilians. Later injury counts also vary. Keep the core toll unresolved rather than silently substitute a loyalist-only count.

original.title: Typhoon Lionrock floods in North Korea
original.description: Typhoon Lionrock crossed Japan's Tohoku region on August 30 and produced torrential rains that caused devastating flash floods in North Korea's North Hamgyong Province along the Tumen River, washing away entire villages and leaving tens of thousands homeless. Initial UN assessments counted 133 dead and 395 missing in North Korea; later analyses put the country's death toll at more than 500, with about 550 total deaths when the 22 killed in Japan and 3 in Russia are included.

retained.title: Typhoon Lionrock floods in North Korea
retained.description: Heavy rain associated with Typhoon Lionrock caused severe flooding in northeastern North Korea in late August 2016. A September 14 UN update reported 138 confirmed deaths and 400 people missing. Those missing were not confirmed dead in that report.

review.note: The September 11 UN report lists 133 confirmed dead and 395 missing; September 14 gives 138 and 400. Neither supports more than 500 confirmed deaths in North Korea or 550 internationally. Missing people cannot simply be added to confirmed deaths. OCHA references August 29 while ACAPS describes August 30; Japan landfall does not establish North Korea's flood onset or its UTC date. Core date and final toll remain unresolved.

sources.name: United Nations in DPR Korea, September 11 update
United Nations in DPR Korea, September 14 update

original.title: Sanaa funeral hall airstrike
original.description: A Saudi-led coalition airstrike struck a large funeral hall in Sanaa's Sabeen district during a mourning ceremony for the father of Houthi-appointed Interior Minister Jalal al-Rowaishan. At least 155 people were killed and more than 525 wounded, including senior Houthi figures. The attack drew international condemnation, the United States said it would reassess support for the coalition, and the coalition later acknowledged an error in conducting the strike.

retained.title: Sanaa funeral hall airstrike
retained.description: Saudi-led coalition airstrikes hit a funeral ceremony in Sanaa on October 8, 2016. The coalition initially denied responsibility before acknowledging the attack. Reported casualty counts differed and were preliminary.

review.note: October 8 funeral attack and coalition responsibility are supported; HRW documents the initial denial and subsequent acknowledgement. The 155 figure was explicitly preliminary in same-day reporting. UN initially reported over 140, while HRW later cited the health ministry's at least 110/610, with identification incomplete. No reconciled final 155/525 tally is established. Preserve this contradiction, not a definitive replacement death count.

original.title: Quetta police training college attack
original.description: Three attackers stormed the Balochistan Police College in Quetta late on October 24, taking unarmed police recruits hostage and battling security forces for several hours before all three were killed. At least 61 people, mostly recruits, were killed and more than 165 wounded. Islamic State's Khorasan branch claimed responsibility for the deadliest attack in Pakistan since the 2014 Peshawar school massacre.

retained.title: Quetta police training college attack
retained.description: Attackers stormed the police training college near Quetta late on October 24, 2016. Lashkar-e-Jhangvi claimed collaboration with Islamic State in the attack. Published victim counts range above the initially reported 61.

review.note: The Tribune supports the October 24 attack and early 61/165 count. Later Dawn gives 64 including two non-cadet personnel. Australia's listing gives at least 62 and notes LeJ claimed collaboration with Islamic State. The original exact total is not reconciled. Remove the false deadliest-since-2014 ranking: the Lahore Easter bombing in 2016 was deadlier.

original.title: South Sudan famine declared
original.description: On 20 February 2017 the United Nations formally declared famine in parts of South Sudan's Unity State (Leer and Mayendit counties), the first famine declared anywhere since 2011. The UN estimated that 100,000 people were in famine conditions, with roughly 4.9 million people needing emergency food assistance and a further one million on the brink of famine. Armed conflict and a collapsed economy prevented aid access; famine-related excess deaths in 2017 were estimated in the tens of thousands (best estimate ~20,000), with UNICEF reporting severe acute malnutrition rates far above emergency thresholds. The famine officially subsided in mid-2017 but hunger conditions persisted across the country.

retained.title: South Sudan famine declared
retained.description: Famine was declared in South Sudan's Leer and Mayendit counties on February 20, 2017. UN agencies reported about 100,000 people facing starvation and one million more on the brink of famine. Famine conditions eased by June following increased assistance, while severe food insecurity persisted.

review.note: February 20 is the supported declaration date, not famine onset. UN sources substantiate Leer/Mayendit, roughly 100,000 facing starvation, 4.9 million severely food insecure and one million near famine; June 21 reports famine easing but worsening nationwide hunger. They do not establish an event-specific 20,000 excess-death estimate. Famine classification mortality thresholds cannot be converted into that annual toll.

sources.name: UN Secretary-General report on South Sudan

original.title: Peru floods and mudslides
original.description: Torrential rains linked to a coastal El Niño event from January through April 2017 caused catastrophic flooding and mudslides across Peru's coastal regions, overwhelming rivers in Lima and the northern departments of Piura, Lambayeque and La Libertad. The Peruvian government reported 162 deaths, with more than 270,000 people left homeless and about one million affected; the EM-DAT international disaster database records a toll of 177. Landslides buried villages and the flooding destroyed bridges, highways and thousands of homes, isolating communities for weeks.

retained.title: Peru floods and mudslides
retained.description: Coastal El Nino conditions caused severe floods and mudslides in Peru during 2016-2017. Peru's meteorological agency reports 162 deaths and nearly 1.5 million people affected. The disaster spanned several months rather than beginning on March 20.

review.note: SENAMHI supports 162 deaths and nearly 1.5 million affected for the coastal El Nino disaster, formally December 2016-May 2017. March 20 is a publication date for a much earlier 75-death report, not the event onset. RPP attributes 162 to an August INDECI report. The claimed EM-DAT 177 and homeless scope were not independently established. Date remains unresolved even after replacing the prose.

original.title: Khan Sheikhoun chemical attack
original.description: On 4 April 2017 an airstrike released sarin gas on the rebel-held town of Khan Sheikhoun in Idlib province. At least 89 people were killed and more than 500 injured, including many women and children, with victims showing classic nerve-agent symptoms; medical workers filmed victims convulsing and foaming at the mouth. The OPCW-UN Joint Investigative Mechanism concluded the Syrian air force dropped the sarin, a finding echoed by the UN Commission of Inquiry, the United States, France and the UK. The attack prompted a US Tomahawk missile strike on Syria's Shayrat air base days later.

retained.title: Khan Sheikhoun chemical attack
retained.description: Sarin was used as a chemical weapon at Khan Shaykhun, Syria, on April 4, 2017. The OPCW-UN Joint Investigative Mechanism attributed responsibility to the Syrian Arab Republic. The OPCW fact-finding team identified approximately 100 fatalities but could not establish an exact total.

review.note: OPCW confirms sarin use on April 4, and the JIM attributes responsibility to the Syrian Arab Republic. Do not confuse the FFM's chemical identification remit with JIM's attribution remit. FFM paragraphs 5.80 and 6.13 describe approximately 100 fatalities after potential duplicates among 107 reported names, explicitly unable to determine exact numbers; this does not verify 89 or over 500 distinct injured. The exact toll remains unresolved, independently of the supported attack attribution.

sources.name: OPCW-UN Joint Investigative Mechanism report S/2017/904
US Department of State, JIM report summary

original.title: Freetown mudslide and floods, Sierra Leone
original.description: After days of torrential rain, a hillside above the Babadorie River valley collapsed on 14 August 2017, sending a wall of mud and debris through the Regent district on the outskirts of Freetown, burying homes and residents as they slept. The final official death toll declared 1,141 dead or missing, with more than 3,000 people displaced and hundreds of children orphaned, according to the World Bank's damage and loss assessment. Deforestation and unregulated hillside construction were cited by authorities as factors amplifying the disaster.

retained.title: Freetown mudslide and floods, Sierra Leone
retained.description: A major landslide entered the Babadorie River valley near Freetown on August 14, 2017, worsening widespread flooding. The World Bank assessment records about 6,000 people affected across the Western Area and 1,141 declared dead or missing, without equating all missing people with confirmed deaths.

review.note: The August 14 landslide and flooding are supported, but 1,141 explicitly combines dead and missing, not confirmed deaths. The assessment concerns the wider Western Area disaster, not solely Regent. No reconciled confirmed-death total was established here. Remove unsupported orphan and displacement counts while retaining the documented affected scope.

sources.name: World Bank damage and loss assessment

original.title: South Asia floods
original.description: Monsoon floods triggered by some of the heaviest rainfall in decades inundated large parts of Bangladesh, northern and northeastern India, and Nepal during August 2017, displacing more than 40 million people. Confirmed fatalities numbered 1,288 by 2 September 2017 (over 1,400 across the three countries per some tallies), with hundreds of thousands of homes destroyed, crops ruined and outbreaks of waterborne disease reported in relief camps. The flooding destroyed infrastructure on a massive scale, leaving millions dependent on emergency food and shelter aid from national governments, the UN and the Red Cross.

retained.title: South Asia floods
retained.description: Monsoon flooding affected Bangladesh, India and Nepal in August 2017. On September 2, UNICEF reported at least 1,288 deaths since mid-August and estimated more than 45 million people affected. Affected population is not the same as displaced population.

review.note: UNICEF's September 2 release supports at least 1,288 reported deaths since mid-August and over 45 million affected, not 40 million displaced. August 28 is an unsupported single-day anchor within an ongoing monsoon disaster. The toll is a dated preliminary count, not a reconciled season total; do not replace the date with the publication date and call it verified.

original.title: Mogadishu truck bombing
original.description: On 14 October 2017 a truck packed with explosives detonated at a busy intersection near the Safari Hotel in Mogadishu, followed shortly by a car bomb attack in the Madina district. The blasts killed at least 587 people and injured more than 300, according to a parliamentary investigative committee that concluded its count in March 2018, with hundreds of victims burned beyond recognition; a two-story building collapsed onto the truck's blast crater. No group claimed responsibility, though Somali officials attributed the attack to al-Shabaab. It was the deadliest bombing in Somalia's history.

retained.title: Mogadishu truck bombing
retained.description: A truck bombing devastated Mogadishu's Zoobe intersection on October 14, 2017. The Zobe Rescue Committee later reported 587 deaths, but a UN monitoring report cites 582 and also notes a separate 587 count. The final toll and scope of the day's separate explosions need reconciliation.

review.note: Hiiraan's March 5 report attributes 587 to the Zobe Rescue Committee of volunteers and officials, not a parliamentary committee. Its final report was released March 4, increasing December's 512. The UN monitoring report gives as many as 582 in its main text and notes ACLED's 587, an unresolved discrepancy. Also distinguish the principal truck blast from the second explosion before assigning a combined toll. Original Hiiraan URL failed to open; an indexed rendering supplied the article text.

sources.name: Hiiraan Online report, accessible archived rendering
UN Somalia Monitoring Group report S/2018/1002

original.title: Battle of Raqqa ends
original.description: The Syrian Democratic Forces, backed by heavy US-led coalition airstrikes, captured the Islamic State's self-declared capital of Raqqa on 17 October 2017 after a four-month siege. The battle left the city largely destroyed, with most buildings ruined by bombing and street fighting, and tens of thousands of residents displaced. Estimates of civilians killed during the campaign range from about 1,300 to 1,873 (Airwars and Amnesty International: 1,300-1,600 from coalition airstrikes; local monitors: 1,854-1,873), including hundreds who died as IS used residents as human shields or as they fled through minefields; the Syrian Observatory for Human Rights counted 1,540 civilians dead.

retained.title: End of the Raqqa campaign declared
retained.description: The SDF and US-led coalition operation to capture Raqqa from Islamic State was declared complete on October 17, 2017. A later Amnesty International and Airwars investigation reported more than 1,600 civilians killed by coalition air and artillery strikes during the June-October campaign. That figure is not an all-perpetrator battle total.

review.note: The operation was declared complete October 17 after beginning June 6. Amnesty/Airwars' later investigation reports more than 1,600 civilian deaths from coalition air and artillery strikes, not a 1,300-1,600 airstrike-only range. That source-specific count does not establish the original 1,800 all-perpetrator battle total or reconcile the several local-monitor totals. Keep core toll unresolved; do not create a synthetic midpoint across differently scoped estimates.

original.title: Siege of Marawi ends
original.description: The five-month armed confrontation between Philippine security forces and the Maute and Abu Sayyaf groups loyal to the Islamic State over the city of Marawi, which began on 23 May 2017, ended on 23 October 2017 when the military announced full recapture of the city. The urban battle killed an estimated 1,233 people, including 978 militants, 168 government forces and 87 civilians, and left most of Marawi, the Philippines' only predominantly Muslim city, in ruins; hundreds of thousands of residents were displaced and reconstruction cost billions. It was the longest urban battle fought by the Philippine military since World War II.

retained.title: Siege of Marawi ends
retained.description: Fighting between Philippine forces and Islamic State-aligned militants in Marawi began on May 23, 2017. The government declared the city liberated on October 17 and announced the end of combat operations on October 23. Published casualty breakdowns differ in their inclusion of civilians who died of illness.

review.note: October 23 is the declared end of combat operations; the separate liberation announcement was October 17. The original 1,233 sums 978 militants, 168 government personnel and 87 civilians; tertiary reporting says 40 of those civilians died of illness. The Army-hosted clipping repeats some later numbers but an authoritative reconciled total and direct/indirect scope were not established; the presidential briefing failed to open. Remove the inaccurate only-Muslim-majority-city claim and other ancillary rankings/costs. The exact total remains unresolved.

sources.name: Philippine Presidential Communications Office, October 27 briefing

original.title: Kabul voter registration center bombing
original.description: A suicide bomber attacked a voter registration center in the Dasht-e-Barchi district of western Kabul, a predominantly Shia Hazara area, during Afghanistan's parliamentary election registration process. The blast killed at least 57 people and wounded more than 100, mostly civilians queued to obtain voter cards. The Islamic State Khorasan Province claimed responsibility for the attack, one of a series targeting the 2018 election process.

retained.title: Kabul voter registration center bombing
retained.description: A suicide bomber attacked a voter registration center in the Dasht-e-Barchi district of western Kabul, a predominantly Shia Hazara area, during Afghanistan's parliamentary election registration process. The blast killed at least 57 people and wounded more than 100, mostly civilians queued to obtain voter cards. The Islamic State Khorasan Province claimed responsibility for the attack, one of a series targeting the 2018 election process.

review.note: 57 was an initial toll. Later reporting gives more than 60, with secondary summaries giving 69; UNAMA records 198 total civilian casualties without a fatality breakdown in the retrieved page. Exact final death count and breakdown remain unresolved; date, registration-site identity and IS attribution are supported.

original.title: Volcán de Fuego eruption
original.description: Guatemala's Volcán de Fuego erupted violently, sending pyroclastic flows and ash that buried the villages of San Miguel Los Lotes and El Rodeo in mud and rock. The eruption killed 425 people according to Guatemala's disaster agency (CONRED), injured hundreds, destroyed thousands of homes, and forced the evacuation of over 12,000 people, while dozens of victims were never recovered from the deposits.

retained.title: Volcán de Fuego eruption
retained.description: Guatemala's Volcán de Fuego erupted violently, sending pyroclastic flows and ash that buried the villages of San Miguel Los Lotes and El Rodeo in mud and rock. The eruption killed 425 people according to Guatemala's disaster agency (CONRED), injured hundreds, destroyed thousands of homes, and forced the evacuation of over 12,000 people, while dozens of victims were never recovered from the deposits.

review.note: June 3 eruption is established. The asserted 425 confirmed CONRED deaths is not established: reports variously combine recovered deaths and missing people, and the 2026 government-newspaper retrospective itself gives 429 dead plus 229 missing. Hundreds injured/thousands of homes destroyed also need final evidence. No numerical replacement proposed without reconciling categories.

original.title: Yemen famine and cholera crisis
original.description: The war-ravaged country faced the world's worst humanitarian crisis in 2018: UN agencies reported 8.4 million people one step away from famine and over 22 million in need of assistance, while a massive cholera outbreak killed at least 2,315 people out of more than 1.1 million suspected cases recorded since the epidemic began in 2017. Port restrictions, collapsed health infrastructure, and food insecurity compounded the crisis, with the UN warning that parts of the country could slip into famine.

retained.title: Yemen famine and cholera crisis
retained.description: The war-ravaged country faced the world's worst humanitarian crisis in 2018: UN agencies reported 8.4 million people one step away from famine and over 22 million in need of assistance, while a massive cholera outbreak killed at least 2,315 people out of more than 1.1 million suspected cases recorded since the epidemic began in 2017. Port restrictions, collapsed health infrastructure, and food insecurity compounded the crisis, with the UN warning that parts of the country could slip into famine.

review.note: The outbreak and humanitarian crisis are established, but July 1 is not established as an event or reporting cutoff. The 2,315 total needs its exact WHO reporting interval; this is a cumulative cholera figure, not famine deaths or deaths on July 1. The outbreak began in 2016, with a major wave in April 2017.

original.title: Western Japan floods and landslides
original.description: Record-breaking rainfall, in some areas exceeding 180 millimeters per hour, triggered devastating flooding and landslides across western Japan in early July 2018, most severely in Hiroshima, Okayama, and Ehime prefectures. Rivers burst their banks, and landslides destroyed hillside homes. At least 225 people were killed and thousands displaced in Japan's worst weather disaster in decades, prompting the evacuation of millions of residents.

retained.title: Western Japan floods and landslides
retained.description: Heavy rainfall from late June through early July 2018 caused flooding and landslides across western Japan, especially Hiroshima, Okayama and Ehime. A published mortality analysis recorded 237 deaths, including 115 in Hiroshima Prefecture. The July 6 calendar entry falls within the multi-day disaster.

review.note: 225 is an early reported tally; published mortality analysis gives 237. JMA documents June 28-July 8 rainfall, including cumulative totals over 1,800 mm, not the asserted 180 mm/hour. July 6 is an anchor within the disaster, not all deaths on that date. The precise July 6 calendar date remains an unestablished selection within a June 28-July 8 rainfall episode; explaining it as an anchor does not verify it as the event date.

original.title: Lombok earthquake sequence
original.description: A series of major earthquakes struck the island of Lombok between July 29 and August 19, 2018, the strongest being a magnitude 7.0 quake on August 5. The quakes destroyed more than 70,000 homes, triggered landslides on Mount Rinjani, and killed at least 563 people, including tourists in the Gili Islands, with over 1,000 injured and roughly 350,000 displaced.

retained.title: Lombok earthquake sequence
retained.description: A series of major earthquakes struck the island of Lombok between July 29 and August 19, 2018, the strongest being a magnitude 7.0 quake on August 5. The quakes destroyed more than 70,000 homes, triggered landslides on Mount Rinjani, and killed at least 563 people, including tourists in the Gili Islands, with over 1,000 injured and roughly 350,000 displaced.

review.note: August 5 date and magnitude 7.0 per Indonesian authority supported. 563 is a sequence-wide figure in secondary accounts. Need final BNPB report for death, housing and displacement totals and especially purported tourist deaths in the Gili Islands; sources retrieved do not establish those full-record details.

original.title: Kerala floods
original.description: Unprecedented monsoon rainfall, the heaviest in the Indian state in nearly a century, caused catastrophic flooding and landslides across Kerala in August 2018. All 14 districts of the state were affected, with the Periyar and Pamba rivers overflowing and over 100 dams releasing water. The state disaster management authority confirmed 483 deaths, while over 1.5 million people were displaced into relief camps and property damage was estimated at billions of dollars.

retained.title: Kerala floods
retained.description: Monsoon flooding and landslides devastated Kerala in August 2018. A case study hosted by the Kerala State Disaster Management Authority reports over 483 deaths and about one million evacuees, with 35 dams opened. Other assessments use different reporting intervals and totals; these deaths did not all occur on August 15.

review.note: Over 100 dams is wrong: state-hosted case study gives 35, UNDP 37. Report intervals produce 433 versus 483 deaths. Preserve 483 only as the broader case-study tally and make multi-day scope clear. The precise August 15 calendar anchor remains unestablished within the multi-day flood period; retain the supported prose correction but withhold until the date/period representation is resolved.

original.title: Typhoon Mangkhut
original.description: Typhoon Mangkhut, the strongest storm of the year, made landfall in northern Luzon, Philippines, on September 15, 2018, with sustained winds of 205 km/h. The typhoon triggered landslides in mining and farming areas, destroyed over 400,000 homes, and killed at least 134 people in the Philippines, with additional deaths reported in Hong Kong and southern China. Storm surges and flooding affected millions across the region.

retained.title: Typhoon Mangkhut
retained.description: Typhoon Mangkhut, the strongest storm of the year, made landfall in northern Luzon, Philippines, on September 15, 2018, with sustained winds of 205 km/h. The typhoon triggered landslides in mining and farming areas, destroyed over 400,000 homes, and killed at least 134 people in the Philippines, with additional deaths reported in Hong Kong and southern China. Storm surges and flooding affected millions across the region.

review.note: Landfall was early September 15 local time, September 14 UTC; UTC date correction supported. 134 is a multinational total in secondary summaries, not Philippine deaths; Hong Kong deaths and 400,000 destroyed homes are not substantiated. Keep unresolved until a consistent final geographic toll and damage definition are established.

original.title: MV Nyerere ferry capsizing
original.description: The passenger ferry MV Nyerere capsized minutes after leaving the dock at Ukerewe Island on Lake Victoria, Tanzania, on a journey to Bugolora in the Mwanza region. The vessel, with a listed capacity of about 100 people, was carrying a far larger number of passengers, many returning from the island's market day. At least 228 people drowned in the disaster, with hundreds of others rescued; officials later arrested ferry crew members over safety violations.

retained.title: MV Nyerere ferry capsizing
retained.description: The overloaded ferry MV Nyerere capsized while approaching Ukara Island on Lake Victoria on September 20, 2018. Later government figures put the death toll at 228, with 41 people rescued. It had been travelling from Ukerewe Island.

review.note: Ferry was approaching Ukara, not just departing Ukerewe. 41 survivors, not hundreds; 228 is the later government tally summarized by secondary source, while September 24 AFP still reported 224. The later 228 toll was not corroborated beyond a secondary summary in this batch; the opened contemporary AFP source still had 224. Route/survivor corrections do not establish a final death tally.

original.title: Sulawesi earthquake and tsunami
original.description: A magnitude 7.5 earthquake struck the Indonesian island of Sulawesi, triggering a tsunami up to six meters high that hit Palu Bay, along with widespread soil liquefaction that swallowed entire neighborhoods. The disaster destroyed tens of thousands of buildings in Palu, Donggala, and Sigi and displaced over 200,000 people. Indonesia's disaster agency (BNPB) confirmed 4,340 deaths, more than 10,000 injured, and hundreds missing.

review.note: Date, magnitude and disaster identity supported. Need reconcile 4,340 with recovered bodies, missing and people presumed buried; calling all confirmed deaths while also listing missing risks category mixing. BNPB page returned 403 on open. Tsunami-height maximum and displacement total also require final source.

original.title: Cyclone Idai
original.description: Cyclone Idai made landfall near the port city of Beira in central Mozambique on the night of 14-15 March 2019, bringing torrential rains and winds of up to 175 km/h that caused the Buzi and Pungwe rivers to burst their banks. More than 1,500 people died across Mozambique, Zimbabwe, Malawi and Madagascar, with the toll later confirmed at 1,593, and more than 2,000 people were reported missing. Hundreds of thousands were left stranded in floodwater, and the United Nations called it one of the worst weather-related disasters to hit the Southern Hemisphere.

sources.name: International Journal of Disaster Risk Science

original.title: Battle for Tripoli (Western Libya offensive)
original.description: On 4 April 2019, forces of the Libyan National Army under Khalifa Haftar launched an offensive to capture Tripoli from the UN-backed Government of National Accord, setting off nearly 14 months of fighting in the capital's southern suburbs. By the end of 2019 the United Nations reported that more than 1,000 people had been killed and about 146,000 displaced, with civilian infrastructure including hospitals and residential areas hit by airstrikes and shelling. The campaign continued into 2020, when a ceasefire and UN-brokered political talks brought a halt to the offensive.

review.note: 1,000 is an interim toll. The offensive ended through military withdrawal in June, before the later ceasefire; final death count remains unresolved.

original.title: Sri Lanka Easter bombings
original.description: On Easter Sunday, 21 April 2019, a series of coordinated suicide bombings struck three churches and three luxury hotels in Colombo, Negombo and Batticaloa, with two further explosions occurring later in the day. A total of 269 people were killed, including dozens of foreign nationals, and more than 500 were injured, making it the deadliest act of violence in Sri Lanka since the end of the civil war. The Islamic State claimed responsibility, and investigations focused on the local group National Thowheeth Jama'ath and its links to international militant networks.

Need primary/reputable final total and confirmation of all location/injury/attribution details; do not substitute the preliminary 359 or 250-260.

original.title: Idlib offensive (Syria)
original.description: On 30 April 2019, the Syrian government, backed by Russian air power, launched a ground offensive against opposition-held areas of Idlib Governorate, the last major rebel stronghold. Between April and August, the Syrian Observatory for Human Rights recorded at least 1,043 civilian deaths and roughly 3,000 combatant deaths, while the United Nations reported more than 500 civilians killed in the first months and hundreds of thousands of people displaced, including repeated attacks on schools, hospitals and camps for displaced people.

review.note: Search supports campaign identity and reports 1,043 civilians in secondary coverage. Need the underlying SOHR final interval and combatant total, UN source for 500 deaths, and distinction between April air campaign and subsequent ground offensive. Not verified from secondary summaries.

original.title: Khartoum massacre
original.description: On 3 June 2019, Sudanese security forces, including the Rapid Support Forces, violently dispersed a civilian sit-in outside the army headquarters in Khartoum that had been demanding a transition to civilian rule. The Sudanese Doctors' Syndicate documented at least 104 deaths, with later tallies exceeding 128 including children, and hundreds of people wounded; an official inquiry reported 87 deaths. The crackdown followed the ouster of President Omar al-Bashir and preceded a power-sharing agreement that established a civilian-led transitional government later that year.

review.note: June 3 attack and RSF involvement supported. Original 104/128 attribution conflates organizations and reporting intervals; exact canonical tally remains unresolved.

original.title: European heat waves
original.description: Record-breaking heat waves struck western Europe in late June and late July 2019, with France registering its highest-ever temperature of 45.9°C at Gallargues-le-Montueux on 28 June. France's public health agency attributed 1,435 excess deaths to the June heat wave, and a subsequent peer-reviewed study estimated roughly 2,500 deaths across Europe attributable to the summer's heat waves. Schools closed, rail services were suspended and cities opened cooling centres as authorities issued the highest heat alerts for the first time in several countries.

retained.title: European heat waves
