review.note: Confirmed national record is 46.0 C at Verargues June 28, not 45.9 C at Gallargues. The French mortality bulletin covers both June and July heatwaves. No identifiable peer-reviewed study supporting the claimed Europe-wide 2,500 total retrieved; replacement death scope must be settled before integration.

original.title: Majiya fuel tanker explosion
original.description: In early July 2019, a fuel tanker that had overturned near the village of Majiya in Jigawa State exploded, killing at least 48 people, many of whom had gathered to collect leaking fuel, and leaving dozens more hospitalised with severe burns. Local officials said most of the dead were burnt beyond recognition and the explosion also destroyed nearby properties. The incident highlighted the recurring danger of fuel collection at tanker crash sites across Nigeria, where fuel shortages have driven people to scoop up spilled petrol.

retained.title: Majiya fuel tanker explosion

review.note: Search did not establish a July 2019 Majiya explosion killing 48. Primary investigation notice and AFP locate the major Majiya disaster on October 15, 2024 with much higher deaths. Likely conflation, but failed search alone is not proof of fabrication. Quarantine pending identity/date resolution; do not silently repurpose as 2024.

original.title: India monsoon floods
original.description: The 2019 southwest monsoon caused severe and prolonged flooding across much of India between June and October, with more than 1,600 people killed in rain-related incidents according to reports citing official data. Bihar was among the hardest-hit states, along with Maharashtra, Kerala, Karnataka and Assam, and heavy flooding in the south coincided with torrential rain in Maharashtra's coastal districts. More than a million people were displaced, crops were destroyed and the floods followed unusually heavy August rainfall that came within weeks of drought in parts of the country.

original.title: Hurricane Dorian
original.location: Abaco Islands and Grand Bahama, Bahamas
original.description: Hurricane Dorian, a Category 5 storm with sustained winds of 185 mph, devastated the northern Bahamas when it made landfall on 1 September 2019, stalling over the Abaco Islands and Grand Bahama for more than a day. The storm killed 84 people across all affected areas, including 74 in the Bahamas, where hundreds of people were initially reported missing and whole settlements were flattened by the storm surge. It was the strongest hurricane on record to hit the Bahamas and caused tens of thousands of people to be displaced or left homeless.

original.title: Typhoon Hagibis
original.description: Typhoon Hagibis, one of the most powerful typhoons to strike Japan in decades, made landfall on the Izu Peninsula near Tokyo on 12 October 2019, bringing record rainfall that caused more than 70 rivers to overflow and widespread landslides. Around 100 people were killed, more than 350 were injured and thousands of homes were flooded, with several prefectures including Nagano, Fukushima and Miyagi among the worst affected. The storm disrupted transport, power and the 2019 Rugby World Cup, and the government described the scale of damage as unprecedented.

original.title: Mogadishu truck bombing
original.description: On 28 December 2019, a truck bomb detonated at the Ex-Control Afgoye checkpoint on the outskirts of Mogadishu, followed by another blast at a bus station in the city, killing at least 85 people and injuring more than 140. The attack hit taxis, buses and minibuses collecting passengers at the checkpoint during rush hour, and al-Shabaab claimed responsibility. It was among the deadliest attacks in Mogadishu in years and targeted a route frequented by civilians travelling between the capital and surrounding towns.

review.note: 85 appears in later secondary totals. A second bus-station blast is not established and may conflate a different bombing. Need final reputable toll and responsibility statement.

original.title: Jakarta flood disaster
original.description: Record rainfall of nearly 400 mm on New Year's Eve overflowed the Ciliwung and Cisadane rivers, flooding large parts of Jakarta and surrounding areas in the early hours of 1 January 2020. Officials reported 66 deaths, the highest toll from flooding in the city since 2007, with about 60,000 people displaced and more than 397,000 evacuated to higher ground at the peak. Water levels reached 30 to 200 cm across many districts and up to four metres in parts of East Jakarta.

No primary final 66-death tally, 60,000 residual-displacement cutoff or full water-depth/rivers support retrieved. Retain unresolved rather than selecting an arbitrary onset time.

original.title: Balyun airstrikes on Turkish troops
original.description: On 27 February 2020, during the Idlib offensive in northwestern Syria, an airstrike attributed to the Syrian and Russian air forces hit a convoy of a Turkish mechanized infantry battalion near Balyun. Turkey reported 34 soldiers killed (33-34 depending on the official source) and more than 30 wounded, making it the deadliest attack on Turkish forces in Syria. Turkey responded by launching Operation Spring Shield, which ended in a Russia-Turkey ceasefire on 5 March 2020.

original.title: Visakhapatnam LG Polymers gas leak
original.description: In the early hours of 7 May 2020, styrene gas leaked from a sealed storage tank at the LG Polymers chemical plant on the outskirts of Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh, India. The National Disaster Response Force reported 13 deaths and more than 1,000 people sickened, with about 300 hospitalized, many of them villagers and workers asleep during the nationwide COVID-19 lockdown. The leak was compared to the 1984 Bhopal gas disaster and led to arrests of company officials.

original.title: Cyclone Amphan
original.description: Cyclone Amphan, the first super cyclonic storm in the Bay of Bengal since 1999, made landfall near Bakkhali in West Bengal, India on 20 May 2020 with winds up to 260 km/h. The storm killed 133 people in total, including 103 in India (most in West Bengal) and 26 in Bangladesh, and displaced millions. Amphan severely damaged Kolkata and the Sundarbans, and its landfall during the COVID-19 pandemic complicated evacuation and relief efforts.

retained.title: Cyclone Amphan

The storm killed 133 people in total, including 103 in India (most in West Bengal) and 26 in Bangladesh, and displaced millions. Amphan severely damaged Kolkata and the Sundarbans, and its landfall during the COVID-19 pandemic complicated evacuation and relief efforts.

review.note: May 20 landfall supported. Landfall winds were 155-165 km/h, gusting 185, not 260; 260 confuses peak offshore strength with landfall. 103+26 does not sum to 133 and remaining country scope is absent. Need final reconciled toll; first Bay-of-Bengal super-cyclone-since-1999 claim also needs authoritative check.

original.title: Hurricane Laura
original.description: Hurricane Laura made landfall near Cameron, Louisiana on 27 August 2020 as a Category 4 storm with winds of 240 km/h, the strongest hurricane to hit the state since 1856. The storm killed 81 people in total across its path, including at least 41 in the United States (30 in Louisiana), 31 in Haiti and 9 in the Dominican Republic, and caused roughly $19 billion in damage. Storm surge and wind destroyed entire communities along the Gulf Coast of Louisiana and Texas.

review.note: Landfall identity and category supported; 81 is a combined direct/indirect total, not Louisiana fatalities. Need final NHC mortality table and check 'strongest since 1856' against 1856/2020 intensity equivalence.

original.title: Second Nagorno-Karabakh War
original.description: On 27 September 2020, Azerbaijan launched a large-scale military offensive against the Armenian-backed Nagorno-Karabakh (Artsakh) region, starting a 44-day war that ended with a Russian-brokered ceasefire on 10 November 2020. Official figures from both sides listed about 2,900 Azerbaijani and 3,800 Armenian soldiers killed, along with roughly 185 civilians, for a combined death toll of more than 6,900, with tens of thousands displaced. Azerbaijan regained control of territory around and within the region under the ceasefire terms.

retained.title: Second Nagorno-Karabakh War

Official counts have continued changing; latest retrieved Armenian report gives 3,833 including 3,755 military and 78 civilians. 6,900 needs matching as-of dates and inclusion policy for missing/foreign fighters, not a mixture of rounded figures. Mortality study estimates are not official named deaths.

original.title: Kabul University attack
original.description: On 2 November 2020, three gunmen from Islamic State Khorasan Province stormed Kabul University during an Iranian book fair, killing 32 people and wounding more than 50 in a siege that lasted several hours. The attackers, killed by security forces, brought the total death count including themselves to 35. The attack targeted students and academics and was one of the deadliest attacks on a university in Afghanistan's recent history.

Do not infer 32 by subtracting attackers from a source saying 35 students/professors. Iranian book-fair context and over-50 injured require corroboration.

original.title: Hurricane Eta
original.description: Hurricane Eta made landfall near Puerto Cabezas, Nicaragua on 3 November 2020 as a Category 4 hurricane, then stalled over Central America for two days, triggering catastrophic flash floods and landslides across the region. At least 189 people died, including 74 in Honduras, 60 in Guatemala and 19 in Panama, with more than 100 missing. Eta was followed within two weeks by Hurricane Iota, which compounded the destruction in Honduras and Nicaragua.

original.title: Mai Kadra massacre
original.description: On 9-10 November 2020, in the first days of the Tigray War, hundreds of Amhara civilians were killed in house-to-house raids in the town of Mai Kadra near the Sudanese border. Estimates of the death toll ranged from hundreds to more than 1,100, with a Reuters investigation confirming at least 767 deaths; Amnesty International reported that hundreds were killed, likely by local Tigrayan security forces, police and militias aligned with the TPLF. The massacre was the first documented mass atrocity of the Tigray conflict.

original.title: Typhoon Vamco (Ulysses)
original.description: Typhoon Vamco, known locally as Ulysses, made landfall in Quezon province on 11 November 2020 as the third typhoon to strike the Philippines in two weeks. The storm caused severe flooding in Metro Manila and Cagayan Valley, killing 102 people with 10 more missing, according to the Philippine disaster agency. More than a million people were displaced, and the flooding in Cagayan was described as the worst in decades.

original.title: Koshebe massacre
original.description: On 28 November 2020, gunmen believed to be Boko Haram fighters attacked farmers harvesting rice fields near the village of Koshebe in Borno State, northeastern Nigeria. The United Nations reported that as many as 110 civilians and peasant farmers were killed, six were wounded and about 15 women were kidnapped. The attack, which followed a dispute with farmers who had disarmed a Boko Haram gunman the previous day, was among the deadliest attacks on civilians in Nigeria during 2020.

original.title: Aden airport attack
original.description: On 30 December 2020, explosions and gunfire hit Aden International Airport just as a plane carrying members of Yemen's newly formed unity government, including the prime minister and the Saudi ambassador, was landing from Riyadh. The attack killed 28 people and wounded 107, though none of the cabinet passengers were hurt. A UN investigation later found the Houthi movement responsible for the attack, which came as the Saudi-brokered power-sharing government returned to the interim capital.

Early Reuters toll was 22; 28/107 later secondary tally and Saudi ambassador aboard require final evidence.

original.title: Sulawesi earthquake
original.description: A magnitude 6.2 earthquake struck near the city of Mamuju on Sulawesi island, killing at least 105 people and injuring hundreds more. The quake toppled homes, hospitals, and hotels, triggering landslides in the mountainous region. Thousands were displaced and months of aftershocks hampered rescue and recovery efforts.

retained.title: Sulawesi earthquake
retained.description: A magnitude 6.2 earthquake struck near the city of Mamuju on Sulawesi island, killing at least 105 people and injuring hundreds more. The quake toppled homes, hospitals, and hotels, triggering landslides in the mountainous region. Thousands were displaced and months of aftershocks hampered rescue and recovery efforts.

review.note: UTC origin is January 14 at 18:28, not January 15. 105 appears in secondary summaries; months of aftershocks hampering rescue is not established. Propose only supported UTC correction pending full final-toll and recovery evidence.

original.title: Myanmar military coup and crackdown
original.description: On February 1, the Myanmar military seized power in a coup, detaining elected leader Aung San Suu Kyi and triggering nationwide civil disobedience and protests. Security forces responded with lethal force, and by the end of 2021 more than 1,400 civilians had been killed and over 10,000 detained, according to monitoring groups such as the Assistance Association for Political Prisoners.

retained.title: Myanmar military coup and crackdown
retained.description: On February 1, the Myanmar military seized power in a coup, detaining elected leader Aung San Suu Kyi and triggering nationwide civil disobedience and protests. Security forces responded with lethal force, and by the end of 2021 more than 1,400 civilians had been killed and over 10,000 detained, according to monitoring groups such as the Assistance Association for Political Prisoners.

review.note: Primary December 6 briefing reports 1,303 killed and 7,796 currently detained. Year-end more-than-1,400 and over-10,000 need December 31 evidence and a distinction between all arrested and still detained. These are cumulative post-coup deaths, not February 1 deaths. Only one source was established in this batch, below the two-source publication minimum.

original.title: Chamoli glacier disaster
original.description: A portion of the Nanda Devi glacier broke off in Chamoli district, sending a massive flash flood of water, ice, and debris down the Rishiganga and Dhauliganga rivers. The flood destroyed two hydroelectric power projects and swept away workers and infrastructure, leaving roughly 200 people dead or missing, most of them power-plant employees.

retained.title: Chamoli rock and ice avalanche
retained.description: A massive rock and ice avalanche from Ronti Peak caused the Chamoli disaster in Uttarakhand on February 7, 2021. Debris swept down the Rishiganga and Dhauliganga valleys and damaged two hydropower projects. Roughly 200 people were killed or remained missing; this is a combined dead-and-missing estimate.

review.note: Scientific reconstruction identifies rock and glacier ice from Ronti Peak, not simply Nanda Devi glacier breaking off. About 200 is dead-and-missing, not 200 recovered/confirmed bodies. A combined killed-or-missing estimate cannot establish 200 deaths for the lives_lost field. Retain the supported avalanche mechanism but withhold until a death-only or legally presumed-dead count is supported.

sources.name: Natural Hazards and Earth System Sciences

original.title: Texas winter storm Uri
original.description: An unusually severe winter storm, Uri, brought record cold and snow across Texas, causing the state's power grid to fail and leaving millions without electricity, heat, or water for days during subfreezing temperatures. At least 246 people died, most from hypothermia, while carbon monoxide poisoning from generators and house fires also claimed lives.

retained.title: Texas winter-weather disaster, February 2021
retained.description: Severe winter weather and power failures left millions of Texans without essential services in February 2021. Texas health officials ultimately identified 246 storm-related deaths, including 158 from hypothermia. The total covers deaths from February 11 through June 4, including later deaths linked to the disaster, rather than deaths on February 13 alone.

review.note: 246 is the state's broad February winter-storm total, including deaths through June and multiple weather episodes; not necessarily all caused by a single storm starting February 13. 158 hypothermia deaths supported. The broader February winter-weather total is supported, but February 13 is not established as the start date of that matched scope. A specific storm-name/date cannot silently stand in for several weather episodes.

sources.name: Texas Department of State Health Services

original.title: India's second COVID-19 wave
original.description: India was overwhelmed by a second wave of COVID-19 driven by the Delta variant from April to June 2021, when hospitals, crematoria, and oxygen supplies ran out in Delhi and other cities. India officially recorded about 400,000 COVID-19 deaths during 2021, the vast majority during this wave, while independent estimates such as the World Health Organization's excess-death analysis placed the true toll far higher.

retained.title: India's second COVID-19 wave
retained.description: India was overwhelmed by a second wave of COVID-19 driven by the Delta variant from April to June 2021, when hospitals, crematoria, and oxygen supplies ran out in Delhi and other cities. India officially recorded about 400,000 COVID-19 deaths during 2021, the vast majority during this wave, while independent estimates such as the World Health Organization's excess-death analysis placed the true toll far higher.

review.note: 400,000 appears to conflate a cumulative pandemic milestone with calendar-2021 deaths and with the April-June wave. The later study estimates 2.4 million excess deaths in 2021 at 7.2 times reported COVID deaths, inconsistent with 400,000 as the annual official count. April 1 is not established as a discrete event date; do not replace reported deaths with excess mortality without changing scope.

original.title: Eleven-day Gaza conflict
original.description: An 11-day war between Israel and Hamas erupted after weeks of tension in Jerusalem, with Israeli airstrikes and Palestinian rocket fire striking densely populated areas. At least 256 Palestinians, including 66 children, and 13 people in Israel were killed. More than 100,000 Gazans were displaced before a ceasefire took effect on May 21.

retained.title: Eleven-day Gaza conflict
retained.description: An 11-day war between Israel and Hamas erupted after weeks of tension in Jerusalem, with Israeli airstrikes and Palestinian rocket fire striking densely populated areas. At least 256 Palestinians, including 66 children, and 13 people in Israel were killed. More than 100,000 Gazans were displaced before a ceasefire took effect on May 21.

review.note: 256 is Gaza-only, while record title/location and description include Israel. Same-cutoff Palestinian/Israeli totals must be reconciled before choosing a combined integer; original description's 256+13 is 269. Counts also revised after ceasefire. Start May 10 supported, not all deaths on that day.

original.title: Tigray famine
original.description: Amid the war between Ethiopian federal forces and the Tigray People's Liberation Front, the United Nations declared a famine in parts of Tigray in June 2021 as an aid blockade prevented food from reaching millions of people. Research from Ghent University estimated that 162,000 to 191,000 people died from violence and starvation-related causes in Tigray between November 2020 and June 2022, most of them during 2021.

retained.title: Tigray famine
retained.description: Amid the war between Ethiopian federal forces and the Tigray People's Liberation Front, the United Nations declared a famine in parts of Tigray in June 2021 as an aid blockade prevented food from reaching millions of people. Research from Ghent University estimated that 162,000 to 191,000 people died from violence and starvation-related causes in Tigray between November 2020 and June 2022, most of them during 2021.

review.note: IPC explicitly says evidence did not support area-level Famine classification; household Catastrophe is different. 190,000 is not a measured June 2021 famine toll. Underlying Ghent estimate, cause categories, November 2020-June 2022 interval and 'most during 2021' require original study; do not label estimate a UN-declared famine's deaths.

original.title: Pacific Northwest heat dome
original.location: Pacific Northwest, United States and Canada
original.description: An exceptional heat dome pushed temperatures to records across the Pacific Northwest, with Lytton, British Columbia, reaching 49.6°C (121.3°F), Canada's hottest temperature ever recorded. The heat is estimated to have caused about 800 deaths or more across Canada and the U.S., mostly among elderly and vulnerable people in homes without air conditioning.

retained.title: Pacific Northwest heat dome
retained.location: Pacific Northwest, United States and Canada
retained.description: An exceptional heat dome pushed temperatures to records across the Pacific Northwest, with Lytton, British Columbia, reaching 49.6°C (121.3°F), Canada's hottest temperature ever recorded. The heat is estimated to have caused about 800 deaths or more across Canada and the U.S., mostly among elderly and vulnerable people in homes without air conditioning.

review.note: June 25-July 1 period, Lytton 49.6 C on June 29 and 619 heat-related BC deaths established. More than 800 investigated BC deaths is not the same as heat-attributed deaths. Need independent US/other-Canada totals and interval to substantiate combined about-800 figure and household demographics.

original.title: Western European floods
original.description: Unprecedented rainfall caused devastating flash floods in western Germany, particularly the Ahr and Erft valleys, and eastern Belgium along the Vesdre river. Around 240 people died, roughly 189 of them in Germany, with dozens more killed in Belgium and other neighboring countries. Thousands lost homes, and scientists linked the extreme rainfall to climate change.

retained.title: Western European floods
retained.description: Unprecedented rainfall caused devastating flash floods in western Germany, particularly the Ahr and Erft valleys, and eastern Belgium along the Vesdre river. Around 240 people died, roughly 189 of them in Germany, with dozens more killed in Belgium and other neighboring countries. Thousands lost homes, and scientists linked the extreme rainfall to climate change.

review.note: July event/weather mechanisms supported. Final geographic death totals vary across updates: secondary totals reach 243 including 196 Germany, not 189. Need primary final country breakdown and attribution study before replacing broad 240 estimate.

original.title: Henan floods
original.description: Torrential rain described as a once-in-a-millennium event inundated Zhengzhou and surrounding areas of Henan province, flooding subway lines, underpasses, and neighborhoods. At least 398 people died across Henan, including 302 in Zhengzhou, where dozens drowned inside subway cars. More than one million residents were evacuated.

retained.title: Henan floods
retained.description: Torrential rains struck Henan from July 17 to 23, 2021, with severe flooding in Zhengzhou on July 20. A subsequent State Council investigation recorded 398 people dead or missing across the province, 380 of them in Zhengzhou. Fourteen people died in the subway flooding. The 398 figure is a combined dead-and-missing toll.

review.note: 398 includes dead and missing across July 17-23, 95.5% (380) in Zhengzhou. Subway deaths were 14, not dozens. 302 is an earlier provincial figure wrongly assigned to Zhengzhou. The reported combined category does not establish 398 confirmed deaths. Withhold the numeric deaths-bearing row until missing-versus-dead accounting is resolved; the July 20 Zhengzhou flooding itself is established.

original.title: Mayfield tornado outbreak
original.description: A historic tornado outbreak spawned an EF4 tornado that leveled the town of Mayfield, Kentucky, and caused damage across six states from Arkansas to Ohio during the night of December 10-11. At least 89 people were killed, most of them in Kentucky, where it was the deadliest tornado event in the state's history, with deaths also reported in Tennessee and elsewhere.

retained.title: Mayfield tornado outbreak
retained.description: A historic tornado outbreak spawned an EF4 tornado that leveled the town of Mayfield, Kentucky, and caused damage across six states from Arkansas to Ohio during the night of December 10-11. At least 89 people were killed, most of them in Kentucky, where it was the deadliest tornado event in the state's history, with deaths also reported in Tennessee and elsewhere.

review.note: NWS assessment supports 89 direct tornado deaths and 71 tornadoes across eight states, not six. 89 is entire-outbreak toll, not one Mayfield tornado. Need UTC beginning of chosen whole-outbreak scope; Mayfield's late December 10 local impact is December 11 UTC.

original.title: Horn of Africa drought and hunger crisis
original.description: Failed rainy seasons through 2022 produced the worst drought in four decades across the Horn of Africa, affecting Somalia, Ethiopia and Kenya. A joint WHO-UNICEF-FAO analysis estimated approximately 43,000 excess deaths in Somalia in 2022 alone, about half of them children under five. More than 20 million people across the region faced acute food insecurity, with famine-level hunger reported in parts of Somalia.

retained.title: Somalia drought: estimated excess deaths in 2022
retained.description: A study commissioned by WHO and UNICEF and released in March 2023 estimated approximately 43,000 excess deaths associated with Somalia's drought during January-December 2022, about half among children younger than five. January 1 marks the start of the study year, not the date these deaths occurred; the total is an estimate rather than a confirmed count.

review.note: 43,000 is modeled excess mortality in Somalia across all 2022, not a January 1 event or Horn-wide confirmed famine toll. Commissioned by WHO/UNICEF, with FAO support; no area-level famine declaration implied. January 1 is a study-year boundary, not an established discrete disaster date. The annual mortality estimate is supported, but the current calendar record needs a justified period representation before publication.

original.title: Russian Invasion of Ukraine — Start of Full-Scale War
original.description: Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine, the largest conventional military attack in Europe since World War II. Tens of thousands of civilians and soldiers have been killed, and millions displaced.

retained.title: Russian Invasion of Ukraine — Start of Full-Scale War
retained.description: Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine, the largest conventional military attack in Europe since World War II. Tens of thousands of civilians and soldiers have been killed, and millions displaced.

review.note: Full-scale invasion began February 24, not March 24. Duplicates original February 24 invasion record. 100,000 lacks date, civilian/military definition and source; possible confusion of casualties with deaths. Merge/remove decision belongs to maintainer; do not apply date correction without duplicate review.

original.title: Bucha massacre
original.description: After Russian forces withdrew from Bucha in early April 2022, Ukrainian authorities discovered mass graves and the bodies of hundreds of civilians killed during the month-long occupation of the town. Ukrainian officials recovered 458 bodies, most showing signs of shooting, torture, or other violent trauma. OHCHR documented at least 73 unlawful killings in Bucha itself and reported more than 1,300 killings across the wider Bucha district, describing the massacre as a grave violation of international law.

retained.title: Bucha massacre
retained.description: After Russian forces withdrew from Bucha in early April 2022, Ukrainian authorities discovered mass graves and the bodies of hundreds of civilians killed during the month-long occupation of the town. Ukrainian officials recovered 458 bodies, most showing signs of shooting, torture, or other violent trauma. OHCHR documented at least 73 unlawful killings in Bucha itself and reported more than 1,300 killings across the wider Bucha district, describing the massacre as a grave violation of international law.

review.note: Municipal 458 includes 39 apparently natural deaths and one bag of remains; not 458 established unlawful killings. OHCHR records 422 bodies recovered by September and 73 documented civilian killings during March 4-30. April 2 is discovery/reporting period, not killing date. Wider 1,300 appears Kyiv-region rather than town-specific and attribution needs correction; retain contradictory denominators.

original.title: KwaZulu-Natal floods
original.description: Torrential rain on 11-13 April 2022 caused catastrophic flash floods and mudslides across KwaZulu-Natal province, South Africa, devastating the city of Durban and surrounding townships. The official death toll was 435, with thousands of homes destroyed, roads and bridges washed out, and critical water and electricity infrastructure severely damaged. It was one of the deadliest natural disasters in South Africa's recorded history.

retained.title: KwaZulu-Natal floods
retained.description: Heavy rain and flooding devastated KwaZulu-Natal, including Durban, in April 2022. On May 3, the provincial government reported 435 deaths and 63 people still missing. Homes, roads, bridges and water infrastructure were extensively damaged. April 11 anchors the multi-day flooding episode.

review.note: 435 is supported as May 3 reported toll, with 63 missing, not a timeless final number. Remove unneeded historical superlative. April 11 remains an unestablished selection within the multi-day episode in the evidence reviewed; the dated May 3 mortality report does not establish that event date.

sources.name: South Africa Department of Water and Sanitation

original.title: BM Container Depot fire and explosions (Sitakunda)
original.description: A fire broke out at the BM Container Depot near Sitakunda, Bangladesh, on 4 June 2022, igniting chemicals stored in shipping containers and triggering a series of massive explosions. At least 49 people were killed and more than 450 injured, many of them firefighters and workers who had tried to contain the initial blaze. The explosions hurled containers hundreds of metres, in one of Bangladesh's deadliest industrial accidents.

retained.title: BM Container Depot fire and explosions (Sitakunda)
retained.description: A fire broke out at the BM Container Depot near Sitakunda, Bangladesh, on 4 June 2022, igniting chemicals stored in shipping containers and triggering a series of massive explosions. At least 49 people were killed and more than 450 injured, many of them firefighters and workers who had tried to contain the initial blaze. The explosions hurled containers hundreds of metres, in one of Bangladesh's deadliest industrial accidents.

review.note: June 4 fire established. Initial 49 was explicitly corrected to 41 after a miscount; later secondary sources say at least 47. Need eventual reconciled death tally rather than reinstating erroneous initial total. More-than-450 injured and explosion-distance details also not established.

original.title: Pakistan floods
original.description: From mid-June 2022, record monsoon rains and glacial melt triggered catastrophic flooding across Pakistan that submerged as much as one-third of the country at its peak. The National Disaster Management Authority reported 1,739 deaths and about 12,900 injuries, with 33 million people affected and more than 2 million homes damaged or destroyed. Among the deadliest floods in the country's history, the disaster caused damages estimated in the tens of billions of dollars and was widely linked to climate change.
sources: National Disaster Management Authority of Pakistan

retained.title: Pakistan floods
retained.description: Monsoon flooding in Pakistan beginning in June 2022 affected more than 33 million people. UNICEF's retrospective reporting records 1,739 deaths and more than 2.2 million homes damaged or destroyed across the flood-affected areas.
sources: National Disaster Management Authority of Pakistan

review.note: 1,739 is a retrospective national total, not the toll on the June start date. UNICEF repeats the one-third-underwater claim, but mapped inundation summarized in the secondary source is substantially smaller; remove this disputed extent and unverified injury/climate details rather than assert them. June 14 is the flood-period anchor, not a one-day disaster. The exact June 14 onset anchor was not corroborated beyond the secondary summary; UNICEF establishes the June-to-seasonal disaster, not this precise day.

original.title: 2022 European heatwaves
original.description: Consecutive heatwaves through summer 2022 brought record temperatures across Europe, including 40.3 degrees Celsius in the United Kingdom, 47 degrees Celsius in Portugal, and widespread wildfires from Spain to France. A peer-reviewed study by the Barcelona Institute for Global Health estimated 61,672 heat-related deaths across Europe between 30 May and 4 September 2022, a toll that a later analysis revised upward to over 70,000. Excess deaths fell most heavily on the elderly in France, Spain, Germany and Italy.
sources: Barcelona Institute for Global Health (Nature Medicine)

retained.title: 2022 European heatwaves
retained.description: A Nature Medicine study estimated 61,672 heat-related deaths across 35 European countries between May 30 and September 4, 2022, with a 95% confidence interval of 37,643-86,807. A later methodological study inferred roughly 70,066 deaths for the full year, a different time scope. These are statistical estimates, not individually confirmed deaths.
sources: Barcelona Institute for Global Health (Nature Medicine)

review.note: 61,672 is a modeled summer estimate for May 30-September 4, not a July 15 toll. The first study's annual estimate was 62,862; the later paper inferred 70,066 for the whole year, not an interchangeable revised summer count. Use the defined study-period start and omit unresearched national temperature records. May 30 is the documented study-interval start, not a verified discrete heat-disaster date. The corrected estimate and interval are supported, but the single-day calendar representation needs resolution before publication.

original.title: Nigeria floods
original.description: Heavy rains from July 2022 produced Nigeria's worst flooding in a decade, peaking in September and October after the release of water from the Lagdo Dam in Cameroon. Nigeria's National Emergency Management Agency reported more than 603 deaths and over 2,400 injuries, with at least 1.4 million people displaced. The floods destroyed more than 200,000 homes and inundated farmland across 33 of Nigeria's 36 states, worsening food insecurity.

retained.title: Nigeria floods
retained.description: Flooding across Nigeria in 2022 killed 662 people, injured 3,174 and displaced about 2.43 million, according to NEMA's director general in January 2023. These are nationwide seasonal totals, not deaths on a single September day.

review.note: NEMA's January 2023 retrospective supersedes 603: 662 deaths, 3,174 injuries and 2,430,445 displaced. September 1 is not established as onset of the season-long floods; a precise event date remains unresolved. Remove unsupported destroyed-home total and overly simple dam-release causation.

original.title: Turkey–Syria earthquake
original.description: A magnitude 7.8 earthquake struck near the Turkey–Syria border at 4:17 a.m., followed by a magnitude 7.5 aftershock hours later, collapsing thousands of buildings across southeastern Turkey and northern Syria. More than 59,000 people were confirmed dead, including about 50,700 in Turkey and over 5,900 in Syria, with an estimated 1.5 million people left homeless. It was one of the deadliest earthquakes in the region in modern history, compounded in Syria by the country's ongoing civil war.

retained.title: Turkey–Syria earthquake
retained.description: A magnitude 7.8 earthquake struck near the Turkey–Syria border at 4:17 a.m., followed by a magnitude 7.5 aftershock hours later, collapsing thousands of buildings across southeastern Turkey and northern Syria. More than 59,000 people were confirmed dead, including about 50,700 in Turkey and over 5,900 in Syria, with an estimated 1.5 million people left homeless. It was one of the deadliest earthquakes in the region in modern history, compounded in Syria by the country's ongoing civil war.

review.note: February 6 UTC is correct, but original country subtotals do not sum to 59,000. EEFIT gives 62,013 (53,537 Turkey plus 8,476 Syria); secondary compilation also records a lower Syrian count of 5,951. A defensible harmonized cross-border confirmed total and cutoff remain unresolved. Avoid selecting one exact total without reconciling Syrian coverage; 04:17 is local, 01:17 UTC.

original.title: Battle of Bakhmut
original.description: Russian forces completed their capture of the eastern Ukrainian city of Bakhmut on May 20, 2023, ending one of the bloodiest battles of the Russia–Ukraine war, which had raged for about ten months. U.S. officials estimated that roughly 20,000 Russian soldiers had been killed in the battle, with tens of thousands more wounded, and Ukrainian officials reported thousands of their own soldiers killed; the city was reduced to ruins. Independent verification of exact casualties was not possible due to the secrecy of the warring sides.
sources: Institute for the Study of War

retained.title: Battle of Bakhmut
retained.description: Russian forces completed their capture of the eastern Ukrainian city of Bakhmut on May 20, 2023, ending one of the bloodiest battles of the Russia–Ukraine war, which had raged for about ten months. U.S. officials estimated that roughly 20,000 Russian soldiers had been killed in the battle, with tens of thousands more wounded, and Ukrainian officials reported thousands of their own soldiers killed; the city was reduced to ruins. sources: Institute for the Study of War

review.note: The Post corrected its report: the U.S. estimate covered Russian losses across Ukraine, not Bakhmut alone. Battle-specific fatalities and the claimed thousands of Ukrainian deaths remain unverified. May 20 was a Russian capture claim disputed by Ukraine; do not present it as an uncontested end date. A reliable replacement battle toll is unavailable.

original.title: Noto Peninsula Earthquake
original.description: A magnitude 7.6 earthquake struck the Noto Peninsula in Ishikawa Prefecture, Japan, on January 1, 2024, triggering tsunami warnings, building collapses, and a major fire in Wajima. The disaster killed 241 people, injured more than 1,300, and destroyed or damaged tens of thousands of homes, with Wajima and Suzu among the hardest-hit towns.

retained.title: Noto Peninsula Earthquake
retained.description: A magnitude 7.6 earthquake struck the Noto Peninsula in Ishikawa Prefecture, Japan, on January 1, 2024, triggering tsunami warnings, building collapses, and a major fire in Wajima. The disaster killed 241 people, injured more than 1,300, and destroyed or damaged tens of thousands of homes, with Wajima and Suzu among the hardest-hit towns.

review.note: January 1 and magnitude 7.6 JMA are established, but 241 is an early 2024 snapshot, not the final toll. An indexed August 14, 2026 Kyodo report gives 750 across affected prefectures: 228 direct plus 522 related deaths; its full page failed to open. Need the current official table and explicit national/prefectural and direct/indirect scope before replacing the toll. Withhold rather than silently freeze an obsolete count.

sources.name: International Journal of Disaster Risk Reduction

original.title: Kerman Bombings (Soleimani Memorial Attack)
original.description: On January 3, 2024, two explosions struck a crowd gathered in Kerman, Iran, for a ceremony commemorating the fourth anniversary of the assassination of General Qasem Soleimani. Islamic State (ISIS) claimed responsibility for the attack, which killed at least 95 people and wounded about 280, making it one of the deadliest attacks in Iran's modern history.

retained.title: Kerman Bombings (Soleimani Memorial Attack)
retained.description: On January 3, 2024, two explosions struck a crowd gathered in Kerman, Iran, for a ceremony commemorating the fourth anniversary of the assassination of General Qasem Soleimani. Islamic State (ISIS) claimed responsibility for the attack, which killed at least 95 people and wounded about 280, making it one of the deadliest attacks in Iran's modern history.

review.note: Date and memorial identity are established. Early 103/95 counts were corrected to 84, then 94 by January 11; a definitive subsequent 95-person count was not established. ISIS claim is supported, but final toll requires reconciliation. The Al Jazeera evidence is used only for the later figure and claim.

original.title: Kenya Floods and Landslides
original.description: Torrential rains and flash floods in Kenya from mid-March through May 2024, driven by an unusually heavy long-rains season, caused rivers to overflow, dams to breach, and landslides to bury communities, including in the capital Nairobi. At least 291 people were killed, hundreds were reported missing, and more than 280,000 were displaced, prompting the government to declare the floods a national disaster.
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs

retained.title: Kenya Floods and Landslides
retained.description: Heavy seasonal rains caused floods and landslides across Kenya in 2024. UNICEF's June 24 snapshot recorded 315 deaths, 38 missing people, 188 injuries and 293,205 displaced people nationwide. These are cumulative seasonal figures, not the toll of one day in Nairobi.
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs

review.note: June 24 national snapshot supports 315 dead, 38 missing, 188 injured and 293,205 displaced, not 291 deaths or hundreds missing. April 26 is not established as onset of this March-June seasonal event. No supported exact replacement day; withhold pending date resolution. National-disaster declaration and dam-breach claims omitted.

original.title: Rio Grande do Sul Floods
original.location: Porto Alegre, Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil
original.description: Record rainfall from late April 2024 triggered catastrophic flooding in Brazil's southern state of Rio Grande do Sul, overwhelming Porto Alegre and hundreds of municipalities. The floods killed at least 183 people, with dozens more reported missing, displaced more than 580,000, and destroyed or damaged thousands of homes, businesses, and roads.

retained.title: Rio Grande do Sul Floods
retained.description: Heavy rain in late April and May 2024 caused widespread flooding in Rio Grande do Sul, including Porto Alegre. Brazil's Senate reported 183 deaths, 806 injuries and 27 missing people in its December 2024 review, with 478 municipalities affected.

review.note: 183 deaths, 806 injuries and 27 missing are supported retrospectively. May 1 is an emergency-declaration date, not established flood onset. IFRC dates intense rains from April 29; other accounts start April 27. Preserve this onset ambiguity rather than declare a placeholder verified. Proposed prose removes unneeded displacement precision.

sources.name: Rio Grande do Sul Civil Defense

original.title: Baghlan Flash Floods

United Nations agencies reported at least 315 people killed and more than 1,600 injured, with tens of thousands of homes destroyed or damaged and several thousand people displaced.
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs

retained.title: Baghlan Flash Floods
retained.description: On May 10, 2024, heavy seasonal rainfall caused flash floods that swept through villages in northern Afghanistan, most severely in Baghlan Province. United Nations agencies reported at least 315 people killed and more than 1,600 injured, with tens of thousands of homes destroyed or damaged and several thousand people displaced.

UNICEF's May report gives preliminary 180 deaths/280 injuries across May 10-11 northeastern flooding; WHO gives over 180/242. Counts and geographic scopes conflict. Tens of thousands of homes is unsupported; RFE/RL cites 2,660 destroyed. Need reconciled Baghlan-specific total.

original.title: Sudan Famine and Humanitarian Crisis
original.description: In August 2024, the Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC) confirmed famine conditions in Zamzam displacement camp near El Fasher, North Darfur — the first famine declaration anywhere in the world since 2011 — amid the civil war between the Sudanese Armed Forces and the Rapid Support Forces. Independent monitors recorded more than 61,000 people killed in the conflict since April 2023, humanitarian agencies reported child malnutrition deaths in the camp, and the UN said more than 25 million people across Sudan were facing acute food insecurity.

retained.title: Sudan Famine and Humanitarian Crisis
retained.description: In August 2024, the Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC) confirmed famine conditions in Zamzam displacement camp near El Fasher, North Darfur — the first famine declaration anywhere in the world since 2011 — amid the civil war between the Sudanese Armed Forces and the Rapid Support Forces. Independent monitors recorded more than 61,000 people killed in the conflict since April 2023, humanitarian agencies reported child malnutrition deaths in the camp, and the UN said more than 25 million people across Sudan were facing acute food insecurity.

review.note: August 1 is publication of the Zamzam famine determination, not onset of famine mortality. 61,000 is estimated all-cause mortality in Khartoum State over April 2023-June 2024, not recorded killings nationwide or famine deaths in Zamzam. First famine since 2011 is false (South Sudan 2017); a famine-specific death total is not established. Do not repurpose the unrelated mortality estimate.

sources.name: United Nations - South Sudan famine declaration

original.title: Super Typhoon Yagi
original.description: Super Typhoon Yagi, the most powerful storm of the 2024 season, made landfall in northern Vietnam on September 7, 2024, after causing destruction in the Philippines and southern China, and spawned flooding and landslides across Vietnam, Laos, Thailand, and Myanmar. The storm and its aftermath killed at least 844 people across the region, more than 320 of them in Vietnam, with hundreds more missing in Myanmar.
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs

retained.title: Super Typhoon Yagi
retained.description: Super Typhoon Yagi, the most powerful storm of the 2024 season, made landfall in northern Vietnam on September 7, 2024, after causing destruction in the Philippines and southern China, and spawned flooding and landslides across Vietnam, Laos, Thailand, and Myanmar. The storm and its aftermath killed at least 844 people across the region, more than 320 of them in Vietnam, with hundreds more missing in Myanmar.

review.note: 844 appears in Global Water Monitor but a secondary compilation ranges to 1,009; national accounting and Myanmar missing/dead reconciliation remain incomplete. September 7 is Vietnam landfall, not onset of multinational impacts. Most powerful storm of the 2024 season is not supported by HKO, which gives a narrower South China Sea ranking. Withhold pending geographic/time-scope alignment.

original.title: Bamako Attack
original.description: On September 17, 2024, jihadist attackers from Jama'at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin (JNIM) stormed a military police school and the military airport in Bamako, Mali, in a coordinated assault. The attack killed at least 77 people, including civilians, and wounded more than 250, making it one of the deadliest attacks in Mali in years and prompting heightened security measures in the capital.

retained.title: Bamako Attack
retained.description: On September 17, 2024, jihadist attackers from Jama'at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin (JNIM) stormed a military police school and the military airport in Bamako, Mali, in a coordinated assault. The attack killed at least 77 people, including civilians, and wounded more than 250, making it one of the deadliest attacks in Mali in years and prompting heightened security measures in the capital.

review.note: Date, JNIM and targets supported. AFP simultaneously reported 77 from a security source and an authenticated official document naming 81 victims and suggesting around 100. The 77 figure cannot be presented as a settled final count; civilian inclusion and exact injured total also need reconciliation.

original.title: Israel–Hamas War: 2024 Death Toll in Gaza
original.description: During 2024, the Israel–Hamas war in the Gaza Strip continued with intense Israeli military operations and armed resistance, with the Gaza Ministry of Health reporting more than 45,600 Palestinians killed since October 2023 — roughly 25,000 of them during 2024 — while most of the territory's 2.1 million residents were repeatedly displaced and UN agencies warned of famine conditions and disease outbreaks. The conflict also involved continued rocket fire into Israel and expanding regional confrontation with Hezbollah and Iran.
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs

retained.title: Israel–Hamas War: 2024 Death Toll in Gaza
retained.description: During 2024, the Israel–Hamas war in the Gaza Strip continued with intense Israeli military operations and armed resistance, with the Gaza Ministry of Health reporting more than 45,600 Palestinians killed since October 2023 — roughly 25,000 of them during 2024 — while most of the territory's 2.1 million residents were repeatedly displaced and UN agencies warned of famine conditions and disease outbreaks. The conflict also involved continued rocket fire into Israel and expanding regional confrontation with Hezbollah and Iran.
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs

review.note: December 31 OCHA publication uses Gaza MoH data through December 30: 45,541 cumulative since October 7, 2023, not 45,600 deaths during 2024. Simple difference from the 21,822 end-2023 snapshot is 23,719 but changes to cumulative reporting are not necessarily deaths occurring within the year. Need actual occurrence-year accounting or explicitly repurpose to a cumulative snapshot, avoiding double counting record 113. Annual toll remains unresolved.

original.title: Russia–Ukraine War: 2024 Casualties
original.description: The Russia–Ukraine war entered its third year in 2024, with Russian offensives in eastern Ukraine, a Ukrainian incursion into Russia's Kursk region, and relentless artillery and drone strikes on cities including Kharkiv, Kyiv, and Odesa. Independent media documented more than 78,000 named Russian soldiers killed by December 2024 and estimated total military deaths on both sides at more than 100,000 during the year — making 2024 the war's deadliest — while the UN recorded about 1,300 civilian deaths in Ukraine in 2024 and more than 12,000 civilians killed since the February 2022 invasion.

retained.title: Russia–Ukraine War: 2024 Casualties
retained.description: The Russia–Ukraine war entered its third year in 2024, with Russian offensives in eastern Ukraine, a Ukrainian incursion into Russia's Kursk region, and relentless artillery and drone strikes on cities including Kharkiv, Kyiv, and Odesa. Independent media documented more than 78,000 named Russian soldiers killed by December 2024 and estimated total military deaths on both sides at more than 100,000 during the year — making 2024 the war's deadliest — while the UN recorded about 1,300 civilian deaths in Ukraine in 2024 and more than 12,000 civilians killed since the February 2022 invasion.

review.note: UN initially documented 2,064 civilian deaths in 2024, later revised to 2,088, not about 1,300. Named Russian deaths are cumulative verified identifications, not all-side annual deaths. The exact 100,000 annual combined military total and deadliest-year assertion are not established; dynamic Mediazona data cannot be backdated to December 2024. December 31 is a reporting-period endpoint, not a one-day battle date.

original.title: Gaza war ceasefire
original.description: A ceasefire between Israel and Hamas took effect on January 19, 2025, after 15 months of war in which the Gaza Health Ministry reported more than 47,000 Palestinians killed and most of the territory's population displaced. The first phase of the agreement included releases of hostages and prisoners before hostilities later resumed.

retained.title: Gaza war ceasefire
retained.description: A ceasefire between Israel and Hamas took effect on January 19, 2025, after 15 months of war in which the Gaza Health Ministry reported more than 47,000 Palestinians killed and most of the territory's population displaced. The first phase of the agreement included releases of hostages and prisoners before hostilities later resumed.

review.note: OCHA establishes that the ceasefire took effect January 19 at 11:15 local time, not its January 22 publication date, and reports hostage/prisoner releases. The 47,000 is a cumulative war toll, not deaths caused by a ceasefire; an exact matching January 19 cutoff is not established here. This overlaps the existing 2023 and 2024 Gaza death records. A later cumulative report cannot verify the number on the ceasefire date. Do not publish a deaths-bearing ceasefire row until its toll scope and duplicate treatment are resolved.

original.title: M23 capture of Goma
original.location: Goma, Democratic Republic of the Congo
original.description: Between January 23 and 30, 2025, Rwandan-backed M23 rebels captured Goma, the capital of North Kivu province in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, after heavy fighting against the national army, UN and SADC peacekeepers, and allied militias; the UN estimated about 2,900 people were killed and another 2,900 wounded, with hundreds of thousands displaced.

retained.title: M23 capture of Goma
retained.location: Goma, Democratic Republic of the Congo
retained.description: Between January 23 and 30, 2025, Rwandan-backed M23 rebels captured Goma, the capital of North Kivu province in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, after heavy fighting against the national army, UN and SADC peacekeepers, and allied militias; the UN estimated about 2,900 people were killed and another 2,900 wounded, with hundreds of thousands displaced.

review.note: The February 5 UN briefing, reproduced by ANSA, supports a provisional 2,900 dead: 2,000 bodies collected from streets and 900 in morgues. This is not a final January 23-30-only total. UNICEF describes January 26-28 fighting and control of most of Goma by January 28; the January 27 UN briefing describes an ongoing battle, while the later experts' annex calls January 27 full conquest. The same report also cites narrower health-facility fatality/injury counts. The exact capture-date framing and matching casualty period remain unsettled; do not silently resolve them with publication dates.

original.title: Sudan famine confirmed in North Darfur camps
original.description: In February 2025, the United Nations confirmed famine conditions in at least five areas of Sudan, including the Zamzam, Abu Shouk and Al Salam displacement camps in North Darfur and two locations in the Western Nuba Mountains. The Sudan Doctors Union estimated in January 2025 that about 522,000 children had died from malnutrition since the civil war began, amid widespread aid access restrictions imposed by the warring parties.

retained.title: Sudan famine confirmed in North Darfur camps
retained.description: On December 24, 2024, FAO, WFP and UNICEF reported the IPC Famine Review Committee's finding of famine in at least five assessed areas, including three North Darfur displacement camps and resident and displaced populations in the Western Nuba Mountains. The assessment covered October-November 2024 and projected further spread.

review.note: The five-area finding was announced December 24, 2024 and assessed October-November conditions, with projections through May 2025. February 19 is not established as a new confirmation. Western Nuba coverage refers to residents and displaced people, not necessarily two named physical sites. A photographer's caption repeats 522,000 child malnutrition deaths attributed to the Sudan Doctors Union, but no underlying estimate, methods or authoritative corroboration was found. IPC people-in-Catastrophe figures are not deaths. The Sudan government also disputed the IPC process; its disagreement does not negate the independent famine classification. Retain in audit, not public canonical data.

original.title: Myanmar earthquake (magnitude 7.7)
original.description: On March 28, 2025, a magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck near Sagaing and Mandalay in Myanmar along the Sagaing Fault, collapsing buildings and infrastructure and also killing 18 people in Bangkok, Thailand. Myanmar's military government reported about 3,770 dead, while independent Myanmar media estimates exceeded 5,000, and the true toll was widely considered higher.

retained.title: Myanmar earthquake (magnitude 7.7)
retained.description: On March 28, 2025, a magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck near Sagaing and Mandalay in Myanmar along the Sagaing Fault, collapsing buildings and infrastructure and also killing 18 people in Bangkok, Thailand. Myanmar's military government reported about 3,770 dead, while independent Myanmar media estimates exceeded 5,000, and the true toll was widely considered higher.

review.note: The March 28 M7.7 earthquake is well supported, but 3,770 is not a final reconciled death count. Myanmar's government reported 3,782 as of August 20, 2025 for six affected regions/states; UNICEF's May 2 report used 3,835 from another reporting stream. Independent Myanmar-media estimates were substantially higher, and the Thai 18-death figure is an early snapshot (ADRC already reports 83 Thailand deaths in its May 7 snapshot). National, cross-border and independent counts need a consistent cutoff and scope. Do not equate the government count with the true whole-event toll or retain 18 as a final Thai total.

original.title: Afghanistan flash floods
original.description: In late April 2025, heavy rains triggered flash floods across northern Afghanistan, with the worst destruction in Baghlan Province, where entire villages were swept away; at least 150 people were killed across the affected provinces per BBC reporting, while the World Food Programme estimated more than 300 dead and hundreds more injured.

retained.title: Afghanistan flash floods
retained.description: In late April 2025, heavy rains triggered flash floods across northern Afghanistan, with the worst destruction in Baghlan Province, where entire villages were swept away; at least 150 people were killed across the affected provinces per BBC reporting, while the World Food Programme estimated more than 300 dead and hundreds more injured.

review.note: Searches did not establish an April 27, 2025 Baghlan flood with these fatalities. The 150 official/300-plus WFP reporting pattern instead matches the May 10, 2024 northern Afghanistan floods, confirmed by contemporaneous May 2024 UN and news reports. The assigned data already has a May 2024 Baghlan event. This suggests a misdated duplicate, not proof that no flooding occurred in 2025. Do not automatically move this row to May 2024 or count both; identity, date and casualty scope require reconciliation.

original.title: Israel-Iran war (Twelve-Day War)
original.description: On June 13, 2025, Israel launched Operation Rising Lion, striking Iranian military and nuclear facilities and killing commanders and nuclear scientists; Iran responded with more than 550 ballistic missiles and over 1,000 drones fired at Israel over 12 days. Roughly 33 people were killed in Israel and about 1,060 in Iran, according to the respective authorities.

retained.title: Israel-Iran war (Twelve-Day War)
retained.description: On June 13, 2025, Israel launched Operation Rising Lion, striking Iranian military and nuclear facilities and killing commanders and nuclear scientists; Iran responded with more than 550 ballistic missiles and over 1,000 drones fired at Israel over 12 days. Roughly 33 people were killed in Israel and about 1,060 in Iran, according to the respective authorities.

review.note: June 13-24 is supported, but 1,093 is not a reconciled total. The original roughly 1,060 in Iran is a July 7 official update; the spokesperson raised it to at least 1,062 on July 22. HRANA reported 1,190 using a separate casualty register. Reuters reports 28 killed in Israel, not the original 33; inclusion of indirect or later deaths is not established for the latter. Do not average competing counts or treat different reporting dates as final same-scope totals. The 550-plus missile claim is supported by AP, but the drone count was not established here. Withhold until the overall numeric toll and scope are resolved.

original.title: Rubaya coltan mine collapse
original.location: Rubaya, North Kivu, Democratic Republic of the Congo
original.description: On 28 January 2026, a landslide at the informal coltan mines in Rubaya, North Kivu, killed more than 400 miners and diggers, with some reports placing the toll higher. The collapse occurred amid a surge of artisanal mining in the conflict-affected region, and a second collapse at the same mines on 3 March 2026 killed at least 200 more people.

retained.title: Rubaya coltan mine collapse
retained.location: Rubaya, North Kivu, Democratic Republic of the Congo
retained.description: Heavy rain caused a landslide and mine collapses at the Rubaya coltan mining complex in North Kivu on 28 January 2026. Rebel-appointed authorities reported at least 200 deaths. A civil-society representative subsequently estimated roughly 400 deaths; that higher figure remained provisional and was not limited to miners.

review.note: The roughly 400 figure is a provisional civil-society estimate, not a confirmed count of miners alone; AP reported at least 200. March 3 is supported by Reuters (published March 4), but that separate collapse has a disputed toll and should not be folded into January's deaths. Exact January onset time unavailable. The numeric field still reflects a provisional estimate; a confirmed comparable toll and January UTC onset remain unresolved.

original.title: Balochistan Liberation Army attacks
original.description: Between 29 January and 5 February 2026, the Balochistan Liberation Army launched a coordinated series of attacks across Balochistan province, Pakistan, including raids on a police station and banks in Kharan, a security post in Panjgur and military positions in Harnai. The week-long campaign left at least 225 people dead, including 36 civilians and 2 security personnel, while Pakistani forces reported killing 216 militants in retaliatory raids.

retained.title: Balochistan Liberation Army attacks
retained.description: Between 29 January and 5 February 2026, the Balochistan Liberation Army launched a coordinated series of attacks across Balochistan province, Pakistan, including raids on a police station and banks in Kharan, a security post in Panjgur and military positions in Harnai. The week-long campaign left at least 225 people dead, including 36 civilians and 2 security personnel, while Pakistani forces reported killing 216 militants in retaliatory raids.

review.note: January 29 is the military operation's beginning, not the coordinated BLA assault (January 31). The reported components are 216 militants, 36 civilians and 22 security personnel = 274, not 225; all are military-reported, not independently confirmed. The original identity key is retained for audit only. The proposed scope is a multi-day campaign, not a proven single-day BLA attack. Its start date must not be presented as the date of all 274 deaths; assault versus military-operation allocation remains unresolved.

original.title: Gamo Zone floods and landslides
original.description: On 10 March 2026, days of heavy rainfall in the Gamo Zone of South Ethiopia triggered widespread flash floods and landslides that killed at least 125 people. The disaster struck farming communities in the southern highlands, destroying homes, roads and farmland across multiple villages.

retained.title: Gamo Zone floods and landslides

The disaster struck farming communities in the southern highlands, destroying homes, roads and farmland across multiple villages.

review.note: 125 deaths supported; sources date the sequence March 9-10, March 10, or early March 11. Exact UTC onset and road/farmland damage remain unresolved.

original.title: Jilli market airstrike
original.description: On 11 April 2026, a Nigerian military airstrike hit a crowded market in Jilli, Yobe State, killing more than 100 civilians; authorities described the strike as a misfire. It was one of the deadliest airstrike incidents in Nigeria's counterinsurgency campaign in 2026 and drew calls for independent investigations into civilian casualties.

retained.title: Jilli market airstrike
retained.description: A Nigerian airstrike hit Jilli market near the Borno-Yobe border on 11 April 2026. Amnesty International reported at least 100 civilians killed, citing survivors and medical contacts. Other estimates were higher. The military said it had targeted militants; accounts of the strike and the casualty total remained disputed.

review.note: April 11 event, April 12 publication. 100 is a rights-group toll, not official final count. Military defended the operation; exact UTC onset unavailable. A single verified UTC onset and reconciliation of the competing casualty accounts remain unavailable; the attributed minimum is not a confirmed final total.

original.title: Mindanao earthquake
original.description: On 8 June 2026, a magnitude 7.8 earthquake struck offshore Sarangani province, Mindanao, on the Cotabato Trench, killing at least 106 people (107 per final tallies) and injuring 1,320, with 7 missing. More than 121,000 homes were damaged or destroyed and damage exceeded ₱71 billion (US$1.44 billion). General Santos, Sarangani, South Cotabato and Davao Occidental were hardest hit, and coastal uplift of up to 2 metres damaged marine habitats across Sarangani Bay.

review.note: 07:37 local June 8 = 23:37 UTC June 7. Date-only correction; final 107 deaths, injuries/missing, housing totals, PHP 71bn loss and uplift claims remain unverified.

original.title: Militant drone-and-ambush attack on police checkpoint in Hangu
original.description: Militants, blamed by police on the Pakistani Taliban (TTP), launched a drone strike and ambush on the Khazina Banda police checkpoint in Hangu district on the evening of July 29, 2026, in an assault that also involved an attack on a neighbouring checkpost. Eleven police officers, including a deputy superintendent of police, were killed as the death toll rose through the following morning, with initial reports citing 9 to 10 officers dead and at least 28 injured; authorities said 15 attackers were also killed in the ensuing gunfight. It was the second major assault on security forces in the area within a week amid escalating attacks in the Afghanistan–Pakistan border region.

review.note: July 29 and 11 police dead supported; attackers killed differ (AP 15, ARY eight). Drone detail, prior assault comparison and precise UTC onset not established.

original.title: US–Saudi airstrikes kill 20 Iran-backed militiamen in Iraq as US strikes on Iran resume
original.description: As part of the 2026 Iran war, US Central Command and Saudi forces carried out joint strikes on positions of Iran-backed militias in Iraq on July 29, 2026, killing 20 Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) militants, including several Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) members, according to the PMF. The same day, after a six-day pause, the US military resumed heavy waves of strikes against dozens of IRGC targets inside Iran in retaliation for an attempted missile attack on US forces in the Middle East a day earlier, an escalation that prompted Iranian retaliatory strikes on Kuwait days later.
sources: Wikipedia: July 2026 United States strikes against Iran

review.note: PMF reported 20 members killed. IRGC advisers may be additional. Overnight July 28-29 requires UTC check; resumed Iran strikes and causal link to Kuwait not fully established.

original.title: Russia launches massive missile and drone strike on Ukraine
original.location: Kyiv, Lviv and Kryvyi Rih, Ukraine
original.description: In the early hours of July 30, 2026, Russia launched one of its largest combined strikes of the war, firing dozens of ballistic and cruise missiles and hundreds of drones (President Zelensky cited over 70 missiles and 280 drones) at cities across Ukraine, with damage reported from east to west in Kyiv, Lviv and Kryvyi Rih. At least 10 civilians, including children, were killed and more than 50 injured, including six people killed by a ballistic missile strike on Kryvyi Rih and a family of six killed in a village hit by a suspected North Korean missile; NATO scrambled jets in response and a stray Russian cruise missile briefly entered Polish airspace.

At least 10 civilians, including children, were killed and more than 50 injured, including six people killed by a ballistic missile strike on Kryvyi Rih and a family of six killed in a village hit by a suspected North Korean missile; NATO scrambled jets in response and a stray Russian cruise missile briefly entered Polish airspace.

review.note: 70 missiles/280 drones supported; Reuters nine deaths, EFE earlier eight, versus record ten. Family and Kryvyi Rih totals may overlap. Polish incursion and UTC onset not confirmed.

original.title: Coal mine explosion in Balochistan
original.description: A methane gas explosion ripped through a coal mine in Balochistan province on 30 July, killing at least 34 miners. Rescue officials recovered 32 bodies and said two workers remained trapped in an inaccessible section of the mine.

retained.title: Coal mine explosion in Balochistan
retained.description: A methane gas explosion ripped through a coal mine in Balochistan province on 30 July, killing at least 34 miners. Rescue officials recovered 32 bodies and said two workers remained trapped in an inaccessible section of the mine.

review.note: AP reports 34 dead, 32 recovered and two to retrieve. July 30 occurrence versus July 31 publication distinguished. Exact time unavailable but no evidence of UTC crossover. Absence of evidence of a crossover does not establish the UTC date; withhold pending an onset time or sufficiently specific time-of-day account.

original.title: IRGC claims retaliatory strike on US base in Kuwait amid Iran war
original.description: On July 31, 2026, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed it had targeted a US base in Kuwait in retaliation for American strikes on Iran, after an earlier Iranian attack on a building in Kuwait housing a Chinese company had killed one person the previous day. The strikes were part of the sharp escalation of the 2026 Iran war following the resumption of US bombardment of IRGC targets in Iran on July 29; no further casualty figures for the Kuwait attack had been released at the time of reporting.

retained.title: Iranian strike on Chinese company building in Kuwait kills worker
retained.description: Kuwait's Defence Ministry said an Iranian attack hit a building belonging to a Chinese company in northern Kuwait on 30 July 2026, killing one worker and causing substantial damage.

review.note: Fatality belongs to July 30 company-building strike, not July 31 base claim; exact clock time unavailable. The proposed July 30 is the reported local occurrence date; UTC conversion remains unverified.

original.title: Russian ballistic missile attack on Kyiv
original.description: Russian forces launched a ballistic missile attack on Kyiv shortly after midnight on 1 August local time, killing at least nine people and injuring more than 20, including children. Fires broke out across four districts and rescue operations continued through the night.

retained.title: Russian ballistic missile attack on Kyiv
retained.description: Russian forces launched a ballistic missile attack on Kyiv shortly after midnight on 1 August local time, killing at least nine people and injuring more than 20, including children. Fires broke out across four districts and rescue operations continued through the night.

review.note: Nine dead and 33 injured supported for overnight July 31-August 1. Exact onset for UTC conversion not established. Appears duplicate of 'Russian missile barrage on Kyiv kills ten' dated August 1; reconcile and retain only one incident.

original.title: Calabar flood and landslide crisis
original.description: Weeks of torrential rain in July 2026 caused flooding and landslides across Calabar, killing at least 10 people, including a baby swept away by floodwater and a father buried in mud. The rains destroyed homes, triggered landslides that killed families, and cut off access roads; the toll was cumulative through the end of July.

The rains destroyed homes, triggered landslides that killed families, and cut off access roads; the toll was cumulative through the end of July.

review.note: Ten is a month-long total published August 1, not deaths on July 31. Primary report supports flooding/landslides but no dated ten-person tally. A defensible onset anchor and overlap with individual incidents remain unresolved.

original.title: Apartment building fire kills four in Changsha
original.description: A fire broke out at 03:54 local time on 1 August at a high-rise residential building in the Poly Lugu Linyu compound, Yuelu District, Changsha, killing four people and injuring two. Firefighters rescued six people from the building, but four later died of their injuries in hospital.

retained.title: Apartment building fire kills four in Changsha

review.note: Fire service statement reproduced by Xinhua gives 03:54 August 1 local = 19:54 July 31 UTC; six rescued, four died by August 2, two receiving treatment. All material claims match. Only one retrieved publication/source chain; a second independent link is still needed before canonical source replacement. Publication withheld: only one usable evidence document retrieved; a second corroborating source is required.

original.title: Plane crash near Nazca kills 13
original.description: A small plane crashed in farmland about 6 km from the city of Nazca in Peru's southern Ica region on Saturday, killing all 13 on board — 11 tourists plus the pilot and co-pilot. Local media reported that seven Italians, two Germans and two Spaniards were among the dead; the flight was on a tour route over the Nazca Lines.

retained.title: Plane crash near Nazca kills 13

original.title: Shooting at In-N-Out restaurant in Twin Falls
original.description: A gunman opened fire in the area of an In-N-Out restaurant in Twin Falls, Idaho, shortly before 2:30 p.m. local time on Saturday, killing at least three people and wounding two. Officials said the gunman was no longer considered a threat, and the investigation remained active.

retained.title: Shooting at In-N-Out restaurant in Twin Falls
retained.description: A shooting near an In-N-Out restaurant in Twin Falls on the afternoon of 1 August 2026 left three people dead and seven injured, according to the city's public update. Police said the immediate threat had ended and the investigation was continuing.

review.note: City and local public radio update injuries to seven. 14:30 MDT is 20:30 UTC August 1. Retrieved accounts vary over whether three deaths include gunman; retain reported three without claiming three homicide victims. Resolve victim/perpetrator breakdown separately. Publication is withheld until the victim/perpetrator scope of the total is reconciled.

original.title: Assam flood death toll reaches 82
original.description: The death toll in ongoing monsoon floods in India's northeastern state of Assam rose to 82 on Saturday, with two people still missing. Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma said the floods hit 2,251 villages and affected more than 1.1 million people; Sivasagar district reported the highest toll with 42 deaths, followed by Charaideo with 21 and Jorhat with 9.

retained.title: Assam flood death toll reaches 82
retained.description: Assam's disaster authority reported a cumulative monsoon-flood death toll of 82 by late 31 July 2026. Reports published the next morning said roughly 193,000 people in five districts remained affected. This is a season-to-date toll, not deaths on one day.

review.note: 82 was announced late Friday July 31, reported Saturday August 1. It is season-to-date, not daily deaths. Current affected population was about 193000; 1.1m may refer to another snapshot. District death breakdown not corroborated. The proposed July 31 is a reporting snapshot, not a verified onset. Its Assam component overlaps the India-wide monsoon tally; publication requires a defensible non-overlapping episode boundary.

original.title: Russian missile barrage on Kyiv kills ten
original.description: In a heavy ballistic missile attack early on Saturday, Russia struck Kyiv and the surrounding region, killing 10 people and wounding more than 30. It was the second major attack on the capital that week; President Volodymyr Zelensky said Ukraine had run out of Patriot interceptor missiles.

It was the second major attack on the capital that week; President Volodymyr Zelensky said Ukraine had run out of Patriot interceptor missiles.

review.note: Likely duplicate of July 31 'Russian ballistic missile attack on Kyiv'. Sources report nine, not ten, in the overnight July 31-August 1 attack; ten may be borrowed from July 30 nationwide strikes. Merge after establishing onset; do not sum both records.

original.title: Suicide bombing at anti-militant rally kills 14 in Swat
original.description: A suicide bomber targeted protesters gathered outside a police station in Kabal, Swat, on Sunday, killing at least 14 people — including eight police officers — and wounding more than two dozen others, officials said. original.title: Ukraine strikes deep inside Russia kill eight
