retained.title: Ukraine strikes deep inside Russia kill eight
retained.description: Large-scale Ukrainian drone strikes on targets deep inside Russia on Sunday killed at least eight people, including at logistics warehouses of retailer Wildberries in the Moscow region. Russia said it shot down 635 UAVs overnight, and the acting governor of the border Belgorod region reported four dead in strikes on civilian areas.

review.note: DW supports eight nationwide but lists Udmurtia and Belgorod, and depicts Wildberries in Samara, not Moscow. AP's next-day account reports nine. Location composition, 635 interceptions, Belgorod four and UTC coverage require reconciliation.

original.title: Israeli fire kills 19 Palestinians in Gaza
original.description: At least 19 Palestinians were killed by Israeli fire over 24 hours, including 18 killed by Israeli forces and one who died of wounds from an earlier attack, according to the Gaza Health Ministry. The deaths brought the number of Palestinians killed since the ceasefire to more than 1,250.

retained.title: Israeli fire kills 19 Palestinians in Gaza
retained.description: At least 19 Palestinians were killed by Israeli fire over 24 hours, including 18 killed by Israeli forces and one who died of wounds from an earlier attack, according to the Gaza Health Ministry. The deaths brought the number of Palestinians killed since the ceasefire to more than 1,250.

review.note: Ministry's August 3 release supports 18 newly killed plus one previous-wound death, not 19 deaths necessarily occurring August 3. Likely overlaps August 2 entry's 18. Cannot count both totals independently; exact rolling-window cutoff and unique victims unresolved.

original.title: Landslide kills 14 at Ethiopian monastery
original.description: Heavy rainfall triggered a landslide that buried worshippers gathered at Tsadqane Debre Mitmaq St. Mary Monastery in Amhara's North Shewa Zone, killing 14 people and injuring at least seven, with an unknown number still missing as search and rescue efforts continued.

retained.title: Landslide kills 14 at Ethiopian monastery
retained.description: Heavy rainfall triggered a landslide that buried worshippers gathered at Tsadqane Debre Mitmaq St. Mary Monastery in Amhara's North Shewa Zone, killing 14 people and injuring at least seven, with an unknown number still missing as search and rescue efforts continued.

review.note: AP's full report supports date, monastery, region, rain, 14 deaths, seven injuries and people unaccounted for. 07:00 local = 04:00 UTC August 3. One retrieved source chain; obtain second independent URL before replacing canonical sources. Publication withheld: only one usable evidence document retrieved; a second corroborating source is required.

original.title: Ukrainian drone strike on Moscow region kills five
original.description: A Ukrainian drone strike on an industrial zone in Novoselki near Chekhov, outside Moscow, started fires at an industrial site and killed five people, wounding at least six others, Moscow Region Governor Andrei Vorobyov said. The attack was part of an escalation of long-range drone strikes exchanged between Russia and Ukraine.

retained.title: Ukrainian drone strike on Moscow region kills five
retained.description: A Ukrainian drone strike on an industrial zone in Novoselki near Chekhov, outside Moscow, started fires at an industrial site and killed five people, wounding at least six others, Moscow Region Governor Andrei Vorobyov said. The attack was part of an escalation of long-range drone strikes exchanged between Russia and Ukraine.

review.note: Governor's five dead/six injured and Novoselki/Chekhov supported. Overnight onset not precise enough to establish August 3 versus 4 UTC; sources share governor statement rather than independent casualty confirmation.

original.title: Serviceman kills four in shooting near Sevastopol
original.description: A Russian serviceman opened fire on fellow soldiers and civilians in the village of Khmelnitskoye near Sevastopol, killing four people - one soldier and three civilians aged 59, 64 and 71 - and wounding four others before being detained, Sevastopol Governor Mikhail Razvozhayev said.

retained.title: Serviceman kills four in shooting near Sevastopol
retained.description: A Russian serviceman opened fire on fellow soldiers and civilians in the village of Khmelnitskoye near Sevastopol, killing four people - one soldier and three civilians aged 59, 64 and 71 - and wounding four others before being detained, Sevastopol Governor Mikhail Razvozhayev said.

review.note: Four dead (one soldier/three civilians), four injured and detention supported. AP explicitly says governor did not specify when it happened: August 4 is report date, not proven occurrence date. Victim ages not established.

original.title: CRPF officer shooting in Assam kills four
original.description: A CRPF officer shot two colleagues dead and seriously wounded another at the 34th Battalion camp in Katimari, Nagaon, before killing himself; the wounded personnel member later died in hospital, bringing the death toll to four, police said.

retained.title: CRPF officer shooting in Assam kills four
retained.description: A CRPF officer shot two colleagues dead and seriously wounded another at the 34th Battalion camp in Katimari, Nagaon, before killing himself; the wounded personnel member later died in hospital, bringing the death toll to four, police said.

review.note: Two colleagues and perpetrator dead, one injured supported; August 12 follow-up still describes three. No support located for injured colleague's later death. Morning August 4 may require exact clock for UTC boundary. Any rewrite must use 'died by suicide' without method.

original.title: Russian drone strike on Mykolaiv kills elderly woman
original.description: Russian drones attacked the southern port city of Mykolaiv overnight, killing an 89-year-old woman and injuring seven people, including two children. Two private houses were destroyed and several other buildings were damaged.

retained.title: Russian drone strike on Mykolaiv kills elderly woman
retained.description: Russian drones attacked the southern port city of Mykolaiv overnight, killing an 89-year-old woman and injuring seven people, including two children. Two private houses were destroyed and several other buildings were damaged.

review.note: Victim age, seven injured including two children, and two destroyed homes supported. Night of August 3-4 not precise enough for UTC day; do not use publication date as onset.

original.title: Israeli fire kills two in Gaza
original.description: Two more Palestinians were killed by Israeli fire in Gaza over 24 hours, with ten others injured, according to the Gaza Health Ministry, bringing the death toll since October 7, 2023 to 73,377. Some victims remained trapped under rubble beyond the reach of rescue crews.

retained.title: Israeli fire kills two in Gaza
retained.description: Two more Palestinians were killed by Israeli fire in Gaza over 24 hours, with ten others injured, according to the Gaza Health Ministry, bringing the death toll since October 7, 2023 to 73,377. Some victims remained trapped under rubble beyond the reach of rescue crews.

review.note: August 4 is bulletin date; two newly reported deaths may include the August 3 vehicle strike. Cumulative 73377 corroborated, but exact death dates/unique victims and full injury/rubble claims not established.

original.title: Russian missile strikes on Kyiv kill two
original.description: Russia attacked Kyiv with waves of ballistic missiles and drones after midnight, killing at least 21 people - three in the capital and 18 in the surrounding region - and injuring more than 45. The assault used 24 ballistic missiles, four Zircon/Onyx missiles and 115 drones, hitting warehouses, a railway station and other civilian infrastructure; air defences intercepted 98 drones.

retained.title: Russian missile strikes on Kyiv kill two
retained.description: Russia attacked Kyiv with waves of ballistic missiles and drones after midnight, killing at least 21 people - three in the capital and 18 in the surrounding region - and injuring more than 45. The assault used 24 ballistic missiles, four Zircon/Onyx missiles and 115 drones, hitting warehouses, a railway station and other civilian infrastructure; air defences intercepted 98 drones.

review.note: Core attack/missile counts supported; sources give 17 combined and later two city deaths, not record 21 with 3+18. Title/number mismatch. Onset after midnight August 5 local implies potentially August 4 UTC; precise onset and final combined toll unresolved.

original.title: Israeli fire kills four in Gaza
original.description: Israel killed four more Palestinians in Gaza over 24 hours, bringing the war's death toll to 73,381, the Gaza Health Ministry said. Since the ceasefire took effect in October 2025, Israeli violations have killed 1,254 Palestinians and injured 4,121.

retained.title: Israeli fire kills four in Gaza
retained.description: Israel killed four more Palestinians in Gaza over 24 hours, bringing the war's death toll to 73,381, the Gaza Health Ministry said. Since the ceasefire took effect in October 2025, Israeli violations have killed 1,254 Palestinians and injured 4,121.

review.note: All quoted ministry totals supported as an August 5 reporting snapshot, but rolling 24h fatalities cannot all be dated August 5. Unique victims and overlap with incident-level entries not established.

original.title: Sri Lanka floods and mudslides kill seven
original.description: Torrential rains triggered floods and mudslides across Sri Lanka's central highlands, killing at least eight people - six in Nuwara Eliya, one in Kandy and one in Puttalam - and affecting more than 16,000 people, with nearly 11,000 evacuated. Authorities closed schools in the affected areas.

retained.title: Sri Lanka floods and mudslides kill seven
retained.description: Torrential rains triggered floods and mudslides across Sri Lanka's central highlands, killing at least eight people - six in Nuwara Eliya, one in Kandy and one in Puttalam - and affecting more than 16,000 people, with nearly 11,000 evacuated. Authorities closed schools in the affected areas.

review.note: Disaster began before August 5; eight already reported August 4, later nine by August 25. Eight/seven title mismatch. Geographic and time windows differ; exact onset/toll scope and 11000 evacuated unresolved. Do not treat cumulative impacts as August 5 deaths.

original.title: India monsoon floods and landslides kill more than 100 since July
original.description: An official tally released on August 5 showed that floods and landslides triggered by monsoon rains had killed at least 133 people across India since the beginning of July: 87 in Assam (47 in Sivasagar district alone), 31 in Jammu and Kashmir, and 15 in Kerala, with seven people still missing and more than 10,000 in relief camps.

retained.title: India monsoon floods and landslides kill more than 100 since July
retained.description: An official tally released on August 5 showed that floods and landslides triggered by monsoon rains had killed at least 133 people across India since the beginning of July: 87 in Assam (47 in Sivasagar district alone), 31 in Jammu and Kashmir, and 15 in Kerala, with seven people still missing and more than 10,000 in relief camps.

review.note: AFP supports 133 since early July, including 87 in Assam. August 5 is release date, not event date. Assam portion overlaps the 82-death Assam record. Must choose non-overlapping disaster scopes and establish onset; do not add both full tolls.

original.title: Russian strike on grain ship in Odesa region kills one
original.description: Russian forces attacked a merchant dry cargo ship flying the flag of Guinea-Bissau and loaded with Ukrainian wheat, damaging the hull and starting a fire. One Ukrainian sailor was killed and three crew members were injured; the crew was evacuated to shore.

retained.title: Russian strike on grain ship in Odesa region kills one
retained.description: Russian forces attacked a merchant dry cargo ship flying the flag of Guinea-Bissau and loaded with Ukrainian wheat, damaging the hull and starting a fire. One Ukrainian sailor was killed and three crew members were injured; the crew was evacuated to shore.

review.note: Mera Queen, flag, wheat, one killed/three injured supported. Odesa report dates strike evening August 5; trade publication uses August 6. Preserve conflict rather than treating report date as proof. Exact UTC date requires primary confirmation.

original.title: Mudslide buries household in Zhashui County, Shaanxi
original.description: A sudden mudslide triggered by days of heavy rainfall buried members of a household in Xingping township, Zhashui County, while they were clearing water near their home on August 5. One person was confirmed dead and two remained missing; continuous rain from July 30 to August 5 reached 321.4 mm in the county.

retained.title: Mudslide buries household in Zhashui County, Shaanxi
retained.description: A sudden mudslide triggered by days of heavy rainfall buried members of a household in Xingping township, Zhashui County, while they were clearing water near their home on August 5. One person was confirmed dead and two remained missing; continuous rain from July 30 to August 5 reached 321.4 mm in the county.

review.note: Xinhua's August 6 dispatch quotes the county flood-control headquarters: the household was buried August 5, with one confirmed dead and two missing. It also supports the July 30-August 5 maximum rainfall figure. Missing people are not included in lives_lost. Publication withheld: only one usable evidence document retrieved; a second corroborating source is required.

original.title: Russian drone attacks across Ukraine kill six
original.description: At least six people were killed in Russian drone attacks on Thursday: three in Balakliia in the Kharkiv region and three in residential areas of the Sumy region, with dozens injured across the affected regions, including 13 in Sumy city after a series of guided bombs. Six more people were injured in the Kherson region when a drone struck a van.

retained.title: Russian strikes kill six in Balakliia and Sumy region
retained.description: Ukrainian authorities reported three people killed in overnight strikes on homes in Balakliia and three in attacks in Sumy region. Reuters reported at least 19 wounded in Sumy-region settlements, another 12 in Sumy city, and six in a drone attack on a van in Kherson region.

review.note: Reuters supports six deaths, three each in Balakliia and Sumy region, but says overnight without times to determine August 5 versus 6 UTC. Sumy city's guided-bomb attack injured 12, not 13; not all attacks are established as drones. Compare the separate Lozova entry to avoid combining separate attacks.

original.title: Israeli airstrike on Beit Lahia kills one
original.description: One Palestinian died of wounds from an earlier attack and five others were injured over 24 hours, according to the Gaza Health Ministry, bringing the death toll since October 7, 2023 to 73,382.

retained.title: Gaza hospitals report one death from earlier wounds
retained.description: An August 6 medical bulletin reported one Palestinian who died of earlier wounds and five injured people received by Gaza hospitals during the preceding 24 hours. It reported a cumulative death toll of 73,382 since October 2023.

review.note: August 6 is the bulletin date, not a proven death or attack date. The report says one person died of earlier wounds during a rolling 24-hour period; it does not identify Beit Lahia or a new airstrike. Cumulative 73,382 and five wounded are supported. Exact death time and incident linkage remain unresolved.

original.title: Storm deaths in the Philippines reach at least 27
original.description: Heavy rains from tropical depressions Luis and Maymay and the enhanced southwest monsoon killed at least 27 people across the Philippines, with 17 injured and one missing, according to the Office of Civil Defense on August 19. About 5.39 million people were affected across Luzon and Mindanao, with nearly 2,000 homes damaged and 461 evacuation centers housing about 42,000 people. Landslides and flooding were widespread, including 10 killed in Baguio City when a rain-drenched mountainside collapsed on three houses.

retained.title: Storm deaths in the Philippines reach at least 27
retained.description: Heavy rains from tropical depressions Luis and Maymay and the enhanced southwest monsoon killed at least 27 people across the Philippines, with 17 injured and one missing, according to the Office of Civil Defense on August 19. About 5.39 million people were affected across Luzon and Mindanao, with nearly 2,000 homes damaged and 461 evacuation centers housing about 42,000 people. Landslides and flooding were widespread, including 10 killed in Baguio City when a rain-drenched mountainside collapsed on three houses.

review.note: The record is a nationwide cumulative storm series, not a discrete Northern Luzon event on August 6. Official reporting begins July 30; the August 20 OCD figure rose to 29 reported deaths, while later reports add other storms and cannot be substituted without matching scope. Reported versus validated counts also differ. Includes potential overlap with August 9 Baguio and Batangas records; do not add all three totals. Resolve episode boundary and validated toll before replacement.

original.title: Russian drone and missile attack on Kyiv region kills three, including child
original.description: Russia attacked Kyiv and the surrounding region overnight on August 8, killing three people, including a child, in strikes on the Brovary district east of Kyiv. Three more people were injured, including another child, and the attack damaged a residential building, cars and outbuildings.

retained.title: Russian drone strike kills three in Brovary district
retained.description: A Russian drone strike destroyed a family home in Brovary district, killing a three-year-old child and his grandparents. Three other family members and a neighbor were hospitalized.

review.note: Three deaths are supported for Brovary, while the wider Kyiv/capital-region total later became four. Do not substitute the wider toll into this narrower record. Later police reporting has four injured, not three. The overnight attack needs a time to distinguish August 7 from 8 UTC.

original.title: IS-linked militants kill at least 13 in eastern Congo village attack
original.location: Banana École, Mambasa, Ituri, DR Congo
original.description: Militants affiliated with the Islamic State group attacked the village of Banana École, a suburb of the territorial capital of Mambasa in eastern DR Congo near the border with Uganda, early Saturday, killing at least 13 people and burning and looting homes, a local civil society group said.

retained.title: IS-linked militants kill at least 13 in eastern Congo village attack
retained.location: Banana École, Mambasa, Ituri, DR Congo
retained.description: An attack attributed to ADF militants killed at least 13 civilians in Banana Ecole, Mambasa territory, Ituri. Local reporting described homes and vehicles burned and villagers abducted. Reports disagree whether the attack occurred August 7 or 8.

review.note: Both sources support at least 13 killed and attribution to ADF/IS-linked militants. AP reports Saturday, whereas the local report explicitly says Friday August 7 around 19:00 local (17:00 UTC). This is not merely a publication-date difference that can be silently resolved. Omit the imprecise Uganda-border characterization.

original.title: Explosive drone attack on police substation kills officer in northern Colombia
original.description: A non-commissioned police officer died after a drone loaded with explosives attacked the San Roque police substation in Curumaní, Cesar department, on the first day of President Abelardo de la Espriella's term. The attack came alongside a separate explosion that damaged the Mondomo tollgate on the Pan-American Highway in Cauca, injuring two guards.

retained.title: Explosive drone attack on police substation kills officer in northern Colombia
retained.description: Explosives dropped from drones struck the San Roque police substation in Curumani, Cesar, killing one officer and wounding another. Local reporting places the attack on the night of August 7.

review.note: Local follow-up dates the attack to the night of August 7; without an hour, August 7 versus 8 UTC remains unresolved. One officer killed and another wounded are supported. Remove unrelated tollgate and presidential-term detail rather than treating those as evidence of this incident's date.

original.title: Ukrainian drone strikes kill five in Russia's Belgorod region
original.description: Ukrainian drone strikes on Sunday killed five people and injured two dozen others, including a 4-year-old boy, in Russia's border region of Belgorod, according to the regional administration. The strikes damaged apartment blocks, private houses and administrative buildings.

retained.title: Ukrainian drone attack on Belgorod kills six
retained.description: Russian authorities reported six people killed in a drone attack on Belgorod during the night of 8-9 August 2026. The toll increased after another body was recovered from an apartment building. Russia attributed the attack to Ukraine.

review.note: The death toll rose from three to five and then six. Interfax's August 9 evening report attributes the sixth death to recovery of another man's body from the damaged apartment building, citing the regional operational headquarters. This is an update to the same overnight August 8-9 attack, not an additional incident. Exact fatal-strike timing remains insufficient to select August 8 versus 9 UTC; publication remains withheld.

original.title: Israeli strikes kill three Palestinians in Gaza
original.description: Israeli strikes across the Gaza Strip killed three Palestinians and wounded nine others on August 9, targeting civilian neighborhoods, displacement camps and areas previously designated as safe, amid ongoing violations of the ceasefire agreement. Gaza's Health Ministry put the cumulative death toll at 73,386.

retained.title: Israeli strikes kill three Palestinians in Gaza
retained.description: Israeli strikes across the Gaza Strip killed three Palestinians and wounded nine others on August 9, targeting civilian neighborhoods, displacement camps and areas previously designated as safe, amid ongoing violations of the ceasefire agreement. Gaza's Health Ministry put the cumulative death toll at 73,386.

review.note: The August 9 WAFA bulletin reports two deaths received in 24 hours, including one from earlier wounds, not three new strike deaths on that date. It supports cumulative 73,386. The cited same-day gunfire report describes three injuries, not deaths. Incident-specific support for three killed, nine wounded, and the asserted target locations was not established; do not infer those from cumulative totals.

original.title: Habagat floods and landslides kill three in Batangas, Philippines
original.description: Widespread flooding and multiple landslides triggered by the southwest monsoon (habagat) killed three people and left one fisherman missing in Batangas province. One victim, 69-year-old construction worker Teodoro Latumbo, died when a landslide buried his barracks in Barangay Calumala, Santa Teresita, late Saturday night.

retained.title: Habagat floods and landslides kill three in Batangas, Philippines
retained.description: Widespread flooding and multiple landslides triggered by the southwest monsoon (habagat) killed three people and left one fisherman missing in Batangas province. One victim, 69-year-old construction worker Teodoro Latumbo, died when a landslide buried his barracks in Barangay Calumala, Santa Teresita, late Saturday night.

review.note: ABS-CBN supports a provincial total of three reported August 9, but its accessible page lacks the narrative needed to date each death. Manila Bulletin places Latumbo's death Saturday night August 8, not August 9. Full three-death chronology remains unresolved. These deaths potentially overlap the nationwide Luis/Maymay/monsoon cumulative record. The provincial/nationwide casualty overlap remains unresolved.

original.title: Houthi strikes on Mokha kill at least seven in Yemen
original.description: Houthi ballistic missile and drone attacks on the western port city of Mokha on Sunday killed at least seven people - three civilians and four military personnel, according to medical sources - and wounded about 15 others, some critically. The Houthis launched a fresh round of strikes hours later.

retained.title: Houthi strikes on Mokha kill at least seven in Yemen
retained.description: Houthi ballistic missile and drone attacks on the western port city of Mokha on Sunday killed at least seven people - three civilians and four military personnel, according to medical sources - and wounded about 15 others, some critically. The Houthis launched a fresh round of strikes hours later.

review.note: August 9 attack is supported, but later accounts conflict: Reuters quotes the military's seven deaths/30 injured; Anadolu has seven/35; AFP via South24 reports eleven (three civilians, eight military)/32. The record's seven/15 is preliminary and may omit later attack waves. Establish whether the intended scope is the first strike or all Sunday attacks before selecting a replacement toll.

original.title: Ukrainian drone attack on Nizhnekamsk kills 13
original.description: A large-scale Ukrainian drone attack on industrial and civilian targets in the Russian city of Nizhnekamsk in Tatarstan killed at least 13 people, including a child, and injured 39 others, authorities said. It was one of the deadliest Ukrainian strikes inside Russia in the war.

retained.title: Ukrainian drone attack on Nizhnekamsk kills 13
retained.description: A Ukrainian drone attack struck Nizhnekamsk on the morning of August 10. Russian authorities reported 13 deaths and 78 injuries. Ukraine said it targeted an oil refinery in the city.

review.note: Later AP reporting gives 13 killed and 78 injured, superseding 39 injured. Remove the ranking and unsupported child detail from the replacement. Russian officials reported casualties; Ukraine said it targeted a refinery, so do not independently assert intentional civilian targeting. Other retrieved reporting describes the night leading into August 10. No sufficiently precise fatal-strike time was established to distinguish August 9 from 10 UTC; withhold despite the supported toll update.

original.title: Ukrainian drone hits Donetsk gas station, killing truck driver
original.description: A Ukrainian drone attack on a gas station complex in the Proletarsky district of Donetsk killed a 45-year-old truck driver and wounded a station employee, according to Denis Pushilin, head of the Donetsk People's Republic.

retained.title: Russian-installed official reports fatal drone strike on Donetsk fuel station
retained.description: Denis Pushilin, the Russian-installed head of occupied Donetsk, said a Ukrainian drone struck a fuel station in the city's Proletarsky district on August 10, killing a 45-year-old truck driver and wounding an employee.

review.note: The report supports the August 10 claim, 45-year-old truck driver killed and station employee wounded, but derives entirely from the Russian-installed official. No independent confirmation was located. Describe it as his allegation rather than presenting responsibility as independently established. Publication withheld: only one usable evidence document retrieved; a second corroborating source is required.

original.title: Russian strikes on Dnipropetrovsk region kill five
original.description: Russian forces carried out massive strikes on the Dnipropetrovsk region on the evening of August 10 and during the night of August 11, killing five people — including three minors — and injuring seven others, according to Ukraine's Prosecutor General's Office. Regional authorities earlier reported three dead, including a 15-year-old boy, and five injured, with drone and artillery attacks hitting five districts and damaging logistics facilities.

retained.title: Russian strikes on Dnipropetrovsk region kill five
retained.description: Russian forces carried out massive strikes on the Dnipropetrovsk region on the evening of August 10 and during the night of August 11, killing five people — including three minors — and injuring seven others, according to Ukraine's Prosecutor General's Office. Regional authorities earlier reported three dead, including a 15-year-old boy, and five injured, with drone and artillery attacks hitting five districts and damaging logistics facilities.

review.note: Primary police report lists four killed across August 10-11, one aged 15, and eight wounded including three children. Prosecutor reporting places the boy's death on the evening of August 10 and two other minors among injured, not dead. AP initially reported three deaths. The record's five dead/three minors is not established, and the aggregate's UTC period is unresolved.

original.title: Ukrainian drone attack on Voronezh region kills one
original.description: A Ukrainian drone attack on the Voronezh region killed a 49-year-old man who was struck by falling UAV debris in the Novousmansky district and died in hospital, and wounded two other people, according to Governor Alexander Gusev. The attack was part of an overnight wave in which Russian air defenses reported intercepting 396 Ukrainian drones, and it sparked fires at two warehouse facilities near Voronezh.

retained.title: Ukrainian drone attack on Voronezh region kills one
retained.description: Voronezh governor Alexander Gusev reported one person killed and two injured in an overnight drone attack, with falling debris setting warehouse facilities on fire. His statement was reported August 11.

review.note: Reuters supports one death, two injuries and warehouse fires according to the governor. It describes an overnight attack without enough timing to choose August 10 versus 11 UTC. The victim's precise age/district and national 396-drone total were not established from retrieved evidence; use a narrower description once the date is resolved.

original.title: Houthi missile strike on cargo ship Tihama in Bab el-Mandeb kills six
original.description: A Houthi missile strike on the commercial vessel Tihama in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait killed six people and injured 10 others, Yemen's coast guard said. Officials described a 'double-tap' attack that set the cargo ship ablaze; among the dead were crew members from Pakistan and Indonesia.

retained.title: Houthi missile strike on cargo ship Tihama in Bab el-Mandeb kills six
retained.description: Yemen's coastguard reported six people killed, including two rescuers, and ten injured in successive missile strikes on the cargo vessel Tihamah in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait on August 11. Later Indonesian reporting still listed one crewman among the missing, leaving a discrepancy with the initial nationality breakdown.

review.note: August 11 attack and Yemeni coastguard's six reported deaths/ten injuries are corroborated, including two rescuers. However, August 14 Indonesian foreign-ministry reporting still classifies its crewman as missing, whereas earlier reports count him dead. Do not silently resolve that discrepancy or label all six confirmed. A later reconciliation is needed for the confirmed-death total. Ship flag also varies between reports, so omit it.

original.title: Man kills wife and four children in Winfield, Kansas murder-suicide
original.description: A 53-year-old man, Ronald H. Williams Sr., shot and killed his wife, 44-year-old Kelly George, and their four children aged 3 to 9 before taking his own life early Tuesday morning, August 11, in Winfield, Kansas. Williams called 911 after the shootings, and police found the six bodies inside the home.

retained.title: Man kills wife and four children in Winfield, Kansas murder-suicide
retained.description: Police found Ronald H. Williams Sr., 53, Kelly George, 44, and four children aged three to nine dead in a Winfield home on August 11. Williams had called 911 around 8:50 a.m. saying he had killed his family and intended to kill himself. Police investigated the deaths as a murder-suicide.

review.note: Police identify six dead and an 08:50 local 911 call on August 11, also that UTC date. Retrieved reporting establishes the family deaths but not marriage/parentage for every child; omit those ancillary assertions and the imprecise 'early' qualifier. Total includes the suspected perpetrator. Publication withheld: only one usable evidence document retrieved; a second corroborating source is required.

original.title: Flash floods in Adré kill three
original.description: Heavy rains in the afternoon triggered flash floods in several neighborhoods of Adré, a town in the Assoungha department of Ouaddaï Province in eastern Chad, killing three people; local media reported five people were swept away by the water.

retained.title: Flash floods in Adré kill three
retained.description: Heavy rains in the afternoon triggered flash floods in several neighborhoods of Adré, a town in the Assoungha department of Ouaddaï Province in eastern Chad, killing three people; local media reported five people were swept away by the water.

review.note: The local August 12 report explicitly dates the rain and flooding to the afternoon of August 11 and supports the town/department/province. Witness accounts describe five swept away, three dead and two rescued; do not treat all five as deaths. Publication withheld: only one usable evidence document retrieved; a second corroborating source is required.

original.title: Russian drone strikes on Kherson kill two
original.description: Russian strike drones killed two people in Kherson overnight on August 12, including a woman struck inside her home, and wounded others in the Tsentralnyi district, according to regional authorities and military administration head Oleksandr Prokudin.

retained.title: Russian drone strikes on Kherson kill two
retained.description: Russian strike drones killed two people in Kherson overnight on August 12, including a woman struck inside her home, and wounded others in the Tsentralnyi district, according to regional authorities and military administration head Oleksandr Prokudin.

review.note: The overnight attack killed two, including a woman inside her home, and injured two in Tsentralnyi district. Available reporting does not give the strike time needed to choose August 11 or 12 UTC. A separately reported August 12 afternoon fatal strike must not be silently merged.

original.title: Russian strikes on Zaporizhzhia region kill one
original.description: Russia carried out more than 1,000 strikes on Zaporizhzhia and the surrounding region over the day, killing one person and wounding at least eight, regional governor Ivan Fedorov said. An overnight drone attack destroyed the Epicentr shopping center in the city, sparking a large fire and power outages, and damaged residential buildings.

retained.title: Russian strikes on Zaporizhzhia region kill one
retained.description: Russia carried out more than 1,000 strikes on Zaporizhzhia and the surrounding region over the day, killing one person and wounding at least eight, regional governor Ivan Fedorov said. An overnight drone attack destroyed the Epicentr shopping center in the city, sparking a large fire and power outages, and damaged residential buildings.

review.note: The 1,000-plus strikes and one death refer to August 11, reported August 12, with nine wounded. The Epicentr attack is a separate overnight event. The record conflates a daily casualty aggregate with the shopping-center strike; the fatal incident time/identity must be resolved before assigning a single UTC date.

original.title: Ukrainian drone attack on Novorossiysk kills three
original.description: A massive Ukrainian drone attack on the Russian Black Sea port of Novorossiysk killed three people — including an eight-year-old child — and injured about 24, damaging roughly 60 residential buildings and forcing major grain terminals in the city to halt operations, according to Krasnodar governor Veniamin Kondratyev. Russia said air defenses shot down 502 Ukrainian drones overnight, and Ukraine said the operation targeted the Novorossiysk naval base with drones, missiles and unmanned naval systems.

retained.title: Ukrainian attacks on Krasnodar region kill three
retained.description: Governor Veniamin Kondratyev reported three deaths, including an eight-year-old child, and 24 injuries in overnight attacks across Krasnodar region. Novorossiysk's port infrastructure and grain terminals were also damaged.

review.note: Three deaths/24 injuries apply to Krasnodar region, not solely Novorossiysk; the child is specifically linked to the city. Overnight timing leaves August 11/12 UTC unresolved. The supported scope correction below avoids attributing all regional casualties to the port.

original.title: Ukrainian attacks on Belgorod region kill two civilians
original.description: Ukrainian forces attacked Russia's Belgorod region more than 170 times over 24 hours, killing two civilians in the Belgorodsky and Graivoronsky districts and injuring three others, acting Governor Alexander Shuvayev said. RIA Novosti later reported three dead and seven people seeking medical help.

retained.title: Ukrainian attacks on Belgorod region kill two civilians
retained.description: Ukrainian forces attacked Russia's Belgorod region more than 170 times over 24 hours, killing two civilians in the Belgorodsky and Graivoronsky districts and injuring three others, acting Governor Alexander Shuvayev said. RIA Novosti later reported three dead and seven people seeking medical help.

review.note: TASS establishes a past-24-hour bulletin on August 12 with two killed and three wounded, not two deaths necessarily occurring August 12 UTC. The record itself juxtaposes a later three-death report without establishing whether it updates the same incidents. Resolve individual victims and reporting interval before choosing a toll/date.

original.title: Ukrainian drone attack on Crimea kills civilian
original.description: A civilian was killed in the village of Novosyolovskoye in the Razdolnensky district of Crimea in an overnight Ukrainian drone attack, regional head Sergey Aksyonov said.

retained.title: Ukrainian drone attack on Crimea kills civilian
retained.description: A civilian was killed in the village of Novosyolovskoye in the Razdolnensky district of Crimea in an overnight Ukrainian drone attack, regional head Sergey Aksyonov said.

review.note: Both reports relay Aksyonov's claim of one civilian death in Novosyolovskoye during the night leading into August 12. Without an incident time, the UTC date could be August 11 or 12. Attribution is a Russian-installed official's claim, not independent verification.

original.title: Severe storms and tornadoes kill three in US Midwest
original.description: Severe storms swept across the US Midwest, spawning tornadoes near Chicago and producing damaging winds and flash flooding. At least three people died, two in Indiana including a four-year-old killed by a fallen tree, and one in Roseville, Ohio, where emergency crews could not reach the victim; hundreds of thousands of customers lost power.

retained.title: Severe storms and tornadoes kill three in US Midwest
retained.description: Three deaths were reported amid the August 11 Midwest storms: a child struck by a falling tree in Indiana, a person killed in a Portage house explosion whose cause was under investigation, and an Ohio resident whom emergency responders could not reach because of flooding.

review.note: Reports published August 12 describe Tuesday August 11 storms. Three associated deaths are reported, but the Portage house-explosion cause was still being investigated and the Ohio death was an indirect emergency-access death. Exact UTC times of the geographically separate deaths were not established. Do not present all three as direct tornado deaths or use publication date as occurrence date.

original.title: Landslide in Rolpa district kills ten
original.description: A landslide triggered by continuous rain swept away nine houses, two cowsheds, a shop and a church in the Kotalbara area of Thabang Rural Municipality in Nepal's western Rolpa district on the night of August 12, 2026, killing 10 people and leaving two missing. Five bodies were recovered at the site and five more were found in neighbouring Pyuthan district, police said.

retained.title: Landslide in Rolpa district kills ten
retained.description: A landslide triggered by continuous rain swept away nine houses, two cowsheds, a shop and a church in the Kotalbara area of Thabang Rural Municipality in Nepal's western Rolpa district on the night of August 12, 2026, killing 10 people and leaving two missing. Five bodies were recovered at the site and five more were found in neighbouring Pyuthan district, police said.

review.note: August 12 evening at Kotalbara is supported. Initial ten dead/three missing contradicts the record's two missing. Police reported 12 recovered dead and one child missing August 15; August 19 reporting says 13 killed without explaining whether the last missing child was recovered or presumed dead. Confirm that distinction before updating lives_lost. The separate August 13 Sunchhahari landslide is not this event.

original.title: Russian drone and missile attack on Zaporizhzhia kills five
original.description: Russian forces launched a combined drone and missile attack on Zaporizhzhia in the early hours, damaging buildings and industrial facilities and causing fires and power outages. Five people were killed and at least 20 were injured, according to the head of the Zaporizhzhia Regional Military Administration, Ivan Fedorov.

retained.title: Russian drone and missile attack on Zaporizhzhia kills five
retained.description: Russian forces launched a combined drone and missile attack on Zaporizhzhia in the early hours, damaging buildings and industrial facilities and causing fires and power outages. Five people were killed and at least 20 were injured, according to the head of the Zaporizhzhia Regional Military Administration, Ivan Fedorov.

review.note: The matching five-dead/20-injured report is dated August 11, with its update at 02:10 local, and describes the August 10-11 attack. This strongly duplicates the original August 11 'Russian combined strike on Zaporizhzhia kills seven' row, whose toll later reached eight and UTC date is August 10. No separate August 13 five-death event was established. Withhold this duplicate candidate pending identity reconciliation; do not publish both.

original.title: Explosion during ordnance disposal in Sevastopol kills five
original.description: Five people were killed on August 13, 2026, during the clearance and disposal of explosive ordnance following a Ukrainian UAV attack on Sevastopol, Russian media reported. Four of the dead were pyrotechnicians of the Russian Ministry of Emergency Situations (EMERCOM) and one was a security guard.

retained.title: Explosion during ordnance disposal in Sevastopol kills five
retained.description: Five people were killed on August 13, 2026, during the clearance and disposal of explosive ordnance following a Ukrainian UAV attack on Sevastopol, Russian media reported. Four of the dead were pyrotechnicians of the Russian Ministry of Emergency Situations (EMERCOM) and one was a security guard.

review.note: EMERCOM confirms four personnel deaths and Reuters adds the security guard, quoting the governor's disposal-after-drone-attack account. EMERCOM says the night of August 13 without an exact time, so August 12 versus 13 UTC remains unresolved. Crimea should be identified as occupied Ukrainian territory.

original.title: Fire at Greater Noida wood-cutting shop kills one worker
original.location: Shahberi, Greater Noida, Uttar Pradesh, India
original.description: A massive fire broke out late at night at a CNC wood-cutting shop in the Shahberi furniture market of Greater Noida West, Uttar Pradesh, killing one young man, Altamas, from suffocation and leaving another, Aman, in serious condition. A short circuit was suspected as the cause; firefighters rescued the two trapped workers and police registered the case.

retained.title: Fire at Greater Noida wood-cutting shop kills one worker
retained.location: Shahberi, Greater Noida, Uttar Pradesh, India
retained.description: A fire at a wood-cutting shop in Shahberi, Greater Noida West, left Altamas dead and Aman injured. Police said both were rescued unconscious and taken to hospital after the overnight fire on August 13-14.

review.note: PTI dates the fire to the intervening night of August 13-14, not a precise time. One died; the other was later stable, not necessarily still critical. An exact time is needed for UTC. Full ThePrint open was denied; indexed PTI text supports the incident and rescue.

original.title: Car crash into truck in Nagpur kills two students
original.description: Two students were killed and one injured when their car crashed into a parked truck in Nagpur, Maharashtra, on the way to a friend's birthday party. CCTV footage of the crash circulated widely on social media.

retained.title: Car crash into truck in Nagpur kills two students
retained.description: Two 17-year-old students died and a third teenager was seriously injured when their car hit a stationary truck in Nagpur early on August 12 local time. Police said they had gone for a drive while waiting for a friend's birthday celebration.

review.note: NDTV's August 13 article explicitly says early Wednesday morning, August 12, and local August 12 reporting corroborates that day. UTC could be August 11 or 12 without the crash time. Two dead and one injured are supported. The teenagers were taking a drive while awaiting a birthday celebration, not necessarily traveling to the party.

original.title: Russian glide bomb hits apartment block in Donetsk region, killing one
original.description: A Russian glide bomb demolished six floors of a 10-story apartment block in Ukraine's eastern Donetsk region on August 14, 2026, killing one person and wounding at least 16 others, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said. Reports from Kramatorsk described 17 wounded in the glide bomb attack.

retained.title: Russian glide bomb hits apartment block in Donetsk region, killing one
retained.description: A Russian guided-bomb attack damaged an apartment building in Kramatorsk, killing one person and injuring others. Reports published August 14 described an overnight strike, with the reported injury count later rising to 22.

review.note: The attack is in Kramatorsk and one death is supported. Injury reports increased from 16/17 to 22. Overnight timing leaves August 13 versus 14 UTC unresolved. Omit the precise floors-destroyed count rather than retain an unchecked structural detail.

original.title: Russian drone strike on Marhanets kills three-month-old baby
original.description: Russian forces struck a multi-storey building in Marhanets, Dnipropetrovsk region, with drones during a nighttime attack, killing a three-month-old boy and injuring 11 people, including children, according to regional military administration chief Oleksandr Hanzha. Rescue and clearance operations continued at the site.

retained.title: Russian drone strike on Marhanets kills three-month-old baby
retained.description: Russian forces struck a multi-storey building in Marhanets, Dnipropetrovsk region, with drones during a nighttime attack, killing a three-month-old boy and injuring 11 people, including children, according to regional military administration chief Oleksandr Hanzha. Rescue and clearance operations continued at the site.

review.note: The three-month-old boy's death and eleven injured, including two children, are supported. The official account says nighttime; no strike time was located to distinguish August 14 and 15 UTC.

original.title: Israeli airstrikes on southern Lebanon kill 11 including women and children
original.description: Two Israeli airstrikes on southern Lebanon on August 15 killed 11 people, including three children and two women, and wounded others. One strike hit a two-story building in Deir Al Zahrani in the Nabatieh District, killing four; another struck a house in Ansar, killing seven, per the Lebanese Health Ministry. The strikes came amid renewed Israeli bombardment and shelling in Nabatieh, prompting hundreds of residents to flee toward Sidon, and were condemned by Lebanese President Joseph Aoun.

retained.title: Israeli airstrikes on southern Lebanon kill 11 including women and children
retained.description: Lebanon's Health Ministry reported eleven deaths in Israeli strikes on Ansar and Deir Zahrani during the night leading into August 15 local time: seven in Ansar, including three children, and four in Deir Zahrani. Nineteen people were reported wounded.

review.note: The ministry's eleven deaths (seven Ansar, four Deir Zahrani) and nineteen wounded are supported. Accounts describe overnight/dawn strikes without enough precise timing for both sites to assign one UTC date. Strip ancillary flight, building-height and condemnation details, but retain the date blocker.

original.title: Russian night attack on Kryvyi Rih kills one and injures six
original.description: Russian forces attacked Kryvyi Rih at night, killing one person and injuring six others, with two industrial enterprises catching fire and power outages reported across the city. Regional authorities said the attack caused fires and damage to civilian infrastructure.

retained.title: Russian attack on Kryvyi Rih kills two
retained.description: An overnight Russian missile and drone attack on Kryvyi Rih damaged industrial facilities. Regional authorities later reported two people killed and fourteen injured after another body was recovered on the morning of August 16.

review.note: Later regional reporting updates one dead/six injured to two dead/fourteen injured. The 04:25 time is a casualty update, not necessarily the strike time. August 15 versus 16 UTC remains unresolved for the overnight attack.

original.title: Historic flooding in Indiana kills seven
original.description: Days of severe storms and record-setting rainfall produced historic flooding across Indiana, killing at least seven people by August 16, with the White River cresting at record levels and the National Guard assisting rescues. Dozens of people were rescued from vehicles and homes as rivers overflowed across the state.

retained.title: Historic flooding in Indiana kills seven
retained.description: Days of severe storms and record-setting rainfall produced historic flooding across Indiana, killing at least seven people by August 16, with the White River cresting at record levels and the National Guard assisting rescues. Dozens of people were rescued from vehicles and homes as rivers overflowed across the state.

review.note: Seven is a cumulative storm/flood-related toll reported August 16, not seven deaths necessarily occurring that day. NWS places the rainfall/flood episode earlier in the week. This overlaps the August 12 Midwest three-death record, which already includes Indiana victims. Resolve incident boundaries, direct/indirect deaths and duplicate victims before publication.

original.title: Ukraine launches one of its largest aerial attacks of the war on Russia, killing at least six
original.location: Moscow region and other areas, Russia
original.description: Ukraine launched one of its largest aerial attacks of the war overnight on August 15-16, with Russia reporting it shot down more than 800 Ukrainian drones, including 187 over the Moscow region, in what TASS called the largest Ukrainian drone attack since the start of the year. At least six people were killed in Russia, and targets included warehouses and industrial plants as well as refineries.

retained.title: Ukrainian attacks across Russia reportedly kill six
retained.location: Moscow region and other areas, Russia
retained.description: Russian authorities reported at least six deaths after widespread overnight Ukrainian drone attacks reported August 16. Attacks affected the Moscow region and other areas, including industrial and energy facilities.

review.note: The six reported deaths and Russian claims of hundreds of drones are supported, but this is an overnight multi-region aggregate without UTC incident times. Do not infer occurrence date from the August 16 release or independently validate the claimed interception count/ranking. Resolve the fatal incidents before publishing a single-date total.

original.title: Ukrainian missile strikes on Koloskovo in Belgorod region kill six
original.location: Koloskovo, Valuysky district, Belgorod region, Russia
original.description: Ukrainian missile strikes killed six people and wounded four others, including a child, in the village of Koloskovo in the Valuysky district of Russia's Belgorod region, about 15 km from the Ukraine border, according to acting governor Alexander Shuvaev. The attack burned a structure and damaged a vehicle, and came amid sharply escalated cross-border missile exchanges between the two countries.

retained.title: Ukrainian missile strikes on Koloskovo in Belgorod region kill six
retained.location: Koloskovo, Valuysky district, Belgorod region, Russia
retained.description: Russian regional authorities reported that a Ukrainian missile attack on Koloskovo in Belgorod region killed six people and injured four, including a child. The announcement was made on August 17; the precise UTC date of the attack remains unestablished.

review.note: The August 17 morning announcement supports six reported deaths and four injuries but does not establish whether the strike was before or after midnight UTC. Border distance is 15 miles, about 24 km, not 15 km. Short proposed prose removes the unsupported distance and burning detail; date remains unresolved.

original.title: Gold mine collapse on Cameroon-CAR border kills over 100 miners
original.location: Zamboye, Garoua-Boulai border area, Cameroon / Central African Republic
original.description: More than 100 miners were killed when an artisanal gold mine caved in at Zamboye, a border village between Cameroon and the Central African Republic, on August 18. By August 19, 107 bodies had been recovered from the rubble, according to the local mayor Amadou Abdon, with the toll expected to rise as rescue operations continued.

retained.title: Gold mine collapse on Cameroon-CAR border kills over 100 miners
retained.description: An artisanal gold mine collapsed at Zamboye near the Cameroon border on August 18. Local reporting attributed 107 recovered bodies to Garoua-Boulai's mayor; AP reported more than 100 deaths, while CAR authorities said the exact toll was still being established.

review.note: CAR authorities locate the mine in their territory; some initial Cameroonian reports mislocate it. The 107 figure is the Garoua-Boulai mayor's provisional recovery account, not a final CAR-confirmed count. CAR prosecutors said the exact total was still being determined. Retain that contradiction explicitly; final toll is unresolved.

original.title: Torrential rains in southwest China kill ten
original.description: Torrential rains across southwest China killed 10 people and forced thousands to evacuate, with flooding and landslides reported across the region. Officials warned that disaster risk remained high as further heavy rainfall was forecast, and emergency response teams were deployed to affected areas.

retained.title: Torrential rains in southwest China kill ten
retained.description: Torrential rains across southwest China killed 10 people and forced thousands to evacuate, with flooding and landslides reported across the region. Officials warned that disaster risk remained high as further heavy rainfall was forecast, and emergency response teams were deployed to affected areas.

review.note: August 19 is publication date. Ten combines five in a Guangxi construction-site landslide on Monday August 17 and five in a Changning, Sichuan banquet-wall collapse at 17:30 CST August 18. This is not one August 19 incident. Preserve the aggregate in audit; split/reconcile actual incidents before publication. The Guangxi incident's precise UTC timing remains unestablished.

original.title: Suspected PDF fighters kill 12 civilians in Mahlaing Township, Myanmar
original.description: Twelve civilians were killed in an attack on Hta Man Gyi village in Mahlaing Township, Mandalay Region, on August 31, 2026, which Myanmar's military government blamed on members of the resistance-aligned People's Defence Force. State media said the attackers entered the village and opened fire on residents.

retained.title: Suspected PDF fighters kill 12 civilians in Mahlaing Township, Myanmar
retained.description: Twelve civilians were killed in an attack on Hta Man Gyi village in Mahlaing Township, Mandalay Region, on August 31, 2026, which Myanmar's military government blamed on members of the resistance-aligned People's Defence Force. State media said the attackers entered the village and opened fire on residents.

review.note: Approximately 04:00 MMT August 31 is August 30 UTC. ACLED describes an unidentified armed group and victims including administrators/security-team or militia leaders assumed unarmed; military media blame PDF. Do not silently endorse either perpetrator identity or civilian status. IOM URL is a country feed, not a stable individual source record; Myawady open failed although search retrieved its text. Corroboration and victim status remain insufficient for publication.

original.title: US airstrikes on IRGC targets in Iran kill five
original.description: The United States carried out additional airstrikes against Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) targets in Iran on September 1, 2026, in response to attempted attacks on commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and on US troops in the region. Five members of the IRGC Aerospace Force were killed in Kermanshah, according to US Central Command.

retained.title: US strike reportedly kills four IRGC members in Kermanshah
retained.description: Iran's provincial IRGC reported four Aerospace Force members killed in a US strike in Kermanshah, according to September 2 reporting. The precise UTC date remains unestablished; the casualty claim came from Iranian authorities, not CENTCOM.

review.note: CENTCOM confirms operations, not five Kermanshah deaths. Anadolu September 2 attributes FOUR Aerospace Force deaths to the provincial IRGC, separately three Basij on Lavan Island. No corroborated five-person Kermanshah total found. The exact Kermanshah strike time/date within the September 1-2 attacks is not established. Do not merge wedding casualties or Lavan deaths.

original.title: Russian missile and drone attacks on Kyiv kill at least 12
original.description: Russian missile and drone attacks on Kyiv and surrounding areas on September 1, 2026, killed at least 12 people, including an Indian national, and wounded dozens more, according to Ukrainian officials. Residential buildings and other civilian infrastructure were damaged in what President Volodymyr Zelenskyy described as a continuing series of Russian strikes on the capital.

retained.title: Russian missile and drone attacks on Kyiv kill at least 12
retained.description: Russian missile and drone attacks on Kyiv and surrounding areas on September 1, 2026, killed at least 12 people, including an Indian national, and wounded dozens more, according to Ukrainian officials. Residential buildings and other civilian infrastructure were damaged in what President Volodymyr Zelenskyy described as a continuing series of Russian strikes on the capital.

review.note: Twelve deaths including an Indian national are supported, but the attack ran more than 12 hours overnight August 31-September 1 and into Tuesday. Fatal incident times were not established sufficiently to assign all twelve to September 1 UTC. The publication date cannot resolve the mixed interval.

original.title: Fuel siphoning deaths in Rivers State, Nigeria, reach 43
original.description: At least 37 people, a figure officials later put at 43, died after inhaling petroleum fumes while allegedly siphoning fuel from an illegally tapped pipeline in Rivers State, Nigeria, on September 3, 2026. The victims were overcome by toxic fumes at the site of the tapped pipeline.

retained.title: Fuel siphoning deaths in Rivers State, Nigeria, reach 43
retained.description: Dozens of people reportedly died during an alleged petroleum-siphoning attempt at Okari Jetty, Okrika, around midnight at the start of September 3 local time. Reports describe toxic-fume exposure and some drownings, but differ between at least 37 deaths and 43 dead or feared dead.

review.note: Channels gives approximately 00:00 WAT September 3, which is September 2 UTC. Anadolu reports 43 dead but Vanguard calls 43 feared dead and later AP reports at least 37. Reports also differ on loading vessel versus tapped pipeline; some victims reportedly drowned after inhalation. No reconciled confirmed 43-person toll retrieved.

original.title: Pakistani security forces kill 48 separatists in Balochistan raids
original.description: The Pakistani military said it killed 48 Baloch separatists in a series of raids on hideouts across Balochistan province over the 72 hours ending September 4, 2026. The operations targeted militant positions across the restive province.

retained.title: Pakistani security forces kill 48 separatists in Balochistan raids
retained.description: Pakistan's military announced September 4 that its forces had killed 48 alleged militants during several raids in Balochistan over the preceding 72 hours. This is an attributed operational aggregate, not a September 4 single-day death toll.

review.note: The military's 48 is a multi-raid total over 72 hours ending September 4, not 48 deaths on that date. Geo identifies six in Mastung September 4, with other operations on earlier dates. Incident-specific dates/UTC and allocation are needed before publication as daily events; reporting does not independently establish military claims about all victims.

original.title: Israeli airstrikes on southern Lebanon kill 11, including children and medics
original.description: Israeli airstrikes in southern Lebanon on September 7, 2026, killed 11 people, including two children killed in a strike on a residential building in Kfar Reman and two medics killed in a separate strike on a vehicle in the same area. Five other people were injured.

retained.title: Israeli strikes on Kfar Rumman kill 13, including children and a medic
retained.description: Israeli strikes on a residential building and a vehicle in Kfar Rumman were reported on September 7. Lebanon's Health Ministry later reported 13 deaths: twelve in the building, including six children, and one medic in the vehicle strike. Two other medics were wounded. The precise UTC date remains unestablished.

review.note: Al-Monitor September 14 is republication: Reuters dateline/photo September 7; MarketScreener explicitly shows September 7 publication and September 14 modification. NOT a new September 14 attack. Updated ministry toll 13 comprises 12 in building, including 6 children/3 women, plus ONE medic killed and 2 medics wounded; original two-medic-death wording is superseded. Earlier AP 12 and WAFA 11 are preliminary. Reuters contains contradictory timing cues: state media 'after midnight' versus witnesses preparing for school; exact UTC date September 6/7 remains unresolved. Two Reuters URLs share one wire report.

original.title: Saudi airstrike on prison in Al-Jawf, Yemen, kills 17
original.description: A Saudi airstrike hit a prison in Al-Jawf Governorate, Yemen, on September 7, 2026, during an offensive against Houthi forces, killing seven people, including a child, and trapping dozens under the rubble. The toll rose to 17 the following day as bodies were recovered.

retained.title: Saudi airstrike on prison in Al-Jawf, Yemen, kills 17
retained.description: A Saudi airstrike hit a prison in Al-Jawf Governorate, Yemen, on September 7, 2026, during an offensive against Houthi forces, killing seven people, including a child, and trapping dozens under the rubble. The toll rose to 17 the following day as bodies were recovered.

review.note: AP September 9 reports 23 recovered deaths, superseding 17; these are updates to the September 7 prison incident. Houthi authorities blame Saudi-led airstrikes; the Yemeni rights centre blames the Houthis. Do not state Saudi responsibility as undisputed. Exact strike time/UTC boundary was not established. Two AP documents share publisher and Houthi-source provenance.

sources.name: Yemeni Center for Rehabilitation of Victims of Violations and Torture

original.title: Death toll in Yemen offensive reaches 500
original.description: The confirmed death toll from an offensive Houthi forces launched in western Yemen reached 500 by September 8, 2026, including 278 Houthi fighters, 216 soldiers of the Yemeni Armed Forces and 29 civilians, according to AFP. Fighting around Taiz and Hodeidah was described as the deadliest in Yemen since 2022.

retained.title: AFP sources report more than 500 deaths in renewed Yemen fighting
retained.description: AFP reported on September 8 that military and medical sources counted at least 278 Houthi fighters,216 government troops and 29 civilians killed since renewed fighting began the previous week. Their components total 523; this is a cumulative attributed figure, not a single-day toll.

review.note: Components 278+216+29 equal 523, not 500. AFP says MORE THAN 500 and attributes figures to unnamed military/medical sources, not a universally confirmed total. Multi-day offensive since the previous week; September 8 is report date, not date of 523 deaths. Reconcile possible overlap with Al-Jawf prison and other Yemen strikes before integration. Arabic liveblog repeats AFP rather than independently verifies counts.

original.title: Russian strikes on Kyiv and Kyiv region kill seven
original.description: Russia launched drones and missiles at Kyiv and the surrounding region on September 8, 2026, after a pause in strikes over the weekend. Five people were killed and 29 injured in the city, while two people were killed and three injured in a drone attack on the Kyiv region in which a warehouse area in Buchansky district caught fire. The attacks damaged civilian infrastructure at at least 16 locations, and the combined toll reached seven.

retained.title: Russian strikes on Kyiv and Kyiv region kill seven
retained.description: Russian strikes reported overnight and during September 8 killed five people in Kyiv and two in the surrounding region, according to Ukrainian authorities. The attacks damaged warehouses and other civilian buildings. Fatal incident times remain insufficiently resolved for a single UTC date.

review.note: City government confirms five killed in September 8 attacks; UATV separately reports two in Kyiv region. Injury counts differ 23/29/35 and need not be retained. Strikes spanned Monday night and Tuesday; exact fatal-incident UTC dates unestablished. Sept 10 two-death Kyiv record may be an earlier bulletin from this attack; do not add without resolving identity.

original.title: Drone strike near courthouse in Umm Ruwaba, Sudan, kills 13
original.description: A drone strike by the Rapid Support Forces hit a courthouse in Umm Ruwaba, North Kordofan, Sudan, on September 8, 2026, killing around 13 people and wounding dozens, according to local reports.

retained.title: Drone strike near courthouse in Umm Ruwaba, Sudan, kills 13
retained.description: A drone strike near the Um Rawaba courthouse on the afternoon of September 8 killed at least 12 people, according to local reports; the Sudan Doctors Network reported 13. Sources blamed the RSF. The precise toll remains unreconciled.

review.note: Tuesday afternoon September 8 supports same UTC date. Sudan Doctors Network reporting gives 13 dead/22 injured; Radio Tamazuj's authorities/eyewitnesses give 12 dead/20 injured outside courthouse. No reconciled final count retrieved. RSF attribution is a claim by monitoring groups/army-aligned authorities, not independently proven here.

original.title: Famine in Jebel Marra, Sudan, kills at least 20
original.description: A famine was reported across Sudan's Jebel Marra area in Darfur on September 8, 2026, with at least 20 people dying from hunger and disease, according to the area's civil authority. Aid groups warned the toll could rise sharply without humanitarian access.

retained.title: Famine in Jebel Marra, Sudan, kills at least 20
retained.description: On September 8, the SLM-AW-aligned civil administration reported famine conditions in Jebel Marra and nearby areas, estimating that up to 20 people were dying daily from hunger and disease. This was a reported mortality estimate, not a verified September 8 event toll.

review.note: Source says UP TO 20 dying EACH DAY from hunger/disease, an estimated mortality rate attributed to SLM-AW-aligned civil administration, not at least 20 identified deaths on September 8. Famine language is a local authority claim, not an IPC determination established here. No incident-level toll/date or second independent source record retrieved.

original.title: Russian large-scale attack on Kyiv kills two
original.description: A large-scale Russian attack on Kyiv on September 10, 2026, killed two people and injured at least ten, according to Ukrainian authorities.

retained.title: Russian large-scale attack on Kyiv kills two
retained.description: A large-scale Russian attack on Kyiv on September 10, 2026, killed two people and injured at least ten, according to Ukrainian authorities.

review.note: Matching two-dead/ten-injured Ukrinform bulletin is dated September 8, not 10; AFP corroborates early September 8 two-death count. September 10 reporting describes a gas-station strike with injuries and a separate regional death, not the claimed city toll. Likely a misdated preliminary duplicate of September 8 aggregate, but cannot assert identical victims without further evidence; do not publish or add twice.

original.title: Russian attacks on Mykolaiv kill four
original.description: Russian attacks on Mykolaiv over the 24 hours to September 10, 2026, killed four people and injured 19, damaging residential buildings and port facilities in the city.

retained.title: Russian attacks on Mykolaiv kill four
retained.description: Russian attacks on Mykolaiv during 9 September and the following night killed four people and injured 19, according to Ukrainian police. The figure covers a reporting interval rather than a single established UTC day.

review.note: Four deaths and 19 injuries are supported for attacks during September 9 and the night into September 10, not four established deaths on September 10 UTC. Ukrinform identifies two women and two men among the dead. The reporting interval crosses dates and individual fatal incident times were not established. The first two documents draw on the same police casualty account.

original.title: Ukrainian drone strike kills woman in Borisoglebsk, Russia
original.description: A Ukrainian drone fell on a house in Borisoglebsk in Russia's Voronezh Oblast on September 10, 2026, killing a woman and injuring two other people, according to regional authorities.

retained.title: Ukrainian drone strike kills woman in Borisoglebsk, Russia
retained.description: Regional authorities said an attack by Ukrainian drones overnight on 9-10 September killed a woman and injured two people in Borisoglebsk, Voronezh Oblast.

review.note: Regional authorities reported a woman killed and two people injured in Borisoglebsk. The attack occurred overnight September 9-10 local time; the morning September 10 announcement is not an incident timestamp. Both sources rely on the regional governor. The UTC date remains unresolved, and attribution to Ukraine is the authorities' account.

original.title: US strike on suspected drug boat in the Caribbean kills three
original.description: The United States military killed three people described as suspected narco-terrorists in strikes on a boat in the Caribbean Sea on September 10, 2026, part of its campaign against drug-trafficking vessels in the region.

retained.title: US strike on suspected drug boat in the Caribbean kills three
retained.description: U.S. Southern Command said its forces killed three people in a strike on a boat in the Caribbean on 9 September 2026. The military alleged that the vessel was involved in drug trafficking; the retrieved reports did not independently establish that allegation.

review.note: SOUTHCOM dates the operation to September 9; September 10 is the reporting date. Both publishers relay the same military announcement, not independent confirmation of the occupants' identities or trafficking allegations. The operation's exact time and the command's date time zone were not established, so the proposed September 9 date is not verified as UTC and the row remains withheld.

original.title: Hurricane Lowell linked to at least two deaths in Hawaii
original.description: Hurricane Lowell battered the western islands of Hawaii in September 2026. By September 10 the bodies of two men had been recovered and the storm was linked to at least two deaths as recovery operations continued.

retained.title: Hurricane Lowell linked to at least two deaths in Hawaii
retained.description: Two deaths were linked to Hurricane Lowell in Hawaii: a man killed by a falling tree on Oahu and a man found dead on Kauai after being reported missing. The reports concern different incident and recovery dates, not two established deaths on 10 September.

review.note: Two deaths were linked to the storm, but September 10 is a report/update date. Hawaii News Now places the fatal Waimanalo tree incident at about 20:35 HST on Monday September 7, which is September 8 UTC. The other man's body was recovered on Kauai on September 9 after he went missing the previous day; recovery time does not establish death time. A single September 10 UTC casualty allocation is unsupported. Storm-surge attribution for the Kauai death was preliminary.

retained.promise: Mobilise $100 billion per year in climate finance for developing countries by 2020

review.note: OECD confirms 83.3 billion in 2020 and first reaching target in 2022. Developed countries, not all UNFCCC parties, were the financing providers. Exact Copenhagen adoption date needs agreement text. Annual ongoing obligation should not be collapsed into permanently kept status.

As of mid-2026 it is still scheduled for release in Q3 2026, though Bloomberg reported in Aug 2025 that mass production could slip ~3 months to mid-2026. Deadline has not yet passed.
evidence: Announced at Computex in Taipei in 2024 by Jensen Huang
Wikipedia's Rubin article: 'scheduled for release in Q3 of 2026'
Bloomberg (Aug 2025) reported a possible delay to mid-2026; NVIDIA denied
Rubin Ultra promised for 2027 at GTC 2025

retained.promise: Rubin is coming in 2026
retained.description: NVIDIA's 2026 Rubin announcement says the platform is in full production and partner products are expected in the second half of 2026. Production and customer availability are separate milestones.
evidence: NVIDIA gives second-half 2026 partner availability, not a specific Q3 launch date.

review.note: Primary 2026 release distinguishes full production from partner availability in second half of 2026. Replaces unsourced Q3 specificity and confusing delay-to-mid-2026 wording. Computex original date and actual availability as of audit still need checking.

original.promise: Bard will be rolling out to trusted testers in the coming weeks
original.description: After ChatGPT's launch, Pichai announced Google's Bard chatbot in a blog post saying it would roll out 'in the coming weeks'. Despite an embarrassing demo error, Bard opened early access on March 21, 2023 to users in the US and UK via waitlist — roughly six weeks later.
evidence: Announced Feb 6, 2023 in Google blog post 'Google AI updates: Bard and new AI features in Search'
Google opened early access for Bard on March 21, 2023, in the US and UK
Google employees were asked to test Bard internally for 2-4 hours before launch

retained.promise: Make Bard more widely available to the public in the coming weeks
retained.description: Pichai announced trusted-tester access on February 6, 2023 and wider public access in coming weeks. Google began US and UK public early access on March 21, 2023.
evidence: Google's February 6 announcement distinguishes immediate testing from later public access.
Google announced public early access March 21.

review.note: Trusted testers opened February 6; 'coming weeks' referred to wider public access. March 31 is an inferred cutoff, not an announced date.

original.promise: Amazon's all-new Alexa voice assistant is coming soon, powered by a new Alexa LLM
original.description: At Amazon's Sept 2023 devices event, Jassy's team said the generative-AI Alexa would arrive 'in the coming months' via a US preview. The launch was repeatedly delayed through all of 2024 (Business Insider reported in June 2024 that it had slipped to 2025), and Alexa+ was not introduced until February 26, 2025 — roughly 17 months after the promise.
evidence: The Verge (Sept 20, 2023): new Alexa to roll out 'in the coming months' via preview, US only
Business Insider (June 2024): Amazon's new generative AI Alexa delayed to 2025
Wikipedia: 'In February 2025, Amazon introduced Alexa+, the latest version of their voice assistant'
No commercial launch occurred in 2024 as promised

The launch was repeatedly delayed through all of 2024 (Business Insider reported in June 2024 that it had slipped to 2025), and Alexa+ was not introduced until February 26, 2025 — roughly 17 months after the promise.
