original.promise: We expect Windows 10 to be running on over one billion devices within two to three years
original.description: At BUILD 2015, Nadella set a public target of 1 billion Windows 10 devices within 2-3 years of the July 2015 release. Microsoft quietly abandoned the goal — Windows 10 only passed 1 billion active devices in March 2020, almost five years after launch. It remains one of the most cited missed CEO targets in tech.
evidence: ZDNet (Apr 30, 2015): 'Microsoft's big Windows 10 goal: one billion or bust'
Wikipedia: Microsoft 'aimed to have Windows 10 installed on over a billion devices within three years of release; ultimately, that goal was reached in March 2020, almost five years later'
The Verge (Mar 16, 2020): 'Microsoft hits its goal of 1 billion devices running Windows 10'

retained.promise: We expect Windows 10 to be running on over one billion devices within two to three years
retained.description: At Build on April 29, 2015, Microsoft set a goal of one billion Windows 10 devices within two to three years of availability. It announced more than one billion monthly active devices on March 16, 2020.
evidence: Terry Myerson's April 2015 post records the target.
Microsoft's March 2020 post records achievement.

review.note: Primary announcement authored/presented by Terry Myerson. It was two-to-three years from availability, not June 2018. Billion monthly-active-device milestone came March 2020; replace superlative with measured outcome.

Apple newsroom (Jan 8, 2024): 'Apple Vision Pro available in the U.S. on February 2'

review.note: Original promise was early 2024 in US; February 29 is not an explicit cutoff. Official sources support $3,499 and February 2 scheduled availability; remove unsupported review/sales assessment. Actual retail launch confirmation remains separate from January forward announcement.

original.promise: Meta AI is on track to be the most used AI assistant in the world by the end of the year
original.description: On Meta's Q2 2024 earnings call Zuckerberg said Meta AI would become the most-used AI assistant worldwide by end of 2024. Meta AI reached 500M monthly users (Oct 2024) and 1B monthly users (May 2025) per Zuckerberg — beating ChatGPT on monthly users — but ChatGPT had ~700M weekly active users by Dec 2024 and remains ahead on engagement, so the 'most used' claim is disputed depending on the metric.
evidence: The Verge (Jul 31, 2024): 'He again telegraphed that the Meta AI assistant is on track to be the most used in the world before the end of the year'
Meta AI hit ~500M MAU by Oct 2024 and ~1B MAU by May 2025 (Zuckerberg claims)
ChatGPT passed 700M weekly active users in Dec 2024 — lead contested on WAU vs MAU basis

retained.promise: Meta AI is on track to be the most used AI assistant in the world by the end of the year
retained.description: Meta's claimed monthly active users and ChatGPT's weekly active users are not directly comparable. ChatGPT's 700-million-weekly-user milestone was reported in August 2025, not December 2024.
evidence: December 2024 ChatGPT reporting put weekly users at about 300 million.
700 million weekly users was reported in August 2025.

review.note: 700m weekly ChatGPT users was an August 2025 milestone, not December 2024. Monthly and weekly measures cannot adjudicate 'most used' without aligned definitions; partial status remains unproven.

original.promise: FTX is fine. Assets are fine.
original.description: Three days before FTX collapsed, SBF tweeted 'FTX is fine. Assets are fine.' On November 11, 2022 — 72 hours later — FTX and its affiliates filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in Delaware after a bank run exposed that customer assets had been used to cover Alameda Research's positions. SBF was later convicted on seven counts of fraud and conspiracy. Prosecutors noted his statements were 'misleading' and technically framed around solvency rather than liquidity.
evidence: Tweet posted November 8, 2022; bankruptcy filed November 11, 2022
Wikipedia: FTX executive described the statements as false / 'misleading but technically true'
SBF convicted Nov 2023 on seven counts including fraud and money laundering

retained.promise: FTX is fine. Assets are fine.
retained.description: The SEC complaint places Bankman-Fried's assurance about FTX assets on or about November 7, 2022 and alleges that customer assets had been diverted to Alameda.
evidence: SEC alleges the assurance was made while Bankman-Fried knew customer assets had been used by Alameda.

review.note: SEC complaint dates tweet on or about November 7, not November 8; remove exact 72-hour narrative. This is a present-tense assurance, not a dated future promise. Insolvency narrative and later convictions require separate judicial outcome source.

original.promise: We will manufacture 2.5 billion doses of the COVID-19 vaccine in 2021
original.description: Pfizer/BioNTech committed in February 2021 to 2 billion doses for 2021, then raised the target to 2.5 billion at end of March 2021 — a pledge tied to Bourla's 'back to normal by end of 2021' message. The partnership exceeded it, producing roughly 3 billion doses during 2021 (3.1B by year-end per company statements), one of the rare mega-pledges of the pandemic era that was fully delivered.
evidence: Wikipedia: 'In February 2021, BioNTech announced it would increase production by more than 50% to manufacture 2 billion doses in 2021, raised again at the end of March to 2.5 billion doses in 2021'
Bloomberg (Mar 30, 2021): 'BioNTech Raises Covid Vaccine Target to 2.5 Billion Doses'
Pfizer/BioNTech reported manufacturing ~3 billion doses in 2021, surpassing the target

retained.promise: We will manufacture 2.5 billion doses of the COVID-19 vaccine in 2021
retained.description: Pfizer and BioNTech forecast at least 2.5 billion doses manufactured by end-2021. BioNTech subsequently reported more than 3.1 billion doses delivered by early March 2022; that is not a 2021 production total.
evidence: Company release distinguishes manufacturing forecast from cumulative deliveries through March 2022.

review.note: 3.1bn delivery figure is early March 2022, not end-2021. Forecast in company release is conditional. Original March 30/Bourla attribution and 2021 manufactured count need original results; remove 'rare mega-pledge' commentary.

original.promise: Hyperinflation is going to happen soon in the US and the world, and it will hit the poorest hardest
original.description: Dorsey tweeted that hyperinflation would hit the US and the world 'soon'. US inflation instead peaked at 9.1% in June 2022 (the highest in 40 years but nowhere near hyperinflation) and fell to roughly 3% by mid-2023. No hyperinflation occurred in the US or globally, and Bitcoin — which Dorsey linked to inflation hedging — fell about 75% from its Nov 2021 peak across 2022.
evidence: Tweet on @jack, April 2, 2022
US CPI peaked at 9.1% (June 2022) then declined to ~3% by mid-2023 — no hyperinflation
Global inflation also normalized through 2023

retained.promise: Hyperinflation is going to happen soon in the US and the world, and it will hit the poorest hardest

original.promise: We expect to regain process leadership by 2025
original.description: At the 'Intel Unleashed' IDM 2.0 event, Gelsinger promised a 5-nodes-in-4-years roadmap (Intel 7/4/3/20A/18A) that would restore Intel's chipmaking lead over TSMC by 2025. Intel 18A was delayed from H2 2024 to 2025, TSMC's N2 kept the process lead, and Gelsinger was ousted as CEO in December 2024 before the goal was reached; Intel's first 18A product (Panther Lake) only shipped in late 2025. Process leadership was not regained in the promised window.
evidence: IDM 2.0 announced March 23, 2021 with 'regain process leadership' from TSMC as the goal
Intel delayed 18A (originally 2024 target) into 2025
Gelsinger removed as CEO December 2, 2024
TSMC (N2, 2025) retained the process lead; Panther Lake (18A) shipped late 2025

Intel 18A was delayed from H2 2024 to 2025, TSMC's N2 kept the process lead, and Gelsinger was ousted as CEO in December 2024 before the goal was reached; Intel's first 18A product (Panther Lake) only shipped in late 2025. retained.promise: Raise the child tax credit from $2,000 to $5,000 per child (Aug 2024 campaign pledge)
retained.description: The One Big Beautiful Bill Act (signed 4 Jul 2025) raised the credit only to $2,200, inflation-indexed, with the refundable portion unchanged — no $5,000 credit was ever enacted.
evidence: Retained from the existing collection; outcome evidence remains to be documented.

review.note: IRS source located for actual credit, but original Vance interview/date/deadline and full post-law parameters still need checking. January 2023 predates the described August 2024 proposal. Distinguish proposal/aspiration from guaranteed enacted amount.

original.promise: Victory Plan (presented 16 Oct 2024) demanded an immediate NATO membership invitation as point one, i.e., an invitation before the war's end
original.description: No invitation was issued. Scholz publicly opposed a wartime invite (24 Oct 2024); the US administration said in March 2025 it does not support NATO membership for Ukraine; by 2026 Ukraine remained outside NATO.

retained.promise: Victory Plan (presented 16 Oct 2024) demanded an immediate NATO membership invitation as point one, i.e., an invitation before the war's end
retained.description: Zelenskyy presented the Victory Plan on October 16, 2024. Its first point requested an invitation to NATO; it was not a guarantee that Ukraine itself would issue or secure one by year-end.
evidence: Retained from the existing collection; outcome evidence remains to be documented.

review.note: Official presentation dated October 16, 2024, not January 2023. Invitation was a request to allies, not something Zelenskyy could issue; no December 31 promise established.

original.promise: Total victory and destruction/elimination of Hamas — 'we will not stop the war before achieving all of its goals' (April 2024), vowing to continue 'until victory'
original.description: Hamas survived as a negotiating party: it signed the US-led Gaza peace plan (Oct 2025), released hostages, refused to disarm (3 Oct 2025), and phase 2 (disarmament) was stalled as of May 2026. 64% of Gaza was under Israeli military control as of April 2026, but 'total victory' was not achieved.

retained.promise: Total victory and destruction/elimination of Hamas — 'we will not stop the war before achieving all of its goals' (April 2024), vowing to continue 'until victory'
retained.description: On April 30, 2024 Netanyahu said Israel would not halt the war before achieving its goals and would enter Rafah with or without a deal. The statement gave no calendar deadline.
evidence: April 30 reporting records continued-war and Rafah statements without a year-end deadline.

review.note: April 30, 2024 statement supports conditional continuation and Rafah goals, not January 2023 or a fixed year-end deadline. Precise Hamas status, geographic control and ceasefire claims need distinct evidence; remove unverified percentages.

original.promise: Bring all 251 hostages home
original.description: 33 hostages returned in phase 1 of the Jan 2025 ceasefire (19 Jan – 27 Feb 2025), 20 more on 13 Oct 2025 under the Gaza peace plan, but phase 2 never started — Israel resumed the war on 18 Mar 2025 — and the promise of everyone returning was not fully met by mid-2026.

retained.promise: Bring all 251 hostages home
retained.description: Reuters reported that the remains of Ran Gvili, described as the last Israeli hostage held in Gaza, were recovered on January 26, 2026. Returned hostages and returned remains must be distinguished.
evidence: January 26, 2026 reporting contradicts the claim that the last Israeli hostage remained unreturned in mid-2026.

review.note: January 2023 predates October 7 abductions and no December 2023 deadline is sourced. Reuters reports recovery of the last Israeli hostage's remains January 26, 2026, contradicting stale mid-2026 narrative. Alive versus remains, foreign hostages and all-251 scope need explicit reconciliation before status replacement.

original.promise: Pass 'Plan C' judicial reform — election of judges by popular vote — during her first months
original.description: The constitutional judicial reform passed both chambers in Sept 2024 and was published; Sheinbaum rejected a Supreme Court bid to strike it down and enacted a constitutional-supremacy law limiting challenges.

retained.promise: Pass 'Plan C' judicial reform — election of judges by popular vote — during her first months
retained.description: President Lopez Obrador signed the judicial reform in September 2024 with President-elect Sheinbaum present, before she took office on October 1.
evidence: Contemporaneous reports attribute signing to Lopez Obrador, with Sheinbaum attending.

review.note: Reporting establishes AMLO signed the reform before Sheinbaum took office, not that she passed it during her first months. January 2023 pledge and first-month commitment need evidence; local September 15 evening can be September 16 UTC.

original.promise: Constitutional ban on re-election of any popularly elected office, promised to take effect in 2027
original.description: The anti-re-election rule was published 1 Apr 2025, but its implementation was postponed from 2027 to 2030.

retained.promise: Constitutional ban on re-election of any popularly elected office, promised to take effect in 2027
retained.description: The anti-re-election rule was published 1 Apr 2025, but its implementation was postponed from 2027 to 2030.
evidence: Retained from the existing collection; outcome evidence remains to be documented.

review.note: Official April 1 decree confirms anti-reelection provisions apply from 2030 elections. Original January 2023/2027 promise, exact offices and role at announcement remain unestablished; do not describe every elected office as newly covered.

original.promise: Free nutritious meals (Makan Bergizi Gratis) for schoolchildren, pregnant women and toddlers — targeting 82.9 million beneficiaries
original.description: Launched on schedule (6 Jan 2025) but scaled back: per-meal budget cut to Rp10,000 (from Rp15–20,000), only ~30 million recipients reached by Sept 2025, Rp171trn budget vs Rp420trn needed for full-year operation, 20,000+ food-poisoning cases in 2025, and corruption arrests at the program body in June 2026.

retained.promise: Free nutritious meals (Makan Bergizi Gratis) for schoolchildren, pregnant women and toddlers — targeting 82.9 million beneficiaries
retained.description: Indonesia launched the free-meals programme on January 6, 2025. Reuters reported 570,000 recipients on opening day and a plan then targeting 82.9 million beneficiaries by 2029.
evidence: Contemporaneous launch report distinguishes initial coverage from the 2029 full-scale target.

review.note: Launch reporting gives 82.9m by 2029, not original 2025 deadline. Later accelerated target requires its own dated announcement. Budget, poisoning and arrest allegations unverified; replace with launch facts.

original.promise: 8% annual economic growth by the end of his term (2029)
original.description: Growth was 5.0% (2024) and ~5.1% (2025), with IMF forecasts of ~4.9–5.1% through 2029 — far below the 8% target.

retained.promise: 8% annual economic growth by the end of his term (2029)
retained.description: Prabowo advocated an 8% annual growth target before taking office in 2024. The record's stated 2029 deadline has not passed; lower interim growth does not establish failure at that deadline.
evidence: 2024 Reuters reports describe the growth ambition, not its eventual outcome.

review.note: Reuters supports an 8% growth ambition; current roughly 5% growth or forecasts cannot establish a missed 2029 deadline in 2026. Exact original date and end-term interpretation require source.

original.promise: Defeat inflation ('kill inflation', the overriding goal of his first year)
original.description: Annual inflation fell from 211.4% (2023) and 254.2% (first month) to 117.8% (2024) and ~31.8% by Sept 2025, with monthly inflation at a five-year low of 1.5% (June 2025) — a huge reduction, though inflation was not eliminated.

retained.promise: Defeat inflation ('kill inflation', the overriding goal of his first year)
retained.description: Annual inflation fell from 211.4% (2023) and 254.2% (first month) to 117.8% (2024) and ~31.8% by Sept 2025, with monthly inflation at a five-year low of 1.5% (June 2025) — a huge reduction, though inflation was not eliminated.
evidence: Retained from the existing collection; outcome evidence remains to be documented.

review.note: Search returned INDEC technical indexes, not the needed CPI tables or original pledge. Date/deadline conflict ('first year' versus 2027) unresolved. Need monthly-versus-annual series; claimed June 1.5% must not be certified from unrelated construction-price data.

original.promise: Reduce poverty
original.description: Poverty first spiked from 41.7% to a peak of 57.4% (Jan 2024) after the shock, then fell to 31.6% in H1 2025 (lowest since 2018, below the 2023 starting point); extreme poverty fell from 18.2% to 7.4%.

retained.promise: Reduce poverty
retained.description: INDEC's survey of 31 urban agglomerations reported poverty of 41.7% in H2 2023, 52.9% in H1 2024 and 31.6% in H1 2025. Indigence fell from 18.1% in H1 2024 to 6.9% in H1 2025.
evidence: INDEC's H1 2025 report supplies a comparable half-year series for the same urban survey scope.

review.note: INDEC's consistent half-year series gives 31.6% poverty and 6.9% indigence in H1 2025, not 7.4%. Its H1 2024 poverty figure is 52.9%, not the separate 57.4% monthly estimate. Original promise/date/deadline and an outcome threshold remain unestablished.

original.promise: Campaign pledge (2023): dollarize the economy and abolish the central bank
original.description: Dollarization was abandoned — instead of dollarizing, the government kept the peso, dismantled the 'cepo' capital controls on 14 Apr 2025 and moved to a managed float in a ~1,000–1,400 ARS/USD band under a US$20bn IMF agreement.

retained.promise: Campaign pledge (2023): dollarize the economy and abolish the central bank
retained.description: In April 2025 Argentina relaxed specified foreign-exchange controls and introduced a moving ARS1,000-1,400 per dollar band. This retained the peso and central bank, but does not by itself establish permanent abandonment of dollarization.
evidence: BCRA lists measures relaxed and the peso-band regime; it does not describe universal removal of all controls.

review.note: BCRA describes April 2025 relaxation of specified controls and a currency band, not complete dismantling. Keeping peso then does not prove permanent abandonment of dollarization. Original date and 2025 deadline unverified.

original.promise: Unblock Poland's EU Recovery funds (KPO, ~€59.8bn) 'within weeks' of taking office
original.description: First tranche of PLN 27bn (~€6.3bn) arrived 15 Apr 2024 after the Commission's positive assessment of 29 Feb 2024; further payments followed through 2025, though the full €59.8bn had not all been disbursed.

retained.promise: Unblock Poland's EU Recovery funds (KPO, ~€59.8bn) 'within weeks' of taking office
retained.description: First tranche of PLN 27bn (~€6.3bn) arrived 15 Apr 2024 after the Commission's positive assessment of 29 Feb 2024; further payments followed through 2025, though the full €59.8bn had not all been disbursed.
evidence: Retained from the existing collection; outcome evidence remains to be documented.

review.note: Commission/Euronews support April 15, 2024 payment and financing total. January 2023 promise and 'within weeks' source absent; unblocking eligibility is not the same as first tranche payment. Near-duplicate of index 78 with conflicting outcome chronology.

original.promise: Liberalize the abortion law — legal abortion on request up to 12 weeks of pregnancy
original.description: The liberalization bill was rejected by the Sejm on 12 Jul 2024 (218 votes against, 215 for); the restrictive law remained unchanged and President-elect Nawrocki (2025) opposes liberalization.

retained.promise: Liberalize the abortion law — legal abortion on request up to 12 weeks of pregnancy
retained.description: The Sejm rejected a bill for partial decriminalization of abortion-related acts by 218 votes to 215. That bill should be distinguished from broader legislation establishing access to abortion on request.
evidence: Sejm's legislative record identifies the proposal as partial decriminalization and records the 215-218 vote.

review.note: Sejm record is partial decriminalization, not the same as comprehensive legal access on request. Original pledge date and deadline unverified; do not equate rejection of this bill with voting down every liberalization proposal.

original.promise: Create Great British Energy, a publicly owned energy company
original.description: Great British Energy Act received royal assent 15 May 2025; the company is operational with up to £8.3bn of backing and its first projects announced (rooftop solar on 200 schools and 200 NHS sites).

retained.promise: Create Great British Energy, a publicly owned energy company
retained.description: Great British Energy Limited was incorporated on October 10, 2024. Its governance page records Royal Assent to the Great British Energy Act on May 15, 2025; company formation and legislation are distinct milestones.
evidence: GBE's governance page records incorporation in 2024, before the 2025 Act.

review.note: GBE's own governance page records incorporation October 10, 2024, separate from May 2025 legislation. This resolves the apparent 2024/2025 outcome contradiction, but original promise date/deadline still unsourced. Search text of statutory explanatory notes says April 15 while company says May 15; verify Act header before relying on explanatory-note date.

original.promise: Deliver 1.5 million new homes over the parliament via radical planning reform
original.description: The planning reform was delivered — Planning and Infrastructure Act received royal assent 18 Dec 2025 — but housing delivery has not come close to the required pace, and the 1.5m target is widely regarded as at risk.

retained.promise: Deliver 1.5 million new homes over the parliament via radical planning reform
retained.description: The Planning and Infrastructure Act received Royal Assent on December 18, 2025 as part of the government's plan to build 1.5 million homes during Parliament. Enactment does not establish the number of completed homes.
evidence: Official announcement confirms enactment and links it to the housing target.

review.note: Royal Assent December 18 confirmed. Planning legislation is an enabling action, not houses delivered; remove unsupported pace assessment unless statistical source added. Original placeholder pledge date and precise end-Parliament deadline unverified.

original.promise: Zeitenwende (27 Feb 2022): €100bn Bundeswehr special fund and reaching NATO's 2% of GDP defence spending
original.description: Germany met 2% of GDP in 2024 (first time since 1992) and 2.22% in 2025, but only about half of the €100bn fund had been drawn down by end-2025 and the Bundeswehr's readiness gaps (munitions, equipment) persisted, with the rebuild continuing under Merz.

retained.promise: Zeitenwende (27 Feb 2022): €100bn Bundeswehr special fund and reaching NATO's 2% of GDP defence spending
retained.description: Scholz announced a EUR100 billion Bundeswehr special fund and higher defence spending in his February 27, 2022 policy statement. Establishing the fund and spending its resources are distinct measures.
evidence: Retained from the existing collection; outcome evidence remains to be documented.

review.note: Speech is February 27, 2022, not January 2023. Creating special fund differs from drawing it down, and original spending pledge was sustained annual expenditure, not merely reaching it once. 2024/2025 percentages and drawdown require budget/NATO evidence.

original.promise: Pension reform raising the retirement age from 62 to 64
original.description: Passed on 16 Mar 2023 via Article 49.3 despite mass protests; the law remains in force through 2025–2026 despite repeal attempts.

retained.promise: Pension reform raising the retirement age from 62 to 64
retained.description: The 2023 pension-age reform was subsequently modified by the December 30, 2025 social-security financing law and May 2026 decrees. The age-64 schedule was shifted to the 1969 birth cohort rather than 1968.
evidence: Official parliamentary responses describe suspension provisions and their implementing decrees.

review.note: Parliamentary responses confirm 2025 legislation suspended/adjusted rollout and May 2026 implementing decrees. Existing claim that the 2023 schedule remained unchanged through 2026 is stale. Need original promise and enactment date; March 16 use of 49.3 is not final promulgation.

original.promise: Restore sound public finances / keep the deficit on a path toward the EU's 3% of GDP ceiling
original.description: The deficit was 5.8% of GDP in 2024 (up from 5.4% in 2023 and at risk of exceeding 6%), public debt reached 116.5% of GDP in 2025, and the 3% target is far out of reach.

retained.promise: Restore sound public finances / keep the deficit on a path toward the EU's 3% of GDP ceiling
retained.description: The deficit was 5.8% of GDP in 2024 (up from 5.4% in 2023 and at risk of exceeding 6%), public debt reached 116.5% of GDP in 2025, and the 3% target is far out of reach.
evidence: Retained from the existing collection; outcome evidence remains to be documented.

review.note: Current Reuters reporting describes a 2029 deficit target, not 2027. Need original dated promise and explicit postponement to adjudicate abandonment; forecasts cannot alone establish a future deadline missed. Exact debt/deficit vintage and definitions remain unverified.

original.promise: Increase medical school admissions by 2,000 per year to fix the doctor shortage (announced 6 Feb 2024)
original.description: The quota increase triggered a mass doctors' strike; the 2025 increase was cut to +1,500 (May 2024) and in April 2025 the government reverted the 2026 quota to the original 3,058 — the promise largely unravelled before his removal.

retained.promise: Increase medical school admissions by 2,000 per year to fix the doctor shortage (announced 6 Feb 2024)
retained.description: On April 17, 2025 the government announced that the 2026 medical-school quota would return to 3,058, the pre-expansion level.
evidence: Education ministry announcement and Yonhap coverage confirm the 2026 quota reversal on April 17, 2025.

review.note: Education ministry/ Yonhap confirm April 17, 2025 return to 3,058 for 2026. This is after the record's own April removal timing, so 'unravelled before removal' is not supported. Original February 6 announcement and exact 2025 increment need sources.

original.promise: Keep the federal carbon price as the cornerstone of climate policy
original.description: He carved out home heating oil (Oct 2023), and the consumer carbon tax was repealed outright on 1 Apr 2025 (prime-ministerial directive signed by Carney on 14 Mar 2025, weeks after Trudeau left office).

retained.promise: Keep the federal carbon price as the cornerstone of climate policy
retained.description: Canada ceased applying the federal consumer fuel charge from April 1, 2025 and removed the consumer-price requirement for provinces. This should not be described as repeal of every federal carbon-pricing mechanism.
evidence: Finance Canada's backgrounder specifies the consumer fuel charge and consumer-facing benchmark.

review.note: Official measure ceased consumer fuel charge, not all industrial carbon pricing. Original January 2023 promise/deadline not sourced. A successor's action must not be described as Trudeau's own implementation; March 14 was transition day, not weeks after departure.

original.promise: Cut immigration levels to ease housing and social pressures
original.description: Permanent-resident targets were cut from 500,000 to 395,000 (2025), 380,000 (2026) and 365,000 (2027), and the plans were implemented.

retained.promise: Cut immigration levels to ease housing and social pressures
retained.description: Permanent-resident targets were cut from 500,000 to 395,000 (2025), 380,000 (2026) and 365,000 (2027), and the plans were implemented.
evidence: Retained from the existing collection; outcome evidence remains to be documented.

review.note: Official 2024 plan supports reduced future targets. January 2023 attribution and actual 2025 admissions are not established; publishing targets does not prove they were implemented. Later 2026-2027 plans could revise the figures.

original.promise: Present major European defence funding proposals within 100 days of her second Commission — delivered as ReArm Europe
original.description: ReArm Europe was announced 4 Mar 2025: up to €800bn for defence, including a €150bn joint-loans facility, endorsed by the European Council on 6 Mar 2025 (later rebranded Readiness 2030).

retained.promise: Present major European defence funding proposals within 100 days of her second Commission — delivered as ReArm Europe
retained.description: The Commission's European Defence White Paper was issued on March 19, 2025 and provides the framework for ReArm Europe. The White Paper and financing-plan announcements are separate milestones.
evidence: Retained from the existing collection; outcome evidence remains to be documented.

review.note: White Paper is dated March 19, 2025 and distinguished from ReArm financing plan. Need original 100-day commitment/start point; January 2023 date cannot describe second Commission. Do not substitute an earlier funding announcement for a promised White Paper without checking scope.

original.promise: Allies must move to a 'wartime mindset' and raise defence spending far above 2% of GDP
original.description: The Hague Summit Declaration (25 Jun 2025) set a new 5%-of-GDP target for 2035 (at least 3.5% core defence + up to 1.5% defence-related spending), replacing the 2014 2% benchmark — all members except Spain signed on.

retained.promise: Allies must move to a 'wartime mindset' and raise defence spending far above 2% of GDP
retained.description: NATO Allies adopted the Hague declaration on June 25, 2025, committing to 5% of GDP annually by 2035, including 3.5% core defence and up to 1.5% related investment. Adoption is not proof of immediate spending delivery.
evidence: NATO reports Allied adoption without a Spain signatory exception.

review.note: NATO records collective adoption, not 'all except Spain signed'. Spain disputed its spending obligation but that differs from not adopting declaration. Agreement to 2035 spending is not actual expenditure by 2025; original Rutte speech/date unverified.

original.promise: We are going to have a 48-team World Cup.
original.description: FIFA Council unanimously voted to expand the World Cup to 48 teams (announced for 2026 after the 2022 tournament stayed at 32). The expanded 48-team tournament kicked off June 11, 2026 in North America.
evidence: FIFA Council unanimously voted for a 48-team format on 2017-01-10
2026 World Cup in USA/Canada/Mexico ran with 48 teams as promised

retained.promise: We are going to have a 48-team World Cup.
retained.description: FIFA Council unanimously voted to expand the World Cup to 48 teams (announced for 2026 after the 2022 tournament stayed at 32). The expanded 48-team tournament kicked off June 11, 2026 in North America.
evidence: FIFA Council unanimously voted for a 48-team format on 2017-01-10
2026 World Cup in USA/Canada/Mexico ran with 48 teams as promised

review.note: FIFA confirms January 10, 2017 expansion decision and June 11, 2026 scheduled opener. Retrieved schedule is prospective, not evidence the tournament actually ran. Need actual competition report and exact Infantino quote before full certification.

original.promise: The labor reforms will be completed by the time of the 2022 World Cup (as reported).
original.description: Qatar's World Cup organizers repeatedly promised major labor reforms for migrant workers before the 2022 tournament. The kafala sponsorship system was abolished (Sept 2020) and minimum wages introduced, but Amnesty International documented continued wage theft, unpaid recruitment fees and unsafe conditions through 2022-2024, and FIFA's promised workers' compensation fund launched only in 2023 at a fraction of reported needs.
evidence: Kafala abolished in September 2020 and wage protection reform passed
Amnesty International 2022 and 2024 reports document ongoing abuses and unpaid wages
FIFA announced a compensation fund for workers in 2022, but payouts were limited

retained.promise: The labor reforms will be completed by the time of the 2022 World Cup (as reported).
retained.description: Amnesty documented continuing gaps in remedy for World Cup workers. Its November 2024 response to FIFA's legacy fund said that fund did not provide the requested compensation for exploited workers.
evidence: Amnesty distinguished a FIFA legacy fund from a worker-compensation programme.

review.note: Amnesty's November 2024 account says FIFA legacy fund excluded compensation for exploited workers; the record's launched-2023 compensation-fund claim is unsupported. Original Al Thawadi quotation/date and full kafala abolition claim need primary legal/interview evidence.

original.promise: We want to study whether we can have a World Cup every two years (as reported).
original.description: FIFA's biennial World Cup campaign (pushed with Arsene Wenger from 2021) was formally studied and proposed, with a vote expected at the 2022 FIFA Congress. UEFA and CONMEBOL campaigned against it, the vote was postponed, and FIFA quietly abandoned the plan in 2023 — the World Cup remains quadrennial.
evidence: FIFA commissioned a feasibility study in 2021 and staged consultation sessions
Expected vote at 2022 FIFA Congress was dropped after UEFA/CONMEBOL opposition
No biennial World Cup adopted; 2026 and 2030 tournaments stay four years apart

retained.promise: We want to study whether we can have a World Cup every two years (as reported).
retained.description: FIFA's 2021 Congress requested a feasibility study of biennial World Cups. FIFA subsequently reported studies and consultations. This fulfills a study commitment, not a separate promise to adopt a biennial tournament.
evidence: FIFA's 2021 report documents the study request and resulting analysis.

review.note: Literal promise is to study feasibility. FIFA's annual report documents commissioned studies and consultations, so non-adoption does not make that study promise broken. Exact May 21 quotation and September 2022 deadline still need source.

original.promise: Paris 2024 will be the first Olympic Games with full gender parity on the field of play (as reported).
original.description: IOC pledged that Paris 2024 would be the first fully gender-balanced Games. The Paris 2024 Games fielded exactly 5,250 women and 5,250 men (50/50), fulfilling the target.
evidence: IOC confirmed equal number of female and male athlete slots at Paris 2024
Final quota breakdown: 5,250 women / 5,250 men

retained.promise: Paris 2024 will be the first Olympic Games with full gender parity on the field of play (as reported).
retained.description: Paris 2024 allocated equal female and male athlete quota places. Equal planned quotas should not be described as proof that the actual number of competing athletes was exactly 5,250 women and 5,250 men.
evidence: IOC's progress report identifies quota places as the parity indicator.

review.note: IOC report measures equal quota places, not proof exactly 5,250 of each gender actually competed. Original March 8 date and actual field require official participation table.

original.promise: I think that will happen and I believe it will happen in the next five to ten years (London franchise, as reported).
original.description: Goodell repeatedly called an NFL franchise in London 'inevitable' with a five-to-ten-year window from 2017. By the midpoint (2022) and through 2026, no London franchise has been awarded; the league has held International Series games but expansion remains undecided.
evidence: Goodell's 2017 comments at NFL owners meetings called London franchise inevitable
No expansion franchise awarded as of mid-2026; London team still 'under consideration'

retained.promise: I think that will happen and I believe it will happen in the next five to ten years (London franchise, as reported).
retained.description: Goodell repeatedly called an NFL franchise in London 'inevitable' with a five-to-ten-year window from 2017. By the midpoint (2022) and through 2026, no London franchise has been awarded; the league has held International Series games but expansion remains undecided.
evidence: Goodell's 2017 comments at NFL owners meetings called London franchise inevitable
No expansion franchise awarded as of mid-2026; London team still 'under consideration'

review.note: NFL source contains a conditional five-to-ten-year prediction, but 2017 date/exact wording not established. Even from 2017, upper endpoint is 2027, not October 2022; evaluating the midpoint as final deadline is invalid. Need original timestamp and current franchise evidence.

original.promise: We believe this will reduce average game time by roughly 25 minutes (pitch clock, as reported).
original.description: MLB adopted the pitch clock and other pace-of-play rules for the 2023 season, with Manfred promising dramatically shorter games. Average nine-inning game time fell from 3:04 in 2022 to 2:40 in 2023 — a 24-minute reduction.
evidence: Pitch clock implemented from opening day 2023
Average game time dropped 24 minutes from 3:04 (2022) to 2:40 (2023)

retained.promise: We believe this will reduce average game time by roughly 25 minutes (pitch clock, as reported).
retained.description: MLB adopted the pitch clock and other pace-of-play rules for the 2023 season, with Manfred promising dramatically shorter games. Average nine-inning game time fell from 3:04 in 2022 to 2:40 in 2023 — a 24-minute reduction.
evidence: Pitch clock implemented from opening day 2023
Average game time dropped 24 minutes from 3:04 (2022) to 2:40 (2023)

review.note: MLB supports reduction in game time during 2023, but retrieved September report is not full-season final result. Exact Manfred quote, September 13 announcement and promised 25-minute metric are unestablished.

original.promise: CNN+ will be the next generation of CNN — a premium streaming subscription service for news (as reported).
original.description: WarnerMedia unveiled CNN+ as a major direct-to-consumer news subscription business, launched March 29, 2022. Warner Bros. Discovery shut it down 26 days later (April 21, 2022), writing off hundreds of millions; the service had roughly 150,000 subscribers at closure, and staff were laid off.
evidence: CNN+ launched 2022-03-29 after $100M+ investment
WBD CEO David Zaslav ceased CNN+ operations on 2022-04-21; ~150K subscribers, product removed

retained.promise: CNN+ will be the next generation of CNN — a premium streaming subscription service for news (as reported).
retained.description: CNN+ launched on March 29, 2022. Warner Bros. Discovery announced its closure on April 21; announcement and final service shutdown were different dates.
evidence: April 21 reporting described cessation as forthcoming, not already completed.

review.note: April 21 was shutdown announcement, not actual cessation. Original November 17 quote/deadline and final shutdown day need source; a pledge to launch differs from a promise of commercial longevity. CNN page also has an apparent 2021 dateline typo despite 2022 heading.

original.promise: We're targeting 150 million DTC subscribers by 2025 (as reported).
original.description: At its February 2022 investor day, Paramount projected 150 million global direct-to-consumer subscribers by 2025. Paramount+ ended 2025 with roughly 70-75 million subscribers; the company was sold to Skydance in 2025, far short of target.
evidence: Investor Day guidance of 150M DTC subs by 2025 reported by Variety/CNBC
Paramount+ subscriber base stayed near 70M through 2024-2025

retained.promise: We're targeting 150 million DTC subscribers by 2025 (as reported).
retained.description: At its February 2022 investor day, Paramount projected 150 million global direct-to-consumer subscribers by 2025. Paramount+ ended 2025 with roughly 70-75 million subscribers; the company was sold to Skydance in 2025, far short of target.
evidence: Investor Day guidance of 150M DTC subs by 2025 reported by Variety/CNBC
Paramount+ subscriber base stayed near 70M through 2024-2025

review.note: Contemporaneous report identifies a 100m-by-2024 target, not 150m-by-2025. Need primary investor transcript to confirm global/US scope because retrieved report's geography also needs corroboration. Paramount+ alone is not necessarily all DTC subscriptions.

original.promise: We expect Peacock to reach 30 to 35 million subscribers by 2024 (as reported).
original.description: At Comcast's June 2021 investor day, NBCUniversal guided Peacock to 30-35 million paid subscribers by end of 2024. Peacock finished 2024 with roughly 36 million paid subscribers, meeting the target.
evidence: Comcast Investor Day 2021 guidance of 30-35M Peacock subs by 2024
Peacock reported ~36M paid subscribers at end of 2024

retained.promise: We expect Peacock to reach 30 to 35 million subscribers by 2024 (as reported).
retained.description: At Comcast's June 2021 investor day, NBCUniversal guided Peacock to 30-35 million paid subscribers by end of 2024. Peacock finished 2024 with roughly 36 million paid subscribers, meeting the target.
evidence: Comcast Investor Day 2021 guidance of 30-35M Peacock subs by 2024
Peacock reported ~36M paid subscribers at end of 2024

review.note: Comcast SEC filing confirms 36m paid Peacock subscribers at end-2024. Original June 22 2021 event/quote and 30-35m paid versus active-account measure remain unsupported.

original.role: CEO, The New York Times Company
original.promise: We intend to reach 10 million subscriptions by 2025 (as reported).
original.description: NYT's May 2020 strategic report set a goal of 10 million total subscriptions by 2025, powered by digital growth. The company passed 10.5 million subscriptions in Q4 2024, ahead of the deadline.
evidence: NYT 2020 strategy report set 10M subscription goal by 2025

original.promise: Instinct MI450 'Helios' (CDNA Next) to ship in 2026 with roughly 12x the inference performance of MI300X; AI accelerator market to reach $500 billion by 2028
original.description: At CES 2025, Su unveiled AMD's 2025-2026 accelerator roadmap: MI350 (mid-2025) and the MI450 'Helios' family for 2026 with a claimed ~12x inference uplift over MI300X, plus a $500B AI-accelerator TAM forecast by 2028. MI350X shipped June 2025 as promised; MI450/Helios was still unreleased as of mid-2026 (expected 2H 2026).
evidence: AMD CES 2025 announcement of MI450 'Helios' for 2026 and $500B TAM by 2028
MI350X/MI355X launched June 2025 (Wikipedia: AMD Instinct)
No MI450/Helios release confirmed as of July 2026

retained.promise: AMD previewed Helios, a rack-scale system based on its MI400-series GPUs.
retained.description: AMD's June announcement described Helios and engineering performance projections. Those projections are not measured shipping-product performance.
evidence: The primary June 12 announcement identifies Helios and MI400.
Outcome not established as of 2026-09-21: a product page and projections do not independently establish a shipment date.

review.note: AMD's June 12, 2025 announcement supports a Helios preview using MI400-series GPUs, with projected MoE inference performance versus MI355X, not the claimed CES January MI450/12x-MI300X announcement. A supported 2026 shipment timetable is still required; do not transfer a forecast between different chips or performance baselines.

original.promise: GM expected Cruise to resume robotaxi operations in 2024 after the 2023 pause
original.description: After the Oct 2023 pedestrian-dragging incident and permit suspensions, Barra signaled Cruise would relaunch driverless operations in 2024 (succeeding Kyle Vogt's earlier goals, including Cruise's 'adding $1 billion in revenue by 2025' target from Sept 2022). Instead, GM stopped funding the Cruise robotaxi program on Dec 10, 2024, folding the unit into GM's driver-assistance work; robotaxis never resumed under Cruise.
evidence: Reuters (Jan 2024): GM expected Cruise relaunch during 2024
GM stopped funding Cruise robotaxi program Dec 2024 (Wikipedia: Cruise)
Vogt-era goal: '$1 billion in revenue by 2025 and $50 billion by 2030' (The Verge, 2022) never approached

retained.promise: GM expected Cruise to resume robotaxi operations in 2024 after the 2023 pause
retained.description: GM announced on December 10, 2024 that it would stop funding Cruise robotaxi development and combine technical work with its personal-vehicle autonomous-driving efforts.
evidence: GM's primary notice establishes the funding and development decision.
Outcome not established as of 2026-09-21 for the alleged relaunch commitment: the exact promised operating mode and dated statement were not retrieved.

review.note: GM's primary December 10 notice establishes withdrawal of robotaxi-development funding, not by itself the alleged January 30 promise to resume driverless service. Testing, supervised operation and commercial driverless service are distinct. The unrelated revenue targets and categorical no-resumption assertion are removed.

original.promise: BotQ factory would build 12,000 humanoid robots per year; Figure 03 shipping in 2025
original.description: Adcock announced the 'BotQ' humanoid factory (early 2025) targeting 12,000 units/year and promised Figure 03 for 2025, building on the BMW manufacturing deployment (deal announced Jan 2024). Figure 03 did launch (Oct 2025) and BMW work proceeded, but by June 2026 only ~740 robots were operating — an order of magnitude below the 12k/year capacity promise.
evidence: BotQ announced early 2025, targeting 12,000 humanoids/year (Wikipedia: Figure AI)
Figure 03 released October 2025
June 2026: ~740 robots operating vs ~600 humans at Figure (Wikipedia)

retained.promise: Figure described BotQ's first-generation manufacturing line as designed for capacity of up to 12,000 humanoid robots per year.
retained.description: The BotQ notice describes planned manufacturing capacity. Figure separately introduced Figure 03 on October 9, 2025; neither fact establishes annual production volume.
evidence: Figure's dated BotQ announcement specifies capacity, not a deployment quota.
Outcome not established as of 2026-09-21: the checked notices do not establish demonstrated annual throughput or a December 2026 deadline.

review.note: The BotQ announcement is March 15, 2025, not February 1. It describes capacity of up to 12,000 a year, not a promise to produce or deploy that many by December 2026. Figure 03 was introduced October 9, but launch is not shipment. An installed-robot count cannot measure manufacturing capacity; the 740 figure is unverified.

original.promise: A legally binding post-Kyoto climate agreement to be concluded at COP15 in Copenhagen by the end of 2009.
original.description: The Bali Roadmap set COP15 as the deadline for a post-2012 agreement. COP15 ended without a binding treaty - only the non-binding Copenhagen Accord was 'taken note of'. A binding successor came only with the Paris Agreement in December 2015, six years late.
evidence: COP15 (Dec 2009) produced no legally binding instrument; the Copenhagen Accord was a 2-page political deal 'taken note of' by the COP
Binding post-Kyoto regime only adopted at Paris, 12 December 2015

retained.promise: The Bali Action Plan directed its working group to complete its work in 2009 and present an agreed outcome to COP15.
retained.description: COP15 extended the working group's mandate instead of completing the process in 2009. The Bali decision did not expressly guarantee a legally binding treaty.
evidence: Decision 1/CP.13 establishes the 2009 work-completion target.
Decision 1/CP.15 extends the working group's mandate; the Accord is a separate decision.

review.note: The Bali decision calls for an agreed outcome and completion of the working group's work in 2009, not expressly a legally binding treaty. COP15's decision extends that group's mandate, while the Accord is only noted. December 18 was a scheduled endpoint; the meeting continued into December 19. The original Bali adoption UTC date still needs confirmation.

original.promise: No new coal plants after the end of this year.
original.description: Guterres' call at the Climate Ambition Summit (12 Dec 2020) - repeated at COP26 - was not heeded. New coal construction continued, led by China, and global coal capacity kept growing through 2025.
evidence: China approved and continued building well over 100 GW of new coal capacity after 2021 (Global Energy Monitor)
Global installed coal capacity grew in 2022-2025; Guterres had to repeat the demand at COP26 and COP27

retained.promise: No new coal plants after the end of this year.

evidence: China approved and continued building well over 100 GW of new coal capacity after 2021 (Global Energy Monitor)
Global installed coal capacity grew in 2022-2025; Guterres had to repeat the demand at COP26 and COP27

review.note: The supplied UN speech URL returned an access challenge. Search found a December 12 press encounter and an April 2021 climate press conference, but not the claimed exact December 2020 quotation. 'This year' on a 2020 date is inconsistent with a 2021 deadline unless the wording or date is repaired. This is also a call on governments, not Guterres's unilateral deliverable; the specific post-deadline coal claims were not verified.

sources.name: UN supplied speech URL, access challenge

original.promise: Reduce the net carbon intensity of our energy products by 20% by 2030 and 45% by 2035, versus 2016 (net zero by 2050).
original.description: Shell's 2021 Energy Transition Strategy set 20% (2030) and 45% (2035) intensity cuts. On 14 June 2023 CEO Wael Sawan scrapped the 2035 target outright and cut the 2030 target to 9-12% - the most high-profile corporate climate target reversal of its era (reneged before the deadline).
evidence: 14 June 2023 update: 2035 target removed; 2030 target weakened from 20% to 9-12%
Sawan also dropped Shell's plan to reduce oil production every year through the decade (Wikipedia: Wael Sawan)
Court-ordered 45% cut (Milieudefensie) later overturned on appeal, Nov 2024

retained.promise: Reduce the net carbon intensity of our energy products by 20% by 2030 and 45% by 2035, versus 2016 (net zero by 2050).
retained.description: Shell retired its 45% net-carbon-intensity reduction target for 2035 on 14 March 2024 and revised its 2030 target from 20% to 15-20%, relative to 2016.
evidence: Shell's 2024 strategy explicitly retires the 2035 intensity target and revises the 2030 range.

review.note: The rollback occurred on 14 March 2024, not 14 June 2023. The revised 2030 intensity range was 15-20%, not 9-12% (the latter was a 2024 target). The 2035 target was retired. Exact 2021 announcement day and ancillary court claim not established; remove superlative.

original.promise: BP will reduce oil and gas production by 40% by 2030 versus 2019.
original.description: Looney's February 2020 'reinvent BP' strategy committed to a 40% oil and gas production cut by 2030. In February 2023, citing energy security and profits, BP abandoned the target and said it would grow oil and gas production through the decade (reneged before the deadline).
evidence: Feb 2023: Looney scrapped the 40% cut, saying BP would 'invest more in oil and gas than previously planned'
Feb 2025 reset under Auchincloss: oil & gas spending raised ~20% to ~$10bn/yr
Greenpeace called the reversal 'proof that fossil fuel companies can't or won't be part of climate crisis solutions' (Wikipedia BP)

retained.promise: BP will reduce oil and gas production by 40% by 2030 versus 2019.
retained.description: BP's August 2020 strategy targeted a 40% reduction in oil and gas production by 2030. Its February 2025 strategy reset instead emphasized increasing oil and gas production and investment.
evidence: BP's 2020 strategy set the 40% reduction goal.
BP's February 2025 reset shifted investment and planned production toward oil and gas.

review.note: The 40% production target belongs to the August 2020 strategy, not the February net-zero announcement. The 2023 step was a weakening to 25%, not an immediate growth pledge; the 2025 reset increased planned production. This is a withdrawn-target judgment, not a measured 2030 outcome.

original.promise: Increase annual low carbon investment tenfold to around $5 billion a year by 2030.
original.description: BP's 2020 strategy promised $5bn/yr low-carbon spend by 2030. On 26 February 2025 CEO Murray Auchincloss cut planned low-carbon investment by more than $5bn/yr to $1.5-2bn/yr and dropped the renewable power and EV-charging targets entirely - abandoning the trajectory mid-course.
evidence: Feb 2025: low-carbon spend cut to $1.5-2bn/yr, >$5bn reduction vs previous plan (Wikipedia BP)
BP's 2030 renewables generation and 10x EV-charging targets dropped in the same reset
Transition spending in 2023-2024 had already run well below the $5bn trajectory

retained.promise: Increase annual low carbon investment tenfold to around $5 billion a year by 2030.
retained.description: BP's August 2020 strategy targeted roughly $5 billion of annual low-carbon investment by 2030. In February 2025 BP reset transition-business investment to $1.5-2 billion annually, more than $5 billion below its intervening guidance.
evidence: BP's August 2020 strategy set a tenfold increase in low-carbon investment.
The February 2025 reset reduced planned transition investment while increasing oil and gas investment.

review.note: Announcement date is August 2020. The $5bn reduction in 2025 is relative to intervening guidance, not subtraction from the original $5bn target. Original exact wording is a paraphrase. The assertion about 2023-24 spending and dropping all EV charging targets was not supported.

original.promise: Reach 35 GW of gross renewable electricity capacity by 2025 (raised to 60 GW at COP26), heading toward 100 GW by 2030.

evidence: ~30 GW gross renewables at end-2024 (TotalEnergies Q4 2024 release) vs 60 GW raised target
Original 35 GW target reached only around the December 2025 deadline
100 GW by 2030 target also re-scoped as the company pivoted back toward LNG

evidence: The 2025 sustainability report retains the 35 GW 2025 target.
The February 2026 results presentation reports 34 GW at year-end 2025.

review.note: Primary reporting retains a 35 GW 2025 goal; no support found for a COP26 increase to 60 GW. Reported year-end capacities were 26 GW (2024) and 34 GW (2025), not 30 and 35. Exact original announcement date remains unestablished.

original.promise: Phase out coal completely by 2023 - a decade ahead of the Danish government's 2030 deadline.
original.description: Ørsted decided in 2017 to abandon coal and confirmed a 2023 exit. It closed its last coal unit (Studstrupværket) in August 2023, on schedule - the first major energy company to complete the coal-to-renewables transition.

Coal share of generation fell from ~50% (2006) to zero by 2023
Wikipedia Ørsted: coal phase-out decision taken in 2017

retained.promise: Phase out coal completely by 2023 - a decade ahead of the Danish government's 2030 deadline.

evidence: Orsted's August 2024 release identifies the final coal closure and the government-directed extension.

review.note: Official release identifies Esbjerg, not Studstrup, as the final coal-fired plant and 31 August 2024 as the closure date. Government-directed extension caused delay from the original 2023 goal. Original exact pledge day remains unverified; 2023 is seven, not ten, years before 2030.

original.promise: Be carbon neutral in own operations and energy generation by 2025, with 95% of energy from renewables by 2023 and 99% by 2025.

Ørsted 2024/2025 reporting confirms carbon neutrality in own operations and generation, with carbon intensity down ~99% vs 2006

retained.promise: Be carbon neutral in own operations and energy generation by 2025, with 95% of energy from renewables by 2023 and 99% by 2025.
retained.description: Orsted reports meeting its 99% renewable-generation share and scope 1-2 emissions-intensity target in 2025. Residual emissions remain; these milestones should not be described as proof of zero emissions.
evidence: Orsted reports meeting a 10 g CO2e/kWh scope 1-2 intensity target and 99% renewable share in 2025.

review.note: Company reporting supports 99% renewable generation and the scope 1-2 intensity target in 2025, not zero emissions or carbon neutrality in 2024. Residual emissions remain; 2018 announcement day and 2023 subtarget need separate evidence.

original.promise: Shut down all German nuclear power plants by 2022 (decision of 30 May 2011).

evidence: Wikipedia Nuclear power in Germany: final three plants 'shut down on 15 April 2023', extended by Scholz decree in late 2022
Eight of seventeen reactors had closed by August 2011; the phase-out was broadly achieved with a short delay

review.note: Last commercial reactors closed 15 April 2023 after a legislated extension beyond end-2022. Full completion after the original deadline is kept (delayed), not partial. Exact May 2011 pledge day was not independently established here.

Unit 1 closed 22 February 2020; Unit 2 closed 29 June 2020

Unit 1 closed 22 February 2020; Unit 2 closed 29 June 2020

original.promise: Reduce California's greenhouse gas emissions to 1990 levels by 2020 (statutory deadline 31 December 2020).
original.description: California's landmark AB 32 set a 2020 target of returning to 1990 emission levels (431 MMTCO2e). CARB data show California met the target in 2016 - four years early - while the economy grew.

Wikipedia AB 32: statutory deadline 31 December 2020; goal met on schedule/early

retained.promise: Reduce California's greenhouse gas emissions to 1990 levels by 2020 (statutory deadline 31 December 2020).

review.note: The original report did identify 2016. CARB's revised inventory says the 431 MMT threshold was met in 2014 instead. Keep reporting vintage explicit. Exact signing day remains to be checked.

original.promise: India will install 175 GW of renewable energy by 2022, including 100 GW of solar.
original.description: Modi announced the 175 GW-by-2022 goal (100 GW solar) at COP21 and it became the JNNSM target. India reached only ~60-67 GW of solar by end-2022 (the 100 GW mark was hit only on 31 January 2025) and ~120 GW of total renewables - both targets missed by wide margins.
evidence: Wikipedia Solar power in India: 66,780 MW solar by 31 March 2023 (~60 GW at end-2022) vs 100 GW; 'widely missed by 40,000 MW shortfall'
100 GW solar reached 31 January 2025 - over two years late; rooftop solar (40 GW of the target) badly underperformed
Total renewables ~120 GW at end-2022 vs 175 GW target

retained.promise: India will install 175 GW of renewable energy by 2022, including 100 GW of solar.

evidence: The NITI Aayog roadmap sets out the 175 GW target and technology components.
Parliamentary committee coverage reports 120.90 GW by the deadline.

review.note: The target excludes large hydro; mixing broad renewable totals changes the apparent shortfall. Parliamentary-report coverage gives 120.90 GW at 31 December 2022. Exact COP21 wording/day and later 100 GW solar milestone remain unverified.

original.promise: The Government must act now to halt biodiversity loss and reduce net greenhouse gas emissions to zero by 2025.

evidence: Wikipedia Extinction Rebellion: Demand 2 = 'reduce greenhouse gas emissions to net-zero by 2025' (Oct 2018)
UK 2024/2025 emissions still ~370 MtCO2e, far from zero (DESNZ statistics)
UK net-zero law targets 2050, not 2025; XR later softened the demand

retained.promise: The Government must act now to halt biodiversity loss and reduce net greenhouse gas emissions to zero by 2025.
retained.description: Extinction Rebellion demanded that the UK government achieve net-zero emissions by 2025. This was an advocacy demand, not a government commitment or a promise by XR to deliver the outcome.
evidence: XR's January 2025 statement reiterates the demand and says the movement is not backing down.

review.note: This is a demand directed at government, not XR's promise to deliver UK net zero. The source also contradicts the claim that XR had backed down in 2025. Recommend excluding from promise scoring; schema has no not-a-promise status. Exact founding-day wording remains unresolved.

original.role: UN Special Envoy for Climate Action, co-chair of GFANZ (COP26)

Instead the alliance collapsed: Vanguard left in 2022, and BlackRock, JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs and State Street exited the Net-Zero Asset Managers initiative in Dec 2024-Jan 2025.
evidence: Wikipedia GFANZ: Race to Zero membership required '2030 interim target setting'; first defections over fossil-fuel rules in 2022
NZAM exodus Dec 2024-Jan 2025: BlackRock, JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs, State Street quit; hundreds of managers left in 2024

retained.role: UN Special Envoy for Climate Action, co-chair of GFANZ (COP26)
retained.promise: GFANZ firms representing $130 trillion in assets commit to net zero by 2050, with 2030 interim targets and credible transition plans within 12 months.
retained.description: GFANZ announced in November 2021 that more than 450 financial firms representing over $130 trillion in assets had net-zero commitments. The 2025 update reports a voluntary transition-planning framework and a restructuring.

review.note: November 2021 announcement supports 450+ firms and $130tn represented assets, not cash pledged for investment. 2025 primary update describes restructuring, not wholesale collapse. 2024 due date lacks derivation; bank/asset-manager alliances are conflated in original exits list. A single broken status for all firms is not established.

original.promise: June 19, 2013: if the labor market improved as forecast, the Fed would 'moderate the monthly pace of purchases later this year' and 'likely conclude purchases around the middle of 2014' (QE3 taper guidance)
original.description: Taper announced Dec 18, 2013; QE3 asset purchases ended Oct 29, 2014
