review.note: The proposal and August 15 date are supported. A December 31 review horizon is not an announced deadline and cannot be published as one. Remove the long quotation and distinguish proposing discussion from promising a peace agreement.

original.promise: Provide free online coaching for various competitive examinations for the youth
original.description: In his Independence Day 2026 address from the Red Fort on August 15, Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced free online coaching for students preparing for competitive examinations, saying coaching classes had become a burden on poor and middle-class families. He cited India's digital public infrastructure and talented teachers as the basis for the initiative. No formal start deadline was announced; one year from the pledge is used as a review horizon.
evidence: August 15, 2026 Independence Day speech announcing free online coaching
Announcement framed as immediate government decision; no explicit rollout date

retained.promise: Provide free online coaching for various competitive examinations for the youth
retained.description: Modi announced free online coaching for competitive examinations on August 15, 2026, using digital public infrastructure and teachers to build a coaching network.
evidence: The official announcement contains no explicit coaching rollout deadline.

review.note: The free-coaching announcement is supported, but the one-year deadline belongs to AI training, not coaching. An editorial review anniversary must not become a promised delivery date.

original.promise: Seven to eight new semiconductor production plants will become operational within the next one to two years
original.description: In his Independence Day 2026 address from the Red Fort on August 15, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said 7-8 new semiconductor production plants are expected to become operational within the next one to two years, strengthening India's domestic chip manufacturing capability as part of the self-reliance push. The one-to-two-year timeline is used to set the review horizon.
evidence: August 15, 2026 Independence Day speech announcing 7-8 new semiconductor plants in 1-2 years
Timeline of 1-2 years implies operational by August 2028 at the latest

retained.promise: Seven to eight new semiconductor production plants will become operational within the next one to two years
retained.description: In his Independence Day 2026 address from the Red Fort on August 15, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said 7-8 new semiconductor production plants are expected to become operational within the next one to two years, strengthening India's domestic chip manufacturing capability as part of the self-reliance push. The one-to-two-year timeline is used to set the review horizon.
evidence: August 15, 2026 Independence Day speech announcing 7-8 new semiconductor plants in 1-2 years
Timeline of 1-2 years implies operational by August 2028 at the latest

review.note: Official sources conflict: the summary says 7-8 plants in 1-2 years, while the English speech transcript says another five, seven or eight plants over seven to eight years. Neither discrepancy can be resolved by selecting the more convenient text. Audio or original-language transcript verification is needed before a numeric deadline can be certified.

original.promise: Nvidia will raise over $500 billion in third-party capital for AI infrastructure through compute financing platforms with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR
original.description: On August 10, 2026, Nvidia signed memorandums of understanding with six major financial institutions - Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR - to launch compute financing platforms aimed at raising more than $500 billion in third-party capital for AI infrastructure. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said the company has the option to backstop up to $125 billion (25%) of the potential deals. No deployment timetable was disclosed; the end of 2028 is used as a review horizon.
evidence: MOUs with six firms announced August 10, 2026; Reuters and CNN coverage August 11-12
No timetable disclosed; Huang confirmed up to $125 billion Nvidia backstop option

retained.promise: Establish compute-financing partnerships aiming to mobilize more than USD 500 billion of third-party capital over time
retained.description: NVIDIA announced MOUs with six financial institutions on August 10, 2026. The contemplated financing is third-party capital, and NVIDIA's potential backstop is optional.
evidence: The company announcement and Reuters report establish the partnerships but no completion timetable.

review.note: Announcement and prospective financing scale are supported. Reuters explicitly says no deployment timetable was disclosed; December 2028 is an editorial horizon. MOUs and an optional backstop do not guarantee fundraising.

original.role: President and CEO of Dangote Group
original.promise: Invest $2 billion in The Gambia, including a 250 MW solar power plant and a modern petroleum products storage terminal
original.description: President Adama Barrow announced that Aliko Dangote committed to invest US$2 billion in The Gambia following a meeting in Banjul on July 7, 2026, on the sidelines of the African Caucus. The pledge covers a 250 MW solar power plant and a modern petroleum products storage terminal. The agreement remains preliminary: binding agreements, technical and feasibility studies, and implementation structures still need to be finalized, and no construction timeline or funding breakdown was disclosed; the end of 2029 is used as a review horizon.
evidence: Announced by President Barrow after July 7, 2026 Banjul meeting; reported July 9, 2026
Preliminary commitment; no construction timeline disclosed

retained.role: President and CEO of Dangote Group
retained.promise: Invest $2 billion in The Gambia, including a 250 MW solar power plant and a modern petroleum products storage terminal
retained.description: President Barrow announced on July 7, 2026 that Dangote had committed USD 2 billion for a 250 MW solar plant and a fuel tank farm in The Gambia.
evidence: The presidency describes a commitment and proposed projects, not completed investment or a dated construction schedule.

review.note: The presidency confirms the July 7 announcement, amount and projects. No construction or full-investment completion deadline is stated; December 2029 remains unsupported.

original.role: Government of Hungary / EU Recovery and Resilience Facility
original.promise: Complete all milestones and targets required to unlock the full 10 billion euros in EU recovery funds by August 31, 2026
original.description: The Tisza government, elected in April 2026, is racing to document compliance with the EU's Recovery and Resilience Facility milestones before the August 31, 2026 deadline to unlock about 10 billion euros in previously frozen funds (roughly 6.5 billion in grants and 3.5 billion in soft loans). Transport and Investment Minister David Vitezy said on August 15 the government was working to recover the full amount, including reapplying in Brussels after years of blocked funds under the previous government.
evidence: Government said on Aug 31 it had met all conditions to unlock the full 10 billion euros in EU recovery funds (Euronews)
Christian Science Monitor reported Hungary fulfilled all EU requirements needed to unlock the funds
Disbursement remains subject to European Commission assessment of the evidence Hungary submitted by the deadline (mreast.eu, Sept)

retained.role: Government of Hungary / EU Recovery and Resilience Facility
retained.promise: Complete all milestones and targets required to unlock the full 10 billion euros in EU recovery funds by August 31, 2026
retained.description: Hungary sought to complete reforms and investments for approximately EUR 10 billion of recovery funding by the EU's end-August deadline. The government said on August 31 that it had met the conditions.
evidence: Outcome not established as of 2026-09-21: the retrieved reporting records Hungary's self-assessment, not the Commission's final acceptance of every milestone.

review.note: The EU confirms the August 31 milestone deadline. A government claim of compliance is not Commission acceptance. The original August 13 promise date was not established; August 24 coverage alone cannot date the earlier commitment.

original.role: Nvidia / OpenAI Ohio data center financing
original.promise: Provide a financial guarantee for OpenAI's Ohio data center project, planned at up to $250 billion and scaled back to under $120 billion covering only the first phase
original.description: Nvidia and OpenAI were nearing an agreement in mid-August 2026 under which the chipmaker would provide a financial backstop for OpenAI's 10-gigawatt Ohio data center campus developed with SoftBank's SB Energy. The Wall Street Journal reported that the planned guarantee was cut from about $250 billion to below $120 billion, covering only the first phase of the project, as Nvidia shifted AI financing risk toward a broader $500 billion compute-financing platform. No completion deadline was disclosed; end of 2027 is used as a review horizon.
evidence: WSJ report (August 13-14, 2026): guarantee scaled back from ~$250 billion to under $120 billion
Reuters/ET and edgen.tech: backstop now covers only phase 1 of the 10-GW Ohio campus

retained.role: Nvidia / OpenAI Ohio data center financing
retained.promise: Provide a financial guarantee for OpenAI's Ohio data center project, planned at up to $250 billion and scaled back to under $120 billion covering only the first phase
retained.description: Reuters reported a contemplated Ohio data-centre guarantee on August 14. NVIDIA's subsequent quarterly filing confirmed August credit-support guarantees with SB Energy covering approximately 4.25 GW of IT load.
evidence: The filing establishes entered guarantees, but not the original asserted announcement date, larger contractual obligation or 2027 deadline.

review.note: August 14 was reporting about negotiations, not a dated public USD 250 billion promise. The later filing confirms August guarantees for about 4.25 GW with SB Energy. No 2027 completion deadline is supported; a smaller discussed guarantee is not proof of partial fulfillment of a binding larger promise.

original.promise: Invest $51 billion in the Argentina LNG project under the RIGI large-investment incentive regime to export gas from Vaca Muerta
original.description: On August 14, 2026, YPF announced it would file its Argentina LNG project under the Large Investment Incentive Regime (RIGI), the largest RIGI application to date at $51 billion, in a project developed with ENI and XRG to export liquefied natural gas from the Vaca Muerta formation. The project aims to position Argentina as a major LNG exporter; no completion date was disclosed, so end of 2032 is used as a review horizon.
evidence: YPF announced the RIGI filing on August 14, 2026
Largest-ever RIGI project; developed with ENI and XRG for Vaca Muerta gas exports

retained.promise: Invest $51 billion in the Argentina LNG project under the RIGI large-investment incentive regime to export gas from Vaca Muerta
retained.description: YPF, Eni and XRG sought RIGI treatment for the Argentina LNG project, involving proposed investment of USD 51 billion and Vaca Muerta resources.
evidence: YPF announced the RIGI filing on August 14, 2026
Largest-ever RIGI project; developed with ENI and XRG for Vaca Muerta gas exports

review.note: Eni's August 14 release confirms the partners' application; EFE says the announcement occurred Thursday August 13. No exact UTC timing reconciles those dates, and no deadline for investing the whole USD 51 billion is established. RIGI application is not final investment approval.

original.promise: Return up to $80 billion to shareholders this year through dividends and share buybacks
original.description: Samsung Electronics announced on August 20, 2026 that it expects shareholder returns of up to $80 billion (110 trillion won) this year through dividends and record share buybacks, in a push to boost investor confidence. The program runs through the end of 2026.
evidence: Announced August 20-21, 2026; up to 110 trillion won in returns
Program runs through end of 2026

retained.promise: Estimate KRW 90 trillion to KRW 110 trillion in shareholder returns attributable to the 2026 plan
retained.description: Samsung's board approved an estimated return plan on August 21, 2026. Some cash-dividend details were to be finalized in October, and remaining returns after confirmation of annual performance in January 2027.
evidence: The primary release distinguishes estimated returns, later Board decisions and a separate employee-compensation buyback.

review.note: Board approval and official announcement were August 21, not August 20. Returns attributed to 2026 are not all payable by December 31: the remainder is to be determined in January 2027. Do not replace an unsupported payment deadline with the date of a determination meeting.

original.promise: Strike a $7 billion licensing and investment deal with AI startup Poolside
original.description: Nvidia reportedly struck a $7 billion licensing and investment deal with AI startup Poolside in late August 2026, a licensing playbook that sidesteps acquisition scrutiny. The deal targets dominance against rivals such as DeepSeek and OpenAI. No completion deadline was disclosed; end of 2027 is used as a review horizon.
evidence: Reported around August 22-24, 2026; $7 billion licensing and investment deal
Deal described as sidestepping acquisition scrutiny; targets DeepSeek/OpenAI

retained.promise: Strike a $7 billion licensing and investment deal with AI startup Poolside
retained.description: Reporting described a Poolside technology-licensing and investment arrangement, rather than an acquisition. The claimed antitrust motivation and competitive dominance are not established contractual commitments.
evidence: Reported around August 22-24, 2026; $7 billion licensing and investment deal
Deal described as sidestepping acquisition scrutiny; targets DeepSeek/OpenAI

review.note: Reporting distinguishes a USD 6 billion licence from a USD 1 billion equity investment. The exact August 22 agreement date and a contractual completion deadline were not established; investor distribution by end-2027 is not the same as NVIDIA's deadline to strike the deal. Yahoo full text returned 429; do not treat report timestamps as signing dates.

original.role: Government of Senegal / International Monetary Fund
original.promise: Reach a US$2.2 billion, 36-month IMF-supported programme to restore debt sustainability and support economic reforms
original.description: IMF staff reached a staff-level agreement with Senegal on September 1, 2026, for a new US$2.2 billion, 36-month loan programme supporting economic reforms, after an earlier arrangement was suspended over previously unreported government debt. Senegal agreed to restore debt sustainability under the programme, which still requires approval by the IMF Executive Board. End of the programme is used as the review horizon.
evidence: Staff-level agreement announced Sept 1, 2026, covering US$2.2 billion over 36 months (Bloomberg)
Senegal agreed to restore debt sustainability in return for the IMF programme (CNBC Africa)

retained.role: Government of Senegal / International Monetary Fund
retained.promise: Seek approval of a proposed 36-month IMF Extended Credit Facility of about USD 2.2 billion
retained.description: Senegal and IMF staff reached an agreement on key policies on September 1, 2026, subject to the Fund's approval process.
evidence: The IMF announcement is a staff-level agreement, not Board approval or disbursement of the whole programme.

review.note: The IMF confirms September 1 staff-level agreement and a proposed 36-month USD 2.2 billion arrangement. This is conditional on approval; programme expiry cannot be calculated from the staff-agreement day before Board approval sets the arrangement start.

original.promise: Develop the joint Freyja anti-ballistic missile programme with partner governments and companies
original.description: Zelenskyy announced on 7 September 2026 new steps toward developing the Freyja anti-ballistic missile programme, saying meetings would soon take place between the governments and companies involved and that long-range capabilities were also being developed. No completion deadline was disclosed; end of 2027 is used as a review horizon.
evidence: Zelenskyy said meetings on Freyja would take place soon (Ukrinform)
RBC-Ukraine reported new steps unveiled for the Freyja anti-ballistic programme

retained.promise: Develop the joint Freyja anti-ballistic missile programme with partner governments and companies
retained.description: Zelenskyy said on September 7 that meetings with partners involved in the joint Freyja programme would take place soon. Ukraine's security council reported an Oslo meeting on implementation on September 9.
evidence: The sources document meetings and development cooperation without a completed-system delivery deadline.

review.note: September 7 statement concerns forthcoming partner meetings, not completion by December 2027. A September 9 Oslo meeting shows activity, not a deployed anti-ballistic capability. No development deadline was established.

sources.name: Ukraine National Security and Defence Council

original.promise: Present Argentina's 2027 budget to Congress by the statutory deadline
original.description: President Milei's cabinet met on 7 September 2026 with the 2027 budget among the agenda items, and he was due to meet libertarian legislators hours before presenting the budget. Under Argentine law the executive must send its budget proposal to Congress by 15 September.
evidence: Milei convened the cabinet on the 2027 budget (Infobae, Sept 7)
MDZ reported Milei would meet legislators hours before presenting the 2027 budget

retained.promise: Present Argentina's 2027 budget to Congress by the statutory deadline
retained.description: The Argentine government submitted the 2027 budget proposal to Congress on September 15, 2026, the reported statutory deadline.
evidence: Chequeado's completed-event report states that the proposal was presented Tuesday September 15.

review.note: Completed September 15 submission is documented, not merely a preview. The original September 7 cabinet meeting does not by itself establish a personal promise that day; statutory obligation and media expectation must be distinguished from announcement.

original.role: Ministers of health of African Union member states
original.promise: Establish at least one emergency medical team in every African country by 2030
original.description: African health ministers adopted a regional framework committing every country on the continent to have at least one trained and deployable emergency medical team by 2030, to speed up responses to outbreaks, disasters and humanitarian crises.
evidence: Framework adopted at a WHO African Region meeting of health ministers, September 2026

retained.promise: Establish at least one functional national emergency medical team in each WHO African Region member state by 2030
retained.description: The regional committee adopted an emergency-medical-team framework during its August 2026 session. The framework targets nationally owned, deployable teams by 2030.
evidence: WHO reports adoption and progress in individual countries, not universal completion; exact adoption day remains unresolved.

review.note: The commitment covers WHO African Region member states, not every AU country. The September 7 story reports August adoption; the provisional agenda places discussion August 27 but is not proof of the final vote date. September 9 is unsupported and cannot simply be replaced with a publication date.
